      "content": "1|# **CURSE OF SLAAD
2|
3|# BEING A SUPPOSEDLY COMPETENT GROUP OF
4|
5|warriors and explorers, the party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard  
6|named Zardan to help him investigate what he fears to be a hostile  
7|incursion by monsters from Limbo into the Material Plane. His brother,  
8|Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts located  
9|on the fringes of this reality, which is garrisoned to monitor and repel  
10|threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable  
11|lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might  
12|have happened. 
13|
14|Beings of Order. Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind  
15|flayers millenia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and  
16|all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose  
17|a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily  
18|built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities  
19|and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment,  
20|from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and  
21|hunt down alien monsters. 
22|
23|ZARDAN, THE GITHZERAI Wizard 
24|
25|Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can  
26|roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat. 
27|
28|Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't  
29|withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the  
30|Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning  
31|abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard. 
32|
33|Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the  
34|adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be  
35|used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a  
36|creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is  
37|made. 
38|
39|You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic  
40|survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and  
41|chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and  
42|leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in  
43|the 
44|
45|center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you. 
46|
47|Githzerai Corpse. If players choose to approach or investigate the  
48|figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep  
49|slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly  
50|should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in  
51|front of it. A DC12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals  
52|that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was  
53|violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan  
54|recognizes this corpse as his brother and given the evidence, he  
55|believes that a red slaad killed him. 
56|
57|SLAADI, THE Terrors from LIMBO 
58|
59|If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the  
60|following. 
61|
62|Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from  
63|the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow  
64|their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The  
65|Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile  
66|abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses. 
67|
68|The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a  
69|red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue  
70|slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called  
71|"chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad. 
72|
73|Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274. 
74|
75|# CHAPTER 1: COMPROMISED CITADEL
76|
77|As the party stands before the small citadel's door, Zardan warns that  
78|they may encounter unimaginable monstrosities and incomprehensible  
79|dangers, and that his brother may be dead, or, even worse, no longer  
80|himself. He takes a breath and opens the door. 
81|
82|# A BROTHER'S FATE
83|
84|You may read from the following text box to describe the Githzerai  
85|citadel's first floor to the party: 
86|
87|# SLAAD ENCOUNTER
88|
89|A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to  
90|the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with  
91|chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing  
92|supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of  
93|value). 
94|
95|The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center  
96|of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive  
97|characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted  
98|expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in  
99|excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their  
100|stomachs are obscenely swollen. 
101|
102|2 
103|
104|3 
105|
106|If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks  
107|feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their  
108|agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison.  
109|Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM276) wriggle onto the floor and attack  
110|the party. 
111|
112|The party should easily finish this combat in 2 rounds; it is meant to  
113|provide them a false sense of confidence before encountering a real  
114|slaad threat. Zardan laments that all the Githzerai were infected, but  
115|is troubled that they haven't actually found the red slaad itself. As a  
116|side note, he wonders aloud what might have happened to the tadpole that  
117|spawned from his brother... 
118|
119|# A BLUE SLAAD ENRAGED
120|
121|As the wizard finishes his thought, a blue slaad (MM276) crashes down  
122|from a shadowy alcove of the high ceiling and cries out in rage at the  
123|sight of its slaughtered baby brothers. Its monstrous croaking is  
124|psychically translated in the party's brains as a vengeful vow that  
125|announces their doom. 
126|
127|Blue Slaad Combat. The blue slaad fights to the death and specifically  
128|targets the characters that killed a tadpole with its claws. Through  
129|violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns  
130|that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the  
131|intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when  
132|they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group,  
133|you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that  
134|the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos. 
135|
136|Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving  
137|throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage. 
138|
139|# GRAVE AFTERMATH
140|
141|After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone  
142|slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the  
143|chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the  
144|wish spell, there is no way to stop this disease. 
145|
146|But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in  
147|Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes'  
148|aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this  
149|curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that  
150|once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to  
151|his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his  
152|insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall  
153|bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be  
154|dire. 
155|
156|Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass. 
157|
158|The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items | made up  
159|for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics  
160|other than the functional properties described above. 
161|
162|# CHAPTER 2: LIMBO MONASTERY
163|
164|You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel  
165|when they first arrive in the plane of chaos: 
166|
167|You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable  
168|flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound 
169|
170|by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of  
171|gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply  
172|thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy  
173|and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree  
174|on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone 
175|
176|watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of 
177|
178|chaos. 
179|
180|# THE EVER-CHANGING CHAOS OF LIMBO
181|
182|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability  
183|threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come  
184|into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a  
185|DC14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random  
186|indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table  
187|(DMG260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be  
188|dispelled with the calm emotions, lesser restoration, or remove curse  
189|spells, and it ends if the character takes a short 
190|
191|rest. 
192|
193|The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil  
194|is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over  
195|it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary  
196|features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share  
197|with your players. 
198|
199|The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on  
200|Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG62), while the Chaos Control  
201|features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind  
202|(DMG61-62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's  
203|roleplay or gameplay load. 
204|
205|# CHAOS CONTROL
206|
207|Creatures in Limbo gain the following action options. 
208|
209|Telekinesis. You can spend an action to mentally move an object you can  
210|see that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful  
211|roll, you move the object 5 feet plus 1 foot for every point by which  
212|you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table  
213|below. 
214|
215|Transmutation. You can spend an action to alter a nonmagical object you  
216|can see that isn't being worn or carried and that is within 30 feet of  
217|you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you change the object  
218|into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder  
219|into a ball of fire). The number to beat is indicated in the DC by  
220|Object Size table below. 
221|
222|Permanence. You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area  
223|centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot  
224|radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the  
225|radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for  
226|24 hours, or until you use this ability again. 
227|

264|# ENCOUNTER ON THE MONASTIC ISLAND
265|
266|The first thing the party notices after acclimating to the chaos is the  
267|Githzerai monastery before them, a spire- like stone structure connected  
268|at both ends to grassy islands. It is shaped like the column formed when  
269|a stalagmite and a stalactite meet, and it is held together thanks to  
270|Zardan's sister's sheer willpower. On the steps leading to one of its  
271|entrances, a Githzerai monk (MM161), Lez'lin, is defending herself  
272|against 2d4 chaos flumphs. 
273|
274|Lez'lin's mind keeps the area around her monastery relatively stable,  
275|but some of Limbo's chaos permeates this oasis anyways. If you want to  
276|inject some of this plane's chaotic matter shifts into this encounter,  
277|use the tables in Appendix B to randomize the battlefield. 
278|
279|"Chaos flumphs" are a homebrew monster I created to serve as Limbo's  
280|low-level life forms of chaos. They essentially have the same stat block  
281|as normal flumphs (MM135), but the Stench Spray action is replaced by  
282|the Chaotic Release action. 
283|

324|
325|Tendrils. Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit:  
326|4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) acid damage. At the end of each  
327|of its turns, the target must make a DC10 Constitution saving throw,  
328|taking 2 (1d4) acid damage on a failure or ending the recurring acid  
329|damage on a success. A lesser restoration spell cast on the target also  
330|ends the recurring acid damage. 
331|
332|Chaotic Release (Recharge 6). The chaos flumph unleashes a spout of  
333|noxious Limbo energy in a direction of its choice. Each creature in a  
334|15-foot cone originating from the chaos flumph must succeed on a DC10  
335|Dexterity saving throw or suffer a random effect until the end of their  
336|next turn: 
337|
338|1. Blinded. The target can't see and automatically fails ability checks  
339|    that require sight. Attack rolls against them have advantage, and  
340|    their own attack rolls have disadvantage. 
341|    
342|2. Charmed. The target can't attack the chaos flumph or target

356|obscured. Their location can be detected if they make noise or leave

361|ability checks.

366|benefit from any bonus to their speed. Attack rolls against them have  
367|advantage, and their own attack rolls have disadvantage. They have  
368|disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.

370|# THE PACIFIST'S HOSPITALITY
371|
372|If the party helps her eliminate the pesky chaos flumphs, Lez'lin  
373|expresses her gratitude. She is inclined to aid the disoriented  
374|newcomers, especially upon learning that her brother Zardan sent them.  
375|She seems unsurprised to learn that some party members are infected with  
376|chaos phage, pointing out that the slaad infection has visibly advanced  
377|to a critical stage. 
378|
379|4

385|Indeed, the adventurers realize that the sudden exposure to Limbo's  
386|chaos aggravated the chaos phage. Their physical appearances become more  
387|toad-like, as determined randomly by the Chaos Phage Visible Symptoms  
388|table, and their hit point maximums are reduced by 3d6. They also become  
389|proficient with their Chaos Control features, meaning they can add their  
390|proficiency bonus to Wisdom checks made for the Telekinesis,  
391|Transmutation, and Permanence actions.

425|Lez'LIN, THE GITHZERAI MONK 
426|
427|Unlike her brother Zardan, Lez'lin possesses incredible mental fortitude  
428|and thrived in the chaotic boil of Limbo. She adheres to the monastic  
429|principles of her people, but her pacifist worldviews led her to isolate  
430|herself from Githzerai communities. She is loath to cause harm to any  
431|creature, no matter how vile or pesky, unless in self-defense. She lives  
432|alone in her small monastery and strives to maintain its structural  
433|integrity, so it may stand as a bastion of nonviolence. 
434|
435|She recalls her brothers fondly, but hasn't seen them for many years  
436|ever since they relocated to the Material Plane. News of Drarth's death  
437|saddens her deeply, but she doesn't let her emotions cloud her focus on  
438|the present. 
439|
440|Lez'lin invites the party inside her foyer, where floating chairs  
441|provide enough comfort for a short rest while the Githzerai assesses  
442|their predicament. Other than the wish spell, she knows of only one way  
443|to cure chaos phage: a death slaad's magic. 
444|
445|# DEATH SLAADI AND YOU
446|
447|Death slaadi are the peak of slaad evolution: stronger, viler, and more  
448|brutal, these monsters are corrupted by the Negative Energy Plane and  
449|take sadistic pleasure in killing and propagating slaadi dominance  
450|across dimensions. The only way to compel a death slaad to remove chaos  
451|phage is by acquiring its control gem, a magical fragment inside most  
452|slaadi's brains that allows whoever possesses it to subjugate the slaad.  
453|Removing the control gem is a near-impossible, very dangerous feat that  
454|can be approached in two ways: 
455|
456|1. The first method is a lengthy surgical procedure that can only be  
457|    attempted if the slaad is incapacitated. A creature must spend 1  
458|    uninterrupted minute and succeed on a DC20 Medicine check to extract  
459|    the gem. Every failed attempt deals 4d10 psychic damage to the  
460|    slaad. 
461|    
462|2. A control gem can also be obtained through magical 
463|    
464|
465|means, such as the 9th-level spell imprisonment (PHB252-253). However,  
466|this spell takes 1 minute to cast and requires the caster to see the  
467|target and stay within 30 feet of it, and the spell is not guaranteed to  
468|succeed. 
469|
470|In short, no matter the method they attempt, the party will undoubtedly  
471|need to incapacitate or restrain a live death slaad for 1 minute in  
472|order to acquire its control gem. Being a pacifist, Lez'lin won't  
473|directly help the party harm a living being, but she is willing to part  
474|with two legendary items that can help them, as long as they are able to  
475|secure the items themselves. 
476|
477|After they have rested, Lez'lin leads the party into the other half of  
478|her monastery, in which some of Limbo's chaos roils. 
479|
480|# SPELL SCROLL OF IMPRISONMENT
481|
482|The first legendary item provides a way to extract a slaad's control  
483|gem. It is protected by 3 layers, which must be removed sequentially to  
484|access it: 
485|
486|First, a Large ball of fire, which can be targeted with Transmutation or  
487|extinguished with 10 gallons of water (or any spell that could sensibly  
488|put out a large fire). 
489|
490|Second, a Medium hollow diamond, which can be transformed with  
491|Transmutation or cracked open with the shatter spell (PHB275). 
492|
493|Lastly, a 2-foot diameter sphere of annihilation (DMG201) encases the  
494|spell scroll. A character can recognize this hole in the multiverse with  
495|a successful DC20 Arcana check (a result between 10 and 20 gives them  
496|the gist). The sphere and the spell scroll move independently of one  
497|another. A creature within 60 feet of the sphere can move it with a  
498|successful DC25 Arcana check. The distance moved is 5 × the creature's  
499|Intelligence modifier (minimum 5 feet). If a creature fails this check,  
500|the sphere moves 10 feet towards them. If the sphere enters a creature's  
501|space, that creature must make a DC13 Dexterity saving throw or touch  
502|it. A creature that voluntarily or involuntarily touches the sphere  
503|takes 4d10 force damage. The sphere can also be moved with a  
504|disadvantaged DC10 Telekinesis check. Moving the sphere of annihilation  
505|by at least 5 feet makes the spell scroll of imprisonment accessible.  
506|Using the Spell Scroll. A low-level warlock or wizard can attempt to  
507|cast imprisonment (PHB252-253) without the required components by  
508|reading the scroll. The user must first make a DC19 saving throw  
509|(Charisma for warlocks and Intelligence for wizards). On a failed save,  
510|the scroll disintegrates. On a successful save, the user can cast the  
511|spell. If the target 
512|
513|stays visible and within 30 feet of the caster for 1 
514|
515|minute, it must make a DC19 Wisdom saving throw. If a targeted slaad  
516|fails this save, its control gem appears in the caster's hand. Whether  
517|the target fails or succeeds on its save, the scroll disintegrates. If  
518|the casting time is interrupted, nothing happens (see DMG200 for more  
519|rules on spell scrolls). 
520|
521|# THE ZERTHIMON STEELBEAST
522|
523|The second legendary item gives the party a chance to go toe-to-toe with  
524|a death slaad and even incapacitate it for several minutes. To access  
525|this artifact, the party must first breach its casing of stone. 
526|
527|The Huge mass of stone can be affected by Transmutation. It cracks if it  
528|receives 15 bludgeoning damage in one hit (AC17), revealing a steel  
529|barrel. This is the Zerthimon Steelbeast, a legendary artifact of the  
530|Githzerai (in essence, it is a modified Apparatus of Kwalish (DMG151),  
531|but adapted to better navigate Limbo and suit the party's needs). It has  
532|sensors that can locate slaadi while exploring Limbo, and its claws can  
533|enter a sphere of annihilation without suffering any consequences,  
534|giving the party an additional way to obtain the spell scroll of  
535|imprisonment. 
536|
537|After acquiring these legendary magic items, the party has all they need  
538|to gain the upper hand on a death slaad and steal its control gem. They  
539|must act quickly, however, as the four hours allotted to them in Limbo  
540|by Zardan's planar hourglass are quickly elapsing... 
541|
542|Zerthimon STEELBEAST 
543|
544|Wondrous item, artifact (requires attunement) 
545|
546|This item first appears to be a Huge steel barrel weighing 500 pounds.  
547|The barrel's door can be forced. open with a successful DC20 Strength  
548|check, or a successful DC20 Dexterity check made with thieves' tools.  
549|The surest way to gain access to this sentient artifact, however, is by  
550|succeeding on a DC15 Persuasion check to instantly attune with it. If a  
551|creature that tries to attune with the Steelbeast is a Githzerai or  
552|lawful good, it gets advantage on this check. If its alignment is  
553|chaotic or evil, the check is made with disadvantage. If a creature  
554|forces its way into the Steelbeast without attuning to it first, it must  
555|spend a short rest inside it learning how to operate its features and  
556|acquainting itself with this wondrous item. 
557|
558|When the Steelbeast is activated, thrusters appear around its rear  
559|circumference, its front surface turns into reinforced glass, two  
560|periscopes extend from either side, a long stinger tail expands from its  
561|back, and two massive pincers unfold. Up to six Medium creatures can fit  
562|inside the Steelbeast, but only the creature attuned to it can direct  
563|its actions. 
564|
565|Sentience. The Zerthimon Steelbeast is a sentient lawful good artifact  
566|with hearing and blindvision out to a range of 60 feet. 
567|
568|The item can speak, read, and understand Common and Gith, and can  
569|communicate telepathically with the creature attuned to it if that  
570|creature is within 60 feet of it. It can also communicate in this way  
571|with all creatures inside it. While you are attuned to it, the  
572|Steelbeast also understands every language you know. 
573|
574|Personality. The Zerthimon Steelbeast speaks in a friendly tone and is  
575|inclined to trust the creature attuned to it. 
576|
577|Its purpose is to eliminate aberrations, such as illithids and slaadi.  
578|It is amiable and courteous with all other creatures (especially  
579|Githzerai), but harbors deep loathing for Limbo's aberrations. It feels  
580|great sorrow for creatures infected by chaos phage or slaad tadpoles and  
581|won't attack them until they become slaadi themselves, or the tadpoles  
582|hatch. 
583|
584|The Steelbeast obeys the creature attuned to it on all matters, but will  
585|attack any slaadi it encounters regardless of its master's orders. A  
586|DC15 Charisma check is the only way to regain control of the Steelbeast.  
587|See Appendix C for the Zerthimon Steelbeast's stat block. 
588|
589|# CHAPTER 3: SLAAD ASSAULT
590|
591|Use the following text box to set the tone for the final battle: 
592|
593|Safe in the belly of the steel apparatus, you have been roaming for what  
594|feels like too long in the chaotic void of Limbo, searching for a death  
595|slaad amidst the flux. Those of you afflicted by chaos phage can see  
596|your symptoms worsening; you feel in the pit of your stomach that very  
597|little time remains. The Zerthimon Steelbeast's sensors lead you further  
598|and further into the primordial soup until, finally, an earthy cliff  
599|fragment melts into bubbles, revealing a grey- skinned, necrotic toad.  
600|The Steelbeast's alarms blare and it rushes forward to meet this deadly  
601|foe, intent on subduing it. The battle of your lives begins now. 
602|
603|# DEATH SLAAD DEN
604|
605|You can use the tables in appendix B to generate a random battlefield of  
606|chaos for the showdown against the death slaad. Death slaadi are at home  
607|in the most chaotic environments of Limbo, so don't hold back on the  
608|initial generation and the terrain's subsequent randomization. 
609|
610|Treat the Zerthimon Steelbeast as untouchable by Limbo's chaotic shifts  
611|as with the Permanence feature of Chaos Control, in case matter randomly  
612|spawns in its area. New matter can instead appear around it. 
613|
614|6 
615|
616|7 
617|
618|# ATTACKING AS THE DEATH SLAAD
619|
620|The death slaad (MM278) relishes this challenge and attacks the  
621|Steelbeast mercilessly with its claws, bite, and 
622|
623|greatsword. It stays close to attack while still trying evade the  
624|Steelbeast's pincers. After a few rounds or after the party performs an  
625|action that would reveal their existence, the slaad shifts its murderous  
626|focus to the characters. 
627|
628|For example, it can telepathically threaten or taunt them, cast fear on  
629|the group, or cast cloudkill inside the Steelbeast. 
630|
631|The slaad fights to the death and prioritizes freeing itself if it is  
632|restrained, unless it sadistically perceives a way to cause pain and  
633|death while grappled. 
634|
635|# OBTAINING THE CONTROL GEM
636|
637|The Steelbeast can use its Shock Stinger or Sleep Gas actions on the  
638|death slaad to incapacitate it for a few minutes (grappling it with  
639|Pincer Grab beforehand can help). The party then has that amount of time  
640|to attempt to extract the slaad's control gem using the method of their  
641|choice. 
642|
643|If the party wants to use the spell scroll of imprisonment but there are  
644|no wizards nor warlocks among them, they can summon Zardan using the  
645|planar recall bead he gave them earlier. The wizard needs to spend one  
646|minute after materializing to acclimate to Limbo's wracking chaos before  
647|he can take actions. If Zardan succeeds on a DC19 Intelligence saving  
648|throw, he can proceed to cast the spell. Otherwise, the scroll  
649|disintegrates. 
650|
651|Keep in mind that Zardan can use the two rolls from his Portent class  
652|feature during this encounter, if he hasn't used them already. 
653|
654|If the death slaad stays within sight and within 30 feet of the scroll's  
655|user for the minute required to cast the spell, it must make a DC19  
656|Wisdom saving throw (with advantage, as per its Magic Resistance trait).  
657|If it succeeds on this saving throw, the spell scroll disintegrates. If  
658|it fails, the death slaad's eyes gloss over and its entire body relaxes.  
659|The scroll disintegrates and is replaced by a cloudy grey asymmetrical  
660|gemstone in the palm of the scroll user's hand. 
661|
662|# EPILOGUE
663|
664|If the party successfully defeats the death slaad and obtains its  
665|control gem, they can force it to magically reverse the chaos phage  
666|afflicting their members (no roll required). The previously ill  
667|characters regain their original hit point maximums, lose their  
668|proficiency with Chaos Control, and their physical and mental states  
669|revert to normal. The party can force the slaad to perform any other  
670|action they desire, so long as they remain in control of its control  
671|gem. 
672|
673|The Zerthimon Steelbeast brings them back to Lez'lin's monastery, where  
674|she reunites with Zardan if the party summoned him. They exchange words  
675|of mourning over their brother Drarth's passing, and thank the group for  
676|risking their lives for this mission. The Githzerai then make plans to  
677|inform their people of a Material Plane citadel's fall and the  
678|Steelbeast expresses its wish to continue eradicating aberrations with  
679|them, despite its attachment to the creature attuned to it. 
680|
681|Everyone bids each other farewell before the planar hourglass's four  
682|hours are up and the party is gently displaced back to the Material  
683|Plane.

# A BROTHER'S FATE

You may read from the following text box to describe the Githzerai  
citadel's first floor to the party: 

# SLAAD ENCOUNTER

A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to  
the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with  
chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing  
supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of  
value). 

The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center  
of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive  
characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted  
expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in  
excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their  
stomachs are obscenely swollen. 

2 

3 

If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks  
feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their  
agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison.  
Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM276) wriggle onto the floor and attack  
the party.

104|violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns  
105|that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the  
106|intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when  
107|they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group,  
108|you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that  
109|the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos. 
110|
111|Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving  
112|throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage. 
113|
114|# GRAVE AFTERMATH
115|
116|After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone  
117|slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the  
118|chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the  
119|wish spell, there is no way to stop this disease. 
120|
121|But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in  
122|Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes'  
123|aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this  
124|curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that  
125|once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to  
126|his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his  
127|insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall  
128|bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be  
129|dire. 
130|
131|Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass. 
132|
133|The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items | made up  
134|for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics  
135|other than the functional properties described above. 
136|
137|## Chapter 2: Limbo Monastery
138|
139|You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel  
140|when they first arrive in the plane of chaos: 
141|
142|You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable  
143|flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound 
144|
145|by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of  
146|gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply  
147|thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy  
148|and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree  
149|on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone 
150|
151|watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of 
152|
153|chaos. 
154|
155|# THE EVER-CHANGING CHAOS OF LIMBO
156|
157|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability  
158|threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come  
159|into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a  
160|DC14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random  
161|indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table  
162|(DMG260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be  
163|dispelled with the calm emotions, lesser restoration, or remove curse  
164|spells, and it ends if the character takes a short 
165|
166|rest. 
167|
168|The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil  
169|is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over  
170|it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary  
171|features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share  
172|with your players. 
173|
174|The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on  
175|Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG62), while the Chaos Control  
176|features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind  
177|(DMG61-62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's  
178|roleplay or gameplay load. 
179|
180|# CHAOS CONTROL
181|
182|Creatures in Limbo gain the following action options. 
183|
184|Telekinesis. You can spend an action to mentally move an object you can  
185|see that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful  
186|roll, you move the object 5 feet plus 1 foot for every point by which  
187|you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table  
188|below. 
189|
190|Transmutation. You can spend an action to alter a nonmagical object you  
191|can see that isn't being worn or carried and that is within 30 feet of  
192|you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you change the object  
193|into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder  
194|into a ball of fire). The number to beat is indicated in the DC by  
195|Object Size table below. 
196|
197|Permanence. You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area  
198|centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot  
199|radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the  
200|radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for  
201|24 hours, or until you use this ability again.

239|# ENCOUNTER ON THE MONASTIC ISLAND
240|
241|The first thing the party notices after acclimating to the chaos is the  
242|Githzerai monastery before them, a spire- like stone structure connected  
243|at both ends to grassy islands. It is shaped like the column formed when  
244|a stalagmite and a stalactite meet, and it is held together thanks to  
245|Zardan's sister's sheer willpower. On the steps leading to one of its  
246|entrances, a Githzerai monk (MM161), Lez'lin, is defending herself  
247|against 2d4 chaos flumphs. 
248|
249|Lez'lin's mind keeps the area around her monastery relatively stable,  
250|but some of Limbo's chaos permeates this oasis anyways. If you want to  
251|inject some of this plane's chaotic matter shifts into this encounter,  
252|use the tables in Appendix B to randomize the battlefield. 
253|
254|"Chaos flumphs" are a homebrew monster I created to serve as Limbo's  
255|low-level life forms of chaos. They essentially have the same stat block  
256|as normal flumphs (MM135), but the Stench Spray action is replaced by  
257|the Chaotic Release action.

345|# THE PACIFIST'S HOSPITALITY
346|
347|If the party helps her eliminate the pesky chaos flumphs, Lez'lin  
348|expresses her gratitude. She is inclined to aid the disoriented  
349|newcomers, especially upon learning that her brother Zardan sent them.  
350|She seems unsurprised to learn that some party members are infected with  
351|chaos phage, pointing out that the slaad infection has visibly advanced  
352|to a critical stage.

361|chaos aggravated the chaos phage. Their physical appearances become more  
362|toad-like, as determined randomly by the Chaos Phage Visible Symptoms  
363|table, and their hit point maximums are reduced by 3d6. They also become  
364|proficient with their Chaos Control features, meaning they can add their  
365|proficiency bonus to Wisdom checks made for the Telekinesis,  
366|Transmutation, and Permanence actions.

400|Lez'LIN, THE GITHZERAI MONK 
401|
402|Unlike her brother Zardan, Lez'lin possesses incredible mental fortitude  
403|and thrived in the chaotic boil of Limbo. She adheres to the monastic  
404|principles of her people, but her pacifist worldviews led her to isolate  
405|herself from Githzerai communities. She is loath to cause harm to any  
406|creature, no matter how vile or pesky, unless in self-defense. She lives  
407|alone in her small monastery and strives to maintain its structural  
408|integrity, so it may stand as a bastion of nonviolence. 
409|
410|She recalls her brothers fondly, but hasn't seen them for many years  
411|ever since they relocated to the Material Plane. News of Drarth's death  
412|saddens her deeply, but she doesn't let her emotions cloud her focus on  
413|the present. 
414|
415|Lez'lin invites the party inside her foyer, where floating chairs  
416|provide enough comfort for a short rest while the Githzerai assesses  
417|their predicament. Other than the wish spell, she knows of only one way  
418|to cure chaos phage: a death slaad's magic. 
419|
420|# DEATH SLAADI AND YOU
421|
422|Death slaadi are the peak of slaad evolution: stronger, viler, and more  
423|brutal, these monsters are corrupted by the Negative Energy Plane and  
424|take sadistic pleasure in killing and propagating slaadi dominance  
425|across dimensions. The only way to compel a death slaad to remove chaos  
426|phage is by acquiring its control gem, a magical fragment inside most  
427|slaadi's brains that allows whoever possesses it to subjugate the slaad.  
428|Removing the control gem is a near-impossible, very dangerous feat that  
429|can be approached in two ways: 
430|
431|1. The first method is a lengthy surgical procedure that can only be  
432|    attempted if the slaad is incapacitated. A creature must spend 1  
433|    uninterrupted minute and succeed on a DC20 Medicine check to extract  
434|    the gem. Every failed attempt deals 4d10 psychic damage to the  
435|    slaad. 
436|    
437|2. A control gem can also be obtained through magical 
438|    
439|
440|means, such as the 9th-level spell imprisonment (PHB252-253). However,  
441|this spell takes 1 minute to cast and requires the caster to see the  
442|target and stay within 30 feet of it, and the spell is not guaranteed to  
443|succeed. 
444|
445|In short, no matter the method they attempt, the party will undoubtedly  
446|need to incapacitate or restrain a live death slaad for 1 minute in  
447|order to acquire its control gem. Being a pacifist, Lez'lin won't  
448|directly help the party harm a living being, but she is willing to part  
449|with two legendary items that can help them, as long as they are able to  
450|secure the items themselves. "

      "content": "1|# Curse of Slaad
2|
3|## Being a Supposedly Competent Group of Warriors and Explorers
4|
5|The party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan to help him investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into the Material Plane. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts located on the fringes of this reality, which is garrisoned to monitor and repel threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened.
6|
7|Beings of Order. Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind  
8|flayers millenia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and  
9|all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose  
10|a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily  
11|built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities  
12|and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment,  
13|from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and  
14|hunt down alien monsters. 
15|
16|### Zardan, the Githzerai Wizard
17|
18|Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can  
19|roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat. 
20|
21|Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't  
22|withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the  
23|Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning  
24|abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard. 
25|
26|Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the  
27|adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be  
28|used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a  
29|creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is  
30|made. 
31|
32|You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic  
33|survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and  
34|chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and  
35|leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in  
36|the 
37|
38|center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you. 
39|
40|Githzerai Corpse. If players choose to approach or investigate the  
41|figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep  
42|slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly  
43|should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in  
44|front of it. A DC12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals  
45|that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was  
46|violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan  
47|recognizes this corpse as his brother and given the evidence, he  
48|believes that a red slaad killed him. 
49|
50|### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo
51|
52|If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the  
53|following. 
54|
55|Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from  
56|the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow  
57|their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The  
58|Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile  
59|abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses. 
60|
61|The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a  
62|red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue  
63|slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called  
64|"chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad. 
65|
66|Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274. 
67|
68|## Chapter 1: Compromised Citadel
69|
70|As the party stands before the small citadel's door, Zardan warns that  
71|they may encounter unimaginable monstrosities and incomprehensible  
72|dangers, and that his brother may be dead, or, even worse, no longer  
73|himself. He takes a breath and opens the door. 
74|
75|## A Brother's Fate
76|
77|You may read from the following text box to describe the Githzerai citadel's first floor to the party:
78|
79|## Slaad Encounter
80|
81|A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of value).
82|
83|The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their stomachs are obscenely swollen.
84|
85|If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison. Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM276) wriggle onto the floor and attack the party.
86|
87|The party should easily finish this combat in 2 rounds; it is meant to  
88|provide them a false sense of confidence before encountering a real  
89|slaad threat. Zardan laments that all the Githzerai were infected, but  
90|is troubled that they haven't actually found the red slaad itself. As a  
91|side note, he wonders aloud what might have happened to the tadpole that  
92|spawned from his brother... 
93|
94|# A BLUE SLAAD ENRAGED
95|
96|As the wizard finishes his thought, a blue slaad (MM276) crashes down  
97|from a shadowy alcove of the high ceiling and cries out in rage at the  
98|sight of its slaughtered baby brothers. Its monstrous croaking is  
99|psychically translated in the party's brains as a vengeful vow that  
100|announces their doom. 
101|
102|Blue Slaad Combat. The blue slaad fights to the death and specifically  
103|targets the characters that killed a tadpole with its claws. Through  
104|violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns  
105|that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the  
106|intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when  
107|they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group,  
108|you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that  
109|the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos. 
110|
111|Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving  
112|throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage. 
113|
114|# GRAVE AFTERMATH
115|
116|After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone  
117|slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the  
118|chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the  
119|wish spell, there is no way to stop this disease. 
120|
121|But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in  
122|Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes'  
123|aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this  
124|curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that  
125|once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to  
126|his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his  
127|insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall  
128|bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be  
129|dire. 
130|
131|Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass. 
132|
133|The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items | made up  
134|for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics  
135|other than the functional properties described above. 
136|
137|## Chapter 2: Limbo Monastery
138|
139|You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel  
140|when they first arrive in the plane of chaos: 
141|
142|You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable  
143|flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound 
144|
145|by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of  
146|gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply  
147|thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy  
148|and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree  
149|on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone 
150|
151|watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of 
152|
153|chaos. 
154|
155|# THE EVER-CHANGING CHAOS OF LIMBO
156|
157|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability  
158|threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come  
159|into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a  
160|DC14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random  
161|indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table  
162|(DMG260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be  
163|dispelled with the calm emotions, lesser restoration, or remove curse  
164|spells, and it ends if the character takes a short 
165|
166|rest. 
167|
168|The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil  
169|is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over  
170|it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary  
171|features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share  
172|with your players. 
173|
174|The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on  
175|Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG62), while the Chaos Control  
176|features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind  
177|(DMG61-62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's  
178|roleplay or gameplay load. 
179|
180|# CHAOS CONTROL
181|
182|Creatures in Limbo gain the following action options. 
183|
184|Telekinesis. You can spend an action to mentally move an object you can  
185|see that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful  
186|roll, you move the object 5 feet plus 1 foot for every point by which  
187|you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table  
188|below. 
189|
190|Transmutation. You can spend an action to alter a nonmagical object you  
191|can see that isn't being worn or carried and that is within 30 feet of  
192|you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you change the object  
193|into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder  
194|into a ball of fire). The number to beat is indicated in the DC by  
195|Object Size table below. 
196|
197|Permanence. You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area  
198|centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot  
199|radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the  
200|radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for  
201|24 hours, or until you use this ability again. 
202|
203|# DC BY OBJECT SIZE
204|
205|Telekinesis DC Transmutation DC 
206|

208|
209|Tiny 
210|
211|5 
212|
213|10 
214|
215|Small

217|10

219|15 
220|

222|
223|15 
224|
225|20 
226|
227|Large 
228|
229|20 
230|
231|25 
232|
233|Huge or larger 
234|
235|25 
236|
237|25 
238|
239|# ENCOUNTER ON THE MONASTIC ISLAND
240|
241|The first thing the party notices after acclimating to the chaos is the  
242|Githzerai monastery before them, a spire- like stone structure connected  
243|at both ends to grassy islands. It is shaped like the column formed when  
244|a stalagmite and a stalactite meet, and it is held together thanks to  
245|Zardan's sister's sheer willpower. On the steps leading to one of its  
246|entrances, a Githzerai monk (MM161), Lez'lin, is defending herself  
247|against 2d4 chaos flumphs. 
248|
249|Lez'lin's mind keeps the area around her monastery relatively stable,  
250|but some of Limbo's chaos permeates this oasis anyways. If you want to  
251|inject some of this plane's chaotic matter shifts into this encounter,  
252|use the tables in Appendix B to randomize the battlefield. 
253|
254|"Chaos flumphs" are a homebrew monster I created to serve as Limbo's  
255|low-level life forms of chaos. They essentially have the same stat block  
256|as normal flumphs (MM135), but the Stench Spray action is replaced by  
257|the Chaotic Release action. 
258|
259|# CHAOS FLUMPH
260|
261|Small aberration, chaotic evil

345|# THE PACIFIST'S HOSPITALITY
346|
347|If the party helps her eliminate the pesky chaos flumphs, Lez'lin  
348|expresses her gratitude. She is inclined to aid the disoriented  
349|newcomers, especially upon learning that her brother Zardan sent them.

360|Indeed, the adventurers realize that the sudden exposure to Limbo's

362|toad-like, as determined randomly by the Chaos Phage Visible Symptoms  
363|table, and their hit point maximums are reduced by 3d6. They also become  
364|proficient with their Chaos Control features, meaning they can add their  
365|proficiency bonus to Wisdom checks made for the Telekinesis,  
366|Transmutation, and Permanence actions.

400|Lez'LIN, THE GITHZERAI MONK 
401|
402|Unlike her brother Zardan, Lez'lin possesses incredible mental fortitude  
403|and thrived in the chaotic boil of Limbo. She adheres to the monastic  
404|principles of her people, but her pacifist worldviews led her to isolate  
405|herself from Githzerai communities. She is loath to cause harm to any  
406|creature, no matter how vile or pesky, unless in self-defense. She lives  
407|alone in her small monastery and strives to maintain its structural  
408|integrity, so it may stand as a bastion of nonviolence. 
409|
410|She recalls her brothers fondly, but hasn't seen them for many years  
411|ever since they relocated to the Material Plane. News of Drarth's death  
412|saddens her deeply, but she doesn't let her emotions cloud her focus on  
413|the present. 
414|
415|Lez'lin invites the party inside her foyer, where floating chairs  
416|provide enough comfort for a short rest while the Githzerai assesses  
417|their predicament. Other than the wish spell, she knows of only one way  
418|to cure chaos phage: a death slaad's magic. 
419|
420|# DEATH SLAADI AND YOU
421|
422|Death slaadi are the peak of slaad evolution: stronger, viler, and more  
423|brutal, these monsters are corrupted by the Negative Energy Plane and  
424|take sadistic pleasure in killing and propagating slaadi dominance  
425|across dimensions. The only way to compel a death slaad to remove chaos  
426|phage is by acquiring its control gem, a magical fragment inside most  
427|slaadi's brains that allows whoever possesses it to subjugate the slaad.  
428|Removing the control gem is a near-impossible, very dangerous feat that

444|
445|In short, no matter the method they attempt, the party will undoubtedly

455|# SPELL SCROLL OF IMPRISONMENT
456|
457|The first legendary item provides a way to extract a slaad's control  
458|gem. It is protected by 3 layers, which must be removed sequentially to  
459|access it: 
460|
461|First, a Large ball of fire, which can be targeted with Transmutation or  
462|extinguished with 10 gallons of water (or any spell that could sensibly  
463|put out a large fire).

465|Second, a Medium hollow diamond, which can be transformed with  
466|Transmutation or cracked open with the shatter spell (PHB275). 
467|
468|Lastly, a 2-foot diameter sphere of annihilation (DMG201) encases the  
469|spell scroll. A character can recognize this hole in the multiverse with  
470|a successful DC20 Arcana check (a result between 10 and 20 gives them  
471|the gist). The sphere and the spell scroll move independently of one  
472|another. A creature within 60 feet of the sphere can move it with a  
473|successful DC25 Arcana check. The distance moved is 5 × the creature's  
474|Intelligence modifier (minimum 5 feet). If a creature fails this check,  
475|the sphere moves 10 feet towards them. If the sphere enters a creature's  
476|space, that creature must make a DC13 Dexterity saving throw or touch  
477|it. A creature that voluntarily or involuntarily touches the sphere  
478|takes 4d10 force damage. The sphere can also be moved with a  
479|disadvantaged DC10 Telekinesis check. Moving the sphere of annihilation  
480|by at least 5 feet makes the spell scroll of imprisonment accessible.  
481|Using the Spell Scroll. A low-level warlock or wizard can attempt to  
482|cast imprisonment (PHB252-253) without the required components by  
483|reading the scroll. The user must first make a DC19 saving throw  
484|(Charisma for warlocks and Intelligence for wizards). On a failed save,  
485|the scroll disintegrates. On a successful save, the user can cast the  
486|spell. If the target 
487|
488|stays visible and within 30 feet of the caster for 1 
489|
490|minute, it must make a DC19 Wisdom saving throw. If a targeted slaad  
491|fails this save, its control gem appears in the caster's hand. Whether  
492|the target fails or succeeds on its save, the scroll disintegrates. If  
493|the casting time is interrupted, nothing happens (see DMG200 for more  
494|rules on spell scrolls). 
495|
496|# THE ZERTHIMON STEELBEAST
497|
498|The second legendary item gives the party a chance to go toe-to-toe with  
499|a death slaad and even incapacitate it for several minutes. To access  
500|this artifact, the party must first breach its casing of stone. 
501|
502|The Huge mass of stone can be affected by Transmutation. It cracks if it  
503|receives 15 bludgeoning damage in one hit (AC17), revealing a steel  
504|barrel. This is the Zerthimon Steelbeast, a legendary artifact of the  
505|Githzerai (in essence, it is a modified Apparatus of Kwalish (DMG151),  
506|but adapted to better navigate Limbo and suit the party's needs). It has  
507|sensors that can locate slaadi while exploring Limbo, and its claws can  
508|enter a sphere of annihilation without suffering any consequences,  
509|giving the party an additional way to obtain the spell scroll of  
510|imprisonment. 
511|
512|After acquiring these legendary magic items, the party has all they need  
513|to gain the upper hand on a death slaad and steal its control gem. They  
514|must act quickly, however, as the four hours allotted to them in Limbo  
515|by Zardan's planar hourglass are quickly elapsing... 
516|
517|Zerthimon STEELBEAST 
518|
519|Wondrous item, artifact (requires attunement) 
520|
521|This item first appears to be a Huge steel barrel weighing 500 pounds.  
522|The barrel's door can be forced. open with a successful DC20 Strength  
523|check, or a successful DC20 Dexterity check made with thieves' tools.  
524|The surest way to gain access to this sentient artifact, however, is by  
525|succeeding on a DC15 Persuasion check to instantly attune with it. If a  
526|creature that tries to attune with the Steelbeast is a Githzerai or  
527|lawful good, it gets advantage on this check. If its alignment is  
528|chaotic or evil, the check is made with disadvantage. If a creature  
529|forces its way into the Steelbeast without attuning to it first, it must  
530|spend a short rest inside it learning how to operate its features and  
531|acquainting itself with this wondrous item. 
532|
533|When the Steelbeast is activated, thrusters appear around its rear  
534|circumference, its front surface turns into reinforced glass, two  
535|periscopes extend from either side, a long stinger tail expands from its  
536|back, and two massive pincers unfold. Up to six Medium creatures can fit  
537|inside the Steelbeast, but only the creature attuned to it can direct  
538|its actions. 
539|
540|Sentience. The Zerthimon Steelbeast is a sentient lawful good artifact  
541|with hearing and blindvision out to a range of 60 feet. 
542|
543|The item can speak, read, and understand Common and Gith, and can  
544|communicate telepathically with the creature attuned to it if that  
545|creature is within 60 feet of it. It can also communicate in this way  
546|with all creatures inside it. While you are attuned to it, the  
547|Steelbeast also understands every language you know. 
548|
549|Personality. The Zerthimon Steelbeast speaks in a friendly tone and is  
550|inclined to trust the creature attuned to it. 
551|
552|Its purpose is to eliminate aberrations, such as illithids and slaadi.  
553|It is amiable and courteous with all other creatures (especially  
554|Githzerai), but harbors deep loathing for Limbo's aberrations. It feels  
555|great sorrow for creatures infected by chaos phage or slaad tadpoles and  
556|won't attack them until they become slaadi themselves, or the tadpoles  
557|hatch. 
558|
559|The Steelbeast obeys the creature attuned to it on all matters, but will  
560|attack any slaadi it encounters regardless of its master's orders. A  
561|DC15 Charisma check is the only way to regain control of the Steelbeast.  
562|See Appendix C for the Zerthimon Steelbeast's stat block.

564|## Chapter 3: Slaad Assault
565|
566|Use the following text box to set the tone for the final battle: 
567|
568|Safe in the belly of the steel apparatus, you have been roaming for what  
569|feels like too long in the chaotic void of Limbo, searching for a death  
570|slaad amidst the flux. Those of you afflicted by chaos phage can see  
571|your symptoms worsening; you feel in the pit of your stomach that very  
572|little time remains. The Zerthimon Steelbeast's sensors lead you further  
573|and further into the primordial soup until, finally, an earthy cliff  
574|fragment melts into bubbles, revealing a grey- skinned, necrotic toad.  
575|The Steelbeast's alarms blare and it rushes forward to meet this deadly  
576|foe, intent on subduing it. The battle of your lives begins now. 
577|
578|# DEATH SLAAD DEN
579|
580|You can use the tables in appendix B to generate a random battlefield of  
581|chaos for the showdown against the death slaad. Death slaadi are at home  
582|in the most chaotic environments of Limbo, so don't hold back on the  
583|initial generation and the terrain's subsequent randomization. 
584|
585|Treat the Zerthimon Steelbeast as untouchable by Limbo's chaotic shifts  
586|as with the Permanence feature of Chaos Control, in case matter randomly  
587|spawns in its area. New matter can instead appear around it. 
588|
589|6 
590|
591|7 
592|
593|# ATTACKING AS THE DEATH SLAAD
594|
595|The death slaad (MM278) relishes this challenge and attacks the  
596|Steelbeast mercilessly with its claws, bite, and 
597|
598|greatsword. It stays close to attack while still trying evade the  
599|Steelbeast's pincers. After a few rounds or after the party performs an  
600|action that would reveal their existence, the slaad shifts its murderous  
601|focus to the characters. 
602|
603|For example, it can telepathically threaten or taunt them, cast fear on  
604|the group, or cast cloudkill inside the Steelbeast. 
605|
606|The slaad fights to the death and prioritizes freeing itself if it is  
607|restrained, unless it sadistically perceives a way to cause pain and  
608|death while grappled. 
609|
610|# OBTAINING THE CONTROL GEM
611|
612|The Steelbeast can use its Shock Stinger or Sleep Gas actions on the  
613|death slaad to incapacitate it for a few minutes (grappling it with  
614|Pincer Grab beforehand can help). The party then has that amount of time  
615|to attempt to extract the slaad's control gem using the method of their  
616|choice. 
617|
618|If the party wants to use the spell scroll of imprisonment but there are  
619|no wizards nor warlocks among them, they can summon Zardan using the  
620|planar recall bead he gave them earlier. The wizard needs to spend one  
621|minute after materializing to acclimate to Limbo's wracking chaos before  
622|he can take actions. If Zardan succeeds on a DC19 Intelligence saving  
623|throw, he can proceed to cast the spell. Otherwise, the scroll  
624|disintegrates. 
625|
626|Keep in mind that Zardan can use the two rolls from his Portent class  
627|feature during this encounter, if he hasn't used them already. 
628|
629|If the death slaad stays within sight and within 30 feet of the scroll's  
630|user for the minute required to cast the spell, it must make a DC19  
631|Wisdom saving throw (with advantage, as per its Magic Resistance trait).  
632|If it succeeds on this saving throw, the spell scroll disintegrates. If  
633|it fails, the death slaad's eyes gloss over and its entire body relaxes.  
634|The scroll disintegrates and is replaced by a cloudy grey asymmetrical  
635|gemstone in the palm of the scroll user's hand. 
636|
637|# EPILOGUE
638|
639|If the party successfully defeats the death slaad and obtains its  
640|control gem, they can force it to magically reverse the chaos phage  
641|afflicting their members (no roll required). The previously ill  
642|characters regain their original hit point maximums, lose their  
643|proficiency with Chaos Control, and their physical and mental states  
644|revert to normal. The party can force the slaad to perform any other  
645|action they desire, so long as they remain in control of its control  
646|gem. 
647|
648|The Zerthimon Steelbeast brings them back to Lez'lin's monastery, where  
649|she reunites with Zardan if the party summoned him. They exchange words  
650|of mourning over their brother Drarth's passing, and thank the group for  
651|risking their lives for this mission. The Githzerai then make plans to  
652|inform their people of a Material Plane citadel's fall and the  
653|Steelbeast expresses its wish to continue eradicating aberrations with  
654|them, despite its attachment to the creature attuned to it. 
655|
656|Everyone bids each other farewell before the planar hourglass's four  
657|hours are up and the party is gently displaced back to the Material  
658|Plane.

980|# HEN RUNNING A COMBAT ENCOUNTER IN THE
981|
982|unstable plane of Limbo, you may want to bring extra chaos to the  
983|battlefield. Use the tables and steps below to introduce random matter  
984|shifts to the combat environment. First of all, separate the combat map  
985|into an appropriate number of equal-sized sections. 
986|
987|1. Every time you introduce a new pocket of matter, 
988|    
989|
990|select a random section of the battlefield in which it will appear,  
991|either by rolling a die, generating a random number, or choosing  
992|yourself. 
993|
994|2. Roll on the Size of New Matter table. 
995|    
996|3. Roll on the Type of New Matter table. 
997|    
998|
999|If the selected section of the battlefield already contains matter, the  
1000|new matter you are rolling for replaces it. If the matter would spawn in  
1001|a creature's space, that creature is pushed into the nearest empty  
1002|space. As the DM, you decide how the new matter is formed: whether it  
1003|arrives from a specific direction, spawns from nothing, transmutes from  
1004|preexisting matter, etc. 
1005|
1006|Use the Floating Terrain table to populate the death slaad encounter  
1007|with some crazy environmental elements. All the list elements are Huge  
1008|in size, meaning they occupy a 15 foot by 15 foot space. Don't shy away  
1009|from rerolling some of the terrain after a few rounds.

1133|# CHAOS CONTROL
1134|
1135|Creatures in Limbo gain the following action options. 
1136|
1137|Telekinesis. You can spend an action to mentally move an object you can  
1138|see that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful  
1139|roll, you move the object 5 feet plus 1 foot for every point by which  
1140|you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table  
1141|below. 
1142|
1143|Transmutation. You can spend an action to alter a nonmagical object you  
1144|can see that isn't being worn or carried and that is within 30 feet of  
1145|you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you change the object  
1146|into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder  
1147|into a ball of fire). The number to beat is indicated in the DC by  
1148|Object Size table below. 
1149|
1150|Permanence. You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area  
1151|centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot  
1152|radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the  
1153|radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for

      "content": "1|# Curse of Slaad
2|
3|## Being a Supposedly Competent Group of Warriors and Explorers
4|
5|The party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan to help him investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into the Material Plane. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts located on the fringes of this reality, which is garrisoned to monitor and repel threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened.
6|
7|Beings of Order. Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind  
8|flayers millenia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and  
9|all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose  
10|a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily  
11|built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities  
12|and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment,  
13|from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and  
14|hunt down alien monsters. 
15|
16|### Zardan, the Githzerai Wizard
17|
18|Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can  
19|roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat. 
20|
21|Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't  
22|withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the  
23|Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning  
24|abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard. 
25|
26|Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the  
27|adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be  
28|used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a  
29|creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is  
30|made. 
31|
32|You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic  
33|survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and  
34|chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and  
35|leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in  
36|the 
37|
38|center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you. 
39|
40|Githzerai Corpse. If players choose to approach or investigate the  
41|figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep  
42|slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly  
43|should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in  
44|front of it. A DC12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals  
45|that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was  
46|violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan  
47|recognizes this corpse as his brother and given the evidence, he  
48|believes that a red slaad killed him. 
49|
50|### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo
51|
52|If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the  
53|following. 
54|
55|Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from  
56|the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow  
57|their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The  
58|Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile  
59|abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses. 
60|
61|The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a  
62|red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue  
63|slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called  
64|"chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad. 
65|
66|Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274. 
67|
68|## Chapter 1: Compromised Citadel
69|
70|As the party stands before the small citadel's door, Zardan warns that  
71|they may encounter unimaginable monstrosities and incomprehensible  
72|dangers, and that his brother may be dead, or, even worse, no longer

345|If the party helps her eliminate the pesky chaos flumphs, Lez'lin

390|Lez'LIN, THE GITHZERAI MONK 
391|
392|Unlike her brother Zardan, Lez'lin possesses incredible mental fortitude  
393|and thrived in the chaotic boil of Limbo. She adheres to the monastic  
394|principles of her people, but her pacifist worldviews led her to isolate  
395|herself from Githzerai communities. She is loath to cause harm to any  
396|creature, no matter how vile or pesky, unless in self-defense. She lives  
397|alone in her small monastery and strives to maintain its structural  
398|integrity, so it may stand as a bastion of nonviolence. 
399|
400|She recalls her brothers fondly, but hasn't seen them for many years  
401|ever since they relocated to the Material Plane. News of Drarth's death  
402|saddens her deeply, but she doesn't let her emotions cloud her focus on  
403|the present.

406|provide enough comfort for a short rest while the Githzerai assesses  
407|their predicament. Other than the wish spell, she knows of only one way  
408|to cure chaos phage: a death slaad's magic.

At the end of each of its turns, the target must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw, taking 2 (1d4) acid damage on a failure or ending the recurring acid damage on a success.       "content": "1|# Curse of Slaad
2|
3|## Being a Supposedly Competent Group of Warriors and Explorers
4|
5|The party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan to help him investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into the Material Plane. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts located on the fringes of this reality, which is garrisoned to monitor and repel threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened.
6|
7|Beings of Order. Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind  
8|flayers millenia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and  
9|all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose  
10|a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily  
11|built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities  
12|and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment,  
13|from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and  
14|hunt down alien monsters. 
15|
16|### Zardan, the Githzerai Wizard
17|
18|Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can  
19|roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat. 
20|
21|Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't  
22|withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the  
23|Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning  
24|abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard. 
25|
26|Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the  
27|adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be  
28|used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a  
29|creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is  
30|made. 
31|
32|You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic  
33|survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and  
34|chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and  
35|leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in  
36|the 
37|
38|center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you. 
39|
40|Githzerai Corpse. If players choose to approach or investigate the  
41|figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep  
42|slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly  
43|should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in  
44|front of it. A DC12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals  
45|that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was  
46|violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan  
47|recognizes this corpse as his brother and given the evidence, he  
48|believes that a red slaad killed him. 
49|
50|### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo
51|
52|If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the  
53|following. 
54|
55|Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from  
56|the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow  
57|their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The  
58|Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile  
59|abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses. 
60|
61|The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a  
62|red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue  
63|slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called  
64|"chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad. 
65|
66|Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274. 
67|
68|## Chapter 1: Compromised Citadel
69|
70|As the party stands before the small citadel's door, Zardan warns that  
71|they may encounter unimaginable monstrosities and incomprehensible  
72|dangers, and that his brother may be dead, or, even worse, no longer  
73|himself. He takes a breath and opens the door. 
74|
75|## A Brother's Fate
76|
77|You may read from the following text box to describe the Githzerai citadel's first floor to the party:
78|
79|## Slaad Encounter
80|"
