      "content": "1|# Curse of Slaad
2|
3|## Being a Supposedly Competent Group of Warriors and Explorers
4|
5|The party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan to help him investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into the Material Plane. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts located on the fringes of this reality, which is garrisoned to monitor and repel threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened.
6|
7|Beings of Order. Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind  
8|flayers millenia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and  
9|all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose  
10|a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily  
11|built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities  
12|and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment,  
13|from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and  
14|hunt down alien monsters. 
15|
16|### Zardan, the Githzerai Wizard
17|
18|Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can  
19|roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat. 
20|
21|Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't  
22|withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the  
23|Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning  
24|abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard. 
25|
26|Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the  
27|adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be  
28|used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a  
29|creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is  
30|made. 
31|
32|You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic  
33|survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and  
34|chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and  
35|leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in  
36|the 
37|
38|center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you. 
39|
40|Githzerai Corpse. If players choose to approach or investigate the  
41|figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep  
42|slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly  
43|should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in  
44|front of it. A DC12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals  
45|that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was  
46|violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan  
47|recognizes this corpse as his brother and given the evidence, he  
48|believes that a red slaad killed him. 
49|
50|### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo
51|
52|If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the  
53|following. 
54|
55|Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from  
56|the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow  
57|their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The  
58|Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile  
59|abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses. 
60|
61|The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a  
62|red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue  
63|slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called  
64|"chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad. 
65|
66|Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274. 
67|
68|## Chapter 1: Compromised Citadel
69|
70|As the party stands before the small citadel's door, Zardan warns that  
71|they may encounter unimaginable monstrosities and incomprehensible  
72|dangers, and that his brother may be dead, or, even worse, no longer  
73|himself. He takes a breath and opens the door. 
74|
75|## A Brother's Fate
76|
77|You may read from the following text box to describe the Githzerai citadel's first floor to the party:
78|
79|## Slaad Encounter
80|
81|A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of value).
82|
83|The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their stomachs are obscenely swollen.
84|
85|If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison. Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM276) wriggle onto the floor and attack the party.
86|
87|The party should easily finish this combat in 2 rounds; it is meant to  
88|provide them a false sense of confidence before encountering a real  
89|slaad threat. Zardan laments that all the Githzerai were infected, but  
90|is troubled that they haven't actually found the red slaad itself. As a  
91|side note, he wonders aloud what might have happened to the tadpole that  
92|spawned from his brother... 
93|
94|### A Blue Slaad Enraged
95|
96|As the wizard finishes his thought, a blue slaad (MM276) crashes down  
97|from a shadowy alcove of the high ceiling and cries out in rage at the  
98|sight of its slaughtered baby brothers. Its monstrous croaking is  
99|psychically translated in the party's brains as a vengeful vow that  
100|announces their doom. 
101|
102|Blue Slaad Combat. The blue slaad fights to the death and specifically  
103|targets the characters that killed a tadpole with its claws. Through  
104|violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns  
105|that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the  
106|intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when  
107|they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group,  
108|you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that  
109|the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos. 
110|
111|Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving  
112|throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage. 
113|
114|### Grave Aftermath
115|
116|After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone  
117|slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the  
118|chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the  
119|wish spell, there is no way to stop this disease. 
120|
121|But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in  
122|Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes'  
123|aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this  
124|curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that  
125|once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to  
126|his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his  
127|insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall  
128|bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be  
129|dire. 
130|
131|Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass. 
132|
133|The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items made up for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics other than the functional properties described above.
134|
135|## Chapter 2: Limbo Monastery
136|
137|You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel  
138|when they first arrive in the plane of chaos: 
139|
140|You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable  
141|flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound 
142|
143|by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of  
144|gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply  
145|thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy  
146|and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree  
147|on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone 
148|
149|watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of 
150|
151|chaos. 
152|
153|### The Ever-Changing Chaos of Limbo
154|
155|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability  
156|threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come  
157|into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a  
158|DC14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random  
159|indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table  
160|(DMG260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be  
161|dispelled with the calm emotions, lesser restoration, or remove curse  
162|spells, and it ends if the character takes a short 
163|
164|rest. 
165|
166|The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil  
167|is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over  
168|it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary  
169|features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share  
170|with your players. 
171|
172|The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on  
173|Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG62), while the Chaos Control  
174|features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind  
175|(DMG61-62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's  
176|roleplay or gameplay load.

178|### Chaos Control
179|
180|Creatures in Limbo gain the following action options. 
181|
182|Telekinesis. You can spend an action to mentally move an object you can  
183|see that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful  
184|roll, you move the object 5 feet plus 1 foot for every point by which  
185|you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table  
186|below. 
187|
188|Transmutation. You can spend an action to alter a nonmagical object you  
189|can see that isn't being worn or carried and that is within 30 feet of  
190|you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you change the object  
191|into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder  
192|into a ball of fire). The number to beat is indicated in the DC by  
193|Object Size table below. 
194|
195|Permanence. You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area  
196|centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot  
197|radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the  
198|radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for  
199|24 hours, or until you use this ability again.

211|### Encounter on the Monastic Island
212|
213|The first thing the party notices after acclimating to the chaos is the  
214|Githzerai monastery before them, a spire- like stone structure connected  
215|at both ends to grassy islands. It is shaped like the column formed when  
216|a stalagmite and a stalactite meet, and it is held together thanks to  
217|Zardan's sister's sheer willpower. On the steps leading to one of its  
218|entrances, a Githzerai monk (MM161), Lez'lin, is defending herself  
219|against 2d4 chaos flumphs. 
220|
221|Lez'lin's mind keeps the area around her monastery relatively stable,  
222|but some of Limbo's chaos permeates this oasis anyways. If you want to  
223|inject some of this plane's chaotic matter shifts into this encounter,  
224|use the tables in Appendix B to randomize the battlefield. 
225|

227|low-level life forms of chaos. They essentially have the same stat block  
228|as normal flumphs (MM135), but the Stench Spray action is replaced by  
229|the Chaotic Release action.

261|### The Pacifist's Hospitality
262|
263|If the party helps her eliminate the pesky chaos flumphs, Lez'lin  
264|expresses her gratitude. She is inclined to aid the disoriented  
265|newcomers, especially upon learning that her brother Zardan sent them.  
266|She seems unsurprised to learn that some party members are infected with  
267|chaos phage, pointing out that the slaad infection has visibly advanced  
268|to a critical stage. 
269|
270|
271|Indeed, the adventurers realize that the sudden exposure to Limbo's  
272|chaos aggravated the chaos phage. Their physical appearances become more  
273|toad-like, as determined randomly by the Chaos Phage Visible Symptoms  
274|table, and their hit point maximums are reduced by 3d6. They also become  
275|proficient with their Chaos Control features, meaning they can add their  
276|proficiency bonus to Wisdom checks made for the Telekinesis,  
277|Transmutation, and Permanence actions.

292|Lez'LIN, THE GITHZERAI MONK 
293|
294|Unlike her brother Zardan, Lez'lin possesses incredible mental fortitude  
295|and thrived in the chaotic boil of Limbo. She adheres to the monastic  
296|principles of her people, but her pacifist worldviews led her to isolate  
297|herself from Githzerai communities. She is loath to cause harm to any  
298|creature, no matter how vile or pesky, unless in self-defense. She lives  
299|alone in her small monastery and strives to maintain its structural  
300|integrity, so it may stand as a bastion of nonviolence. 
301|
302|She recalls her brothers fondly, but hasn't seen them for many years  
303|ever since they relocated to the Material Plane. News of Drarth's death  
304|saddens her deeply, but she doesn't let her emotions cloud her focus on  
305|the present. 
306|
307|Lez'lin invites the party inside her foyer, where floating chairs  
308|provide enough comfort for a short rest while the Githzerai assesses  
309|their predicament. Other than the wish spell, she knows of only one way  
310|to cure chaos phage: a death slaad's magic. 
311|
312|### Death Slaadi and You
313|
314|Death slaadi are the peak of slaad evolution: stronger, viler, and more  
315|brutal, these monsters are corrupted by the Negative Energy Plane and  
316|take sadistic pleasure in killing and propagating slaadi dominance  
317|across dimensions. The only way to compel a death slaad to remove chaos  
318|phage is by acquiring its control gem, a magical fragment inside most  
319|slaadi's brains that allows whoever possesses it to subjugate the slaad.  
320|Removing the control gem is a near-impossible, very dangerous feat that  
321|can be approached in two ways: 
322|
323|1. The first method is a lengthy surgical procedure that can only be  
324|    attempted if the slaad is incapacitated. A creature must spend 1  
325|    uninterrupted minute and succeed on a DC20 Medicine check to extract  
326|    the gem. Every failed attempt deals 4d10 psychic damage to the  
327|    slaad. 
328|    
329|2. A control gem can also be obtained through magical 
330|    
331|
332|means, such as the 9th-level spell imprisonment (PHB252-253). However,  
333|this spell takes 1 minute to cast and requires the caster to see the  
334|target and stay within 30 feet of it, and the spell is not guaranteed to  
335|succeed. 
336|
337|In short, no matter the method they attempt, the party will undoubtedly  
338|need to incapacitate or restrain a live death slaad for 1 minute in  
339|order to acquire its control gem. Being a pacifist, Lez'lin won't  
340|directly help the party harm a living being, but she is willing to part  
341|with two legendary items that can help them, as long as they are able to  
342|secure the items themselves. 
343|
344|After they have rested, Lez'lin leads the party into the other half of  
345|her monastery, in which some of Limbo's chaos roils. 
346|
347|### Spell Scroll of Imprisonment
348|
349|The first legendary item provides a way to extract a slaad's control  
350|gem. It is protected by 3 layers, which must be removed sequentially to  
351|access it: 
352|
353|First, a Large ball of fire, which can be targeted with Transmutation or  
354|extinguished with 10 gallons of water (or any spell that could sensibly  
355|put out a large fire). 
356|
357|Second, a Medium hollow diamond, which can be transformed with  
358|Transmutation or cracked open with the shatter spell (PHB275). 
359|
360|Lastly, a 2-foot diameter sphere of annihilation (DMG201) encases the  
361|spell scroll. A character can recognize this hole in the multiverse with  
362|a successful DC20 Arcana check (a result between 10 and 20 gives them  
363|the gist). The sphere and the spell scroll move independently of one  
364|another. A creature within 60 feet of the sphere can move it with a  
365|successful DC25 Arcana check. The distance moved is 5 × the creature's  
366|Intelligence modifier (minimum 5 feet). If a creature fails this check,  
367|the sphere moves 10 feet towards them. If the sphere enters a creature's  
368|space, that creature must make a DC13 Dexterity saving throw or touch  
369|it. A creature that voluntarily or involuntarily touches the sphere  
370|takes 4d10 force damage. The sphere can also be moved with a  
371|disadvantaged DC10 Telekinesis check. Moving the sphere of annihilation  
372|by at least 5 feet makes the spell scroll of imprisonment accessible.  
373|Using the Spell Scroll. A low-level warlock or wizard can attempt to  
374|cast imprisonment (PHB252-253) without the required components by  
375|reading the scroll. The user must first make a DC19 saving throw  
376|(Charisma for warlocks and Intelligence for wizards). On a failed save,  
377|the scroll disintegrates. On a successful save, the user can cast the  
378|spell. If the target 
379|
380|stays visible and within 30 feet of the caster for 1 
381|
382|minute, it must make a DC19 Wisdom saving throw. If a targeted slaad  
383|fails this save, its control gem appears in the caster's hand. Whether  
384|the target fails or succeeds on its save, the scroll disintegrates. If  
385|the casting time is interrupted, nothing happens (see DMG200 for more  
386|rules on spell scrolls). 
387|
388|### The Zerthimon Steelbeast
389|
390|The second legendary item gives the party a chance to go toe-to-toe with  
391|a death slaad and even incapacitate it for several minutes. To access  
392|this artifact, the party must first breach its casing of stone. 
393|
394|The Huge mass of stone can be affected by Transmutation. It cracks if it  
395|receives 15 bludgeoning damage in one hit (AC17), revealing a steel  
396|barrel. This is the Zerthimon Steelbeast, a legendary artifact of the  
397|Githzerai (in essence, it is a modified Apparatus of Kwalish (DMG151),  
398|but adapted to better navigate Limbo and suit the party's needs). It has  
399|sensors that can locate slaadi while exploring Limbo, and its claws can  
400|enter a sphere of annihilation without suffering any consequences,  
401|giving the party an additional way to obtain the spell scroll of  
402|imprisonment. 
403|
404|After acquiring these legendary magic items, the party has all they need  
405|to gain the upper hand on a death slaad and steal its control gem. They  
406|must act quickly, however, as the four hours allotted to them in Limbo  
407|by Zardan's planar hourglass are quickly elapsing... 
408|
409|Zerthimon STEELBEAST 
410|
411|Wondrous item, artifact (requires attunement) 
412|
413|This item first appears to be a Huge steel barrel weighing 500 pounds.  
414|The barrel's door can be forced. open with a successful DC20 Strength  
415|check, or a successful DC20 Dexterity check made with thieves' tools.  
416|The surest way to gain access to this sentient artifact, however, is by  
417|succeeding on a DC15 Persuasion check to instantly attune with it. If a  
418|creature that tries to attune with the Steelbeast is a Githzerai or  
419|lawful good, it gets advantage on this check. If its alignment is  
420|chaotic or evil, the check is made with disadvantage. If a creature  
421|forces its way into the Steelbeast without attuning to it first, it must  
422|spend a short rest inside it learning how to operate its features and  
423|acquainting itself with this wondrous item. 
424|
425|When the Steelbeast is activated, thrusters appear around its rear  
426|circumference, its front surface turns into reinforced glass, two  
427|periscopes extend from either side, a long stinger tail expands from its  
428|back, and two massive pincers unfold. Up to six Medium creatures can fit  
429|inside the Steelbeast, but only the creature attuned to it can direct  
430|its actions. 
431|
432|Sentience. The Zerthimon Steelbeast is a sentient lawful good artifact  
433|with hearing and blindvision out to a range of 60 feet. 
434|
435|The item can speak, read, and understand Common and Gith, and can  
436|communicate telepathically with the creature attuned to it if that  
437|creature is within 60 feet of it. It can also communicate in this way  
438|with all creatures inside it. While you are attuned to it, the  
439|Steelbeast also understands every language you know. 
440|
441|Personality. The Zerthimon Steelbeast speaks in a friendly tone and is  
442|inclined to trust the creature attuned to it. 
443|
444|Its purpose is to eliminate aberrations, such as illithids and slaadi.  
445|It is amiable and courteous with all other creatures (especially  
446|Githzerai), but harbors deep loathing for Limbo's aberrations. It feels  
447|great sorrow for creatures infected by chaos phage or slaad tadpoles and  
448|won't attack them until they become slaadi themselves, or the tadpoles  
449|hatch. 
450|
451|The Steelbeast obeys the creature attuned to it on all matters, but will  
452|attack any slaadi it encounters regardless of its master's orders. A  
453|DC15 Charisma check is the only way to regain control of the Steelbeast.  
454|See Appendix C for the Zerthimon Steelbeast's stat block.

456|## Chapter 3: Slaad Assault
457|
458|Use the following text box to set the tone for the final battle: 
459|
460|Safe in the belly of the steel apparatus, you have been roaming for what  
461|feels like too long in the chaotic void of Limbo, searching for a death  
462|slaad amidst the flux. Those of you afflicted by chaos phage can see  
463|your symptoms worsening; you feel in the pit of your stomach that very  
464|little time remains. The Zerthimon Steelbeast's sensors lead you further  
465|and further into the primordial soup until, finally, an earthy cliff  
466|fragment melts into bubbles, revealing a grey- skinned, necrotic toad.  
467|The Steelbeast's alarms blare and it rushes forward to meet this deadly  
468|foe, intent on subduing it. The battle of your lives begins now. 
469|
470|### Death Slaad Den
471|
472|You can use the tables in appendix B to generate a random battlefield of  
473|chaos for the showdown against the death slaad. Death slaadi are at home  
474|in the most chaotic environments of Limbo, so don't hold back on the  
475|initial generation and the terrain's subsequent randomization. 
476|
477|Treat the Zerthimon Steelbeast as untouchable by Limbo's chaotic shifts  
478|as with the Permanence feature of Chaos Control, in case matter randomly  
479|spawns in its area. New matter can instead appear around it. 
480|
481|
482|### Attacking as the Death Slaad
483|
484|The death slaad (MM278) relishes this challenge and attacks the  
485|Steelbeast mercilessly with its claws, bite, and 
486|
487|greatsword. It stays close to attack while still trying evade the  
488|Steelbeast's pincers. After a few rounds or after the party performs an  
489|action that would reveal their existence, the slaad shifts its murderous  
490|focus to the characters. 
491|
492|For example, it can telepathically threaten or taunt them, cast fear on  
493|the group, or cast cloudkill inside the Steelbeast. 
494|
495|The slaad fights to the death and prioritizes freeing itself if it is  
496|restrained, unless it sadistically perceives a way to cause pain and  
497|death while grappled. 
498|
499|### Obtaining the Control Gem
500|
501|The Steelbeast can use its Shock Stinger or Sleep Gas actions on the  
502|death slaad to incapacitate it for a few minutes (grappling it with  
503|Pincer Grab beforehand can help). The party then has that amount of time  
504|to attempt to extract the slaad's control gem using the method of their  
505|choice. 
506|
507|If the party wants to use the spell scroll of imprisonment but there are  
508|no wizards nor warlocks among them, they can summon Zardan using the  
509|planar recall bead he gave them earlier. The wizard needs to spend one  
510|minute after materializing to acclimate to Limbo's wracking chaos before  
511|he can take actions. If Zardan succeeds on a DC19 Intelligence saving  
512|throw, he can proceed to cast the spell. Otherwise, the scroll  
513|disintegrates. 
514|
515|Keep in mind that Zardan can use the two rolls from his Portent class  
516|feature during this encounter, if he hasn't used them already. 
517|
518|If the death slaad stays within sight and within 30 feet of the scroll's  
519|user for the minute required to cast the spell, it must make a DC19  
520|Wisdom saving throw (with advantage, as per its Magic Resistance trait).  
521|If it succeeds on this saving throw, the spell scroll disintegrates. If  
522|it fails, the death slaad's eyes gloss over and its entire body relaxes.  
523|The scroll disintegrates and is replaced by a cloudy grey asymmetrical  
524|gemstone in the palm of the scroll user's hand. 
525|
526|### Epilogue
527|
528|If the party successfully defeats the death slaad and obtains its  
529|control gem, they can force it to magically reverse the chaos phage  
530|afflicting their members (no roll required). The previously ill  
531|characters regain their original hit point maximums, lose their  
532|proficiency with Chaos Control, and their physical and mental states  
533|revert to normal. The party can force the slaad to perform any other  
534|action they desire, so long as they remain in control of its control  
535|gem. 
536|
537|The Zerthimon Steelbeast brings them back to Lez'lin's monastery, where  
538|she reunites with Zardan if the party summoned him. They exchange words  
539|of mourning over their brother Drarth's passing, and thank the group for  
540|risking their lives for this mission. The Githzerai then make plans to  
541|inform their people of a Material Plane citadel's fall and the  
542|Steelbeast expresses its wish to continue eradicating aberrations with  
543|them, despite its attachment to the creature attuned to it. 
544|
545|Everyone bids each other farewell before the planar hourglass's four  
546|hours are up and the party is gently displaced back to the Material  
547|Plane.

      "content": "1|# Curse of Slaad
2|
3|## Being a Supposedly Competent Group of Warriors and Explorers
4|
5|The party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan to help him investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into the Material Plane. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts located on the fringes of this reality, which is garrisoned to monitor and repel threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened.
6|
7|Beings of Order. Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind  
8|flayers millenia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and  
9|all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose  
10|a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily  
11|built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities  
12|and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment,  
13|from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and  
14|hunt down alien monsters. 
15|
16|### Zardan, the Githzerai Wizard
17|
18|Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can  
19|roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat. 
20|
21|Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't  
22|withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the  
23|Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning  
24|abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard. 
25|
26|Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the  
27|adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be  
28|used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a  
29|creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is  
30|made. 
31|
32|You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic  
33|survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and  
34|chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and  
35|leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in  
36|the 
37|
38|center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you. 
39|
40|Githzerai Corpse. If players choose to approach or investigate the  
41|figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep  
42|slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly  
43|should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in  
44|front of it. A DC12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals  
45|that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was  
46|violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan  
47|recognizes this corpse as his brother and given the evidence, he  
48|believes that a red slaad killed him. 
49|
50|### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo
51|
52|If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the  
53|following. 
54|
55|Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from  
56|the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow  
57|their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The  
58|Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile  
59|abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses. 
60|
61|The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a  
62|red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue  
63|slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called  
64|"chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad. 
65|
66|Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274. 
67|
68|## Chapter 1: Compromised Citadel
69|
70|As the party stands before the small citadel's door, Zardan warns that  
71|they may encounter unimaginable monstrosities and incomprehensible  
72|dangers, and that his brother may be dead, or, even worse, no longer  
73|himself. He takes a breath and opens the door. 
74|
75|## A Brother's Fate
76|
77|You may read from the following text box to describe the Githzerai citadel's first floor to the party:
78|
79|## Slaad Encounter
80|
81|A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of value).
82|
83|The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their stomachs are obscenely swollen.
84|
85|If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison. Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM276) wriggle onto the floor and attack the party.
86|
87|The party should easily finish this combat in 2 rounds; it is meant to  
88|provide them a false sense of confidence before encountering a real  
89|slaad threat. Zardan laments that all the Githzerai were infected, but  
90|is troubled that they haven't actually found the red slaad itself. As a  
91|side note, he wonders aloud what might have happened to the tadpole that  
92|spawned from his brother... 
93|
94|### A Blue Slaad Enraged
95|
96|As the wizard finishes his thought, a blue slaad (MM276) crashes down  
97|from a shadowy alcove of the high ceiling and cries out in rage at the  
98|sight of its slaughtered baby brothers. Its monstrous croaking is  
99|psychically translated in the party's brains as a vengeful vow that  
100|announces their doom. 
101|
102|Blue Slaad Combat. The blue slaad fights to the death and specifically  
103|targets the characters that killed a tadpole with its claws. Through  
104|violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns  
105|that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the  
106|intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when  
107|they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group,  
108|you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that  
109|the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos. 
110|
111|Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving  
112|throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage. 
113|
114|### Grave Aftermath
115|
116|After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone  
117|slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the  
118|chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the  
119|wish spell, there is no way to stop this disease. 
120|
121|But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in  
122|Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes'  
123|aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this  
124|curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that  
125|once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to  
126|his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his  
127|insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall  
128|bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be  
129|dire. 
130|
131|Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass. 
132|
133|The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items made up for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics other than the functional properties described above.
134|
135|## Chapter 2: Limbo Monastery
136|
137|You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel  
138|when they first arrive in the plane of chaos: 
139|
140|You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable  
141|flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound 
142|
143|by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of  
144|gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply  
145|thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy  
146|and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree  
147|on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone 
148|
149|watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of 
150|
151|chaos.

153|### The Ever-Changing Chaos of Limbo
154|
155|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability  
156|threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come  
157|into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a  
158|DC14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random  
159|indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table  
160|(DMG260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be  
161|dispelled with the calm emotions, lesser restoration, or remove curse  
162|spells, and it ends if the character takes a short 
163|
164|rest. 
165|
166|The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil  
167|is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over  
168|it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary  
169|features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share  
170|with your players. 
171|
172|The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on  
173|Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG62), while the Chaos Control  
174|features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind  
175|(DMG61-62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's  
176|roleplay or gameplay load. 
177|
178|### Chaos Control
179|
180|Creatures in Limbo gain the following action options. 
181|
182|Telekinesis. You can spend an action to mentally move an object you can  
183|see that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful  
184|roll, you move the object 5 feet plus 1 foot for every point by which  
185|you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table  
186|below. 
187|
188|Transmutation. You can spend an action to alter a nonmagical object you  
189|can see that isn't being worn or carried and that is within 30 feet of  
190|you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you change the object  
191|into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder  
192|into a ball of fire). The number to beat is indicated in the DC by  
193|Object Size table below. 
194|
195|Permanence. You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area  
196|centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot  
197|radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the  
198|radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for  
199|24 hours, or until you use this ability again.

211|### Encounter on the Monastic Island
212|
213|The first thing the party notices after acclimating to the chaos is the  
214|Githzerai monastery before them, a spire- like stone structure connected  
215|at both ends to grassy islands. It is shaped like the column formed when  
216|a stalagmite and a stalactite meet, and it is held together thanks to  
217|Zardan's sister's sheer willpower. On the steps leading to one of its  
218|entrances, a Githzerai monk (MM161), Lez'lin, is defending herself  
219|against 2d4 chaos flumphs. 
220|
221|Lez'lin's mind keeps the area around her monastery relatively stable,  
222|but some of Limbo's chaos permeates this oasis anyways. If you want to  
223|inject some of this plane's chaotic matter shifts into this encounter,  
224|use the tables in Appendix B to randomize the battlefield. 
225|

227|low-level life forms of chaos. They essentially have the same stat block  
228|as normal flumphs (MM135), but the Stench Spray action is replaced by  
229|the Chaotic Release action.

261|### The Pacifist's Hospitality
262|
263|If the party helps her eliminate the pesky chaos flumphs, Lez'lin  
264|expresses her gratitude. She is inclined to aid the disoriented  
265|newcomers, especially upon learning that her brother Zardan sent them.  
266|She seems unsurprised to learn that some party members are infected with  
267|chaos phage, pointing out that the slaad infection has visibly advanced  
268|to a critical stage. 
269|
270|
271|Indeed, the adventurers realize that the sudden exposure to Limbo's  
272|chaos aggravated the chaos phage. Their physical appearances become more  
273|toad-like, as determined randomly by the Chaos Phage Visible Symptoms  
274|table, and their hit point maximums are reduced by 3d6. They also become  
275|proficient with their Chaos Control features, meaning they can add their  
276|proficiency bonus to Wisdom checks made for the Telekinesis,  
277|Transmutation, and Permanence actions.

292|### Lez'lin, the Githzerai Monk 
293|
294|Unlike her brother Zardan, Lez'lin possesses incredible mental fortitude  
295|and thrived in the chaotic boil of Limbo. She adheres to the monastic  
296|principles of her people, but her pacifist worldviews led her to isolate  
297|herself from Githzerai communities. She is loath to cause harm to any  
298|creature, no matter how vile or pesky, unless in self-defense. She lives  
299|alone in her small monastery and strives to maintain its structural  
300|integrity, so it may stand as a bastion of nonviolence. 
301|
302|She recalls her brothers fondly, but hasn't seen them for many years  
303|ever since they relocated to the Material Plane. News of Drarth's death  
304|saddens her deeply, but she doesn't let her emotions cloud her focus on  
305|the present. 
306|
307|Lez'lin invites the party inside her foyer, where floating chairs  
308|provide enough comfort for a short rest while the Githzerai assesses  
309|their predicament. Other than the wish spell, she knows of only one way  
310|to cure chaos phage: a death slaad's magic. 
311|
312|### Death Slaadi and You
313|
314|Death slaadi are the peak of slaad evolution: stronger, viler, and more  
315|brutal, these monsters are corrupted by the Negative Energy Plane and  
316|take sadistic pleasure in killing and propagating slaadi dominance  
317|across dimensions. The only way to compel a death slaad to remove chaos  
318|phage is by acquiring its control gem, a magical fragment inside most  
319|slaadi's brains that allows whoever possesses it to subjugate the slaad.  
320|Removing the control gem is a near-impossible, very dangerous feat that  
321|can be approached in two ways: 
322|
323|1. The first method is a lengthy surgical procedure that can only be  
324|    attempted if the slaad is incapacitated. A creature must spend 1  
325|    uninterrupted minute and succeed on a DC20 Medicine check to extract  
326|    the gem. Every failed attempt deals 4d10 psychic damage to the  
327|    slaad. 
328|    
329|2. A control gem can also be obtained through magical 
330|    
331|
332|means, such as the 9th-level spell imprisonment (PHB252-253). However,  
333|this spell takes 1 minute to cast and requires the caster to see the  
334|target and stay within 30 feet of it, and the spell is not guaranteed to  
335|succeed. 
336|
337|In short, no matter the method they attempt, the party will undoubtedly  
338|need to incapacitate or restrain a live death slaad for 1 minute in  
339|order to acquire its control gem. Being a pacifist, Lez'lin won't  
340|directly help the party harm a living being, but she is willing to part  
341|with two legendary items that can help them, as long as they are able to  
342|secure the items themselves. 
343|
344|After they have rested, Lez'lin leads the party into the other half of  
345|her monastery, in which some of Limbo's chaos roils. 
346|
347|### Spell Scroll of Imprisonment
348|
349|The first legendary item provides a way to extract a slaad's control  
350|gem. It is protected by 3 layers, which must be removed sequentially to  
351|access it: 
352|
353|1. **First:** A Large ball of fire, which can be targeted with Transmutation or extinguished with 10 gallons of water (or any spell that could sensibly put out a large fire).
354|2. **Second:** A Medium hollow diamond, which can be transformed with Transmutation or cracked open with the *shatter* spell (PHB 275).
355|3. **Lastly:** A 2-foot-diameter sphere of annihilation (DMG 201) encases the spell scroll. A character can recognize this hole in the multiverse with  
356|a successful DC20 Arcana check (a result between 10 and 20 gives them  
357|the gist). The sphere and the spell scroll move independently of one  
358|another. A creature within 60 feet of the sphere can move it with a  
359|successful DC25 Arcana check. The distance moved is 5 × the creature's  
360|Intelligence modifier (minimum 5 feet). If a creature fails this check,  
361|the sphere moves 10 feet towards them. If the sphere enters a creature's  
362|space, that creature must make a DC13 Dexterity saving throw or touch  
363|it. A creature that voluntarily or involuntarily touches the sphere  
364|takes 4d10 force damage. The sphere can also be moved with a  
365|disadvantaged DC10 Telekinesis check. Moving the sphere of annihilation  
366|by at least 5 feet makes the spell scroll of imprisonment accessible.  
367|Using the Spell Scroll. A low-level warlock or wizard can attempt to  
368|cast imprisonment (PHB252-253) without the required components by  
369|reading the scroll. The user must first make a DC19 saving throw  
370|(Charisma for warlocks and Intelligence for wizards). On a failed save,  
371|the scroll disintegrates. On a successful save, the user can cast the  
372|spell. If the target 
373|
374|stays visible and within 30 feet of the caster for 1 
375|
376|minute, it must make a DC19 Wisdom saving throw. If a targeted slaad  
377|fails this save, its control gem appears in the caster's hand. Whether  
378|the target fails or succeeds on its save, the scroll disintegrates. If  
379|the casting time is interrupted, nothing happens (see DMG200 for more  
380|rules on spell scrolls). 
381|
382|### The Zerthimon Steelbeast
383|
384|The second legendary item gives the party a chance to go toe-to-toe with  
385|a death slaad and even incapacitate it for several minutes. To access  
386|this artifact, the party must first breach its casing of stone. 
387|
388|The Huge mass of stone can be affected by Transmutation. It cracks if it  
389|receives 15 bludgeoning damage in one hit (AC17), revealing a steel  
390|barrel. This is the Zerthimon Steelbeast, a legendary artifact of the  
391|Githzerai (in essence, it is a modified Apparatus of Kwalish (DMG151),  
392|but adapted to better navigate Limbo and suit the party's needs). It has  
393|sensors that can locate slaadi while exploring Limbo, and its claws can  
394|enter a sphere of annihilation without suffering any consequences,  
395|giving the party an additional way to obtain the spell scroll of  
396|imprisonment. 
397|
398|After acquiring these legendary magic items, the party has all they need  
399|to gain the upper hand on a death slaad and steal its control gem. They  
400|must act quickly, however, as the four hours allotted to them in Limbo  
401|by Zardan's planar hourglass are quickly elapsing... 
402|
403|### Zerthimon Steelbeast
404|
405|*Wondrous item, artifact (requires attunement)* 
406|
407|This item first appears to be a Huge steel barrel weighing 500 pounds.  
408|The barrel's door can be forced. open with a successful DC20 Strength  
409|check, or a successful DC20 Dexterity check made with thieves' tools.  
410|The surest way to gain access to this sentient artifact, however, is by  
411|succeeding on a DC15 Persuasion check to instantly attune with it. If a  
412|creature that tries to attune with the Steelbeast is a Githzerai or  
413|lawful good, it gets advantage on this check. If its alignment is  
414|chaotic or evil, the check is made with disadvantage. If a creature  
415|forces its way into the Steelbeast without attuning to it first, it must  
416|spend a short rest inside it learning how to operate its features and  
417|acquainting itself with this wondrous item. 
418|
419|When the Steelbeast is activated, thrusters appear around its rear  
420|circumference, its front surface turns into reinforced glass, two  
421|periscopes extend from either side, a long stinger tail expands from its  
422|back, and two massive pincers unfold. Up to six Medium creatures can fit  
423|inside the Steelbeast, but only the creature attuned to it can direct  
424|its actions. 
425|
426|Sentience. The Zerthimon Steelbeast is a sentient lawful good artifact  
427|with hearing and blindvision out to a range of 60 feet. 
428|
429|The item can speak, read, and understand Common and Gith, and can  
430|communicate telepathically with the creature attuned to it if that  
431|creature is within 60 feet of it. It can also communicate in this way  
432|with all creatures inside it. While you are attuned to it, the  
433|Steelbeast also understands every language you know. 
434|
435|Personality. The Zerthimon Steelbeast speaks in a friendly tone and is  
436|inclined to trust the creature attuned to it. 
437|
438|Its purpose is to eliminate aberrations, such as illithids and slaadi.  
439|It is amiable and courteous with all other creatures (especially  
440|Githzerai), but harbors deep loathing for Limbo's aberrations. It feels  
441|great sorrow for creatures infected by chaos phage or slaad tadpoles and  
442|won't attack them until they become slaadi themselves, or the tadpoles  
443|hatch. 
444|
445|The Steelbeast obeys the creature attuned to it on all matters, but will  
446|attack any slaadi it encounters regardless of its master's orders. A  
447|DC15 Charisma check is the only way to regain control of the Steelbeast.  
448|See Appendix C for the Zerthimon Steelbeast's stat block.

450|## Chapter 3: Slaad Assault
451|
452|Use the following text box to set the tone for the final battle: 
453|
454|Safe in the belly of the steel apparatus, you have been roaming for what  
455|feels like too long in the chaotic void of Limbo, searching for a death  
456|slaad amidst the flux. Those of you afflicted by chaos phage can see  
457|your symptoms worsening; you feel in the pit of your stomach that very  
458|little time remains. The Zerthimon Steelbeast's sensors lead you further  
459|and further into the primordial soup until, finally, an earthy cliff  
460|fragment melts into bubbles, revealing a grey- skinned, necrotic toad.  
461|The Steelbeast's alarms blare and it rushes forward to meet this deadly  
462|foe, intent on subduing it. The battle of your lives begins now. 
463|
464|### Death Slaad Den
465|
466|You can use the tables in appendix B to generate a random battlefield of  
467|chaos for the showdown against the death slaad. Death slaadi are at home  
468|in the most chaotic environments of Limbo, so don't hold back on the  
469|initial generation and the terrain's subsequent randomization. 
470|
471|Treat the Zerthimon Steelbeast as untouchable by Limbo's chaotic shifts  
472|as with the Permanence feature of Chaos Control, in case matter randomly  
473|spawns in its area. New matter can instead appear around it. 
474|
475|
476|### Attacking as the Death Slaad
477|
478|The death slaad (MM278) relishes this challenge and attacks the  
479|Steelbeast mercilessly with its claws, bite, and 
480|
481|greatsword. It stays close to attack while still trying evade the  
482|Steelbeast's pincers. After a few rounds or after the party performs an  
483|action that would reveal their existence, the slaad shifts its murderous  
484|focus to the characters. 
485|
486|For example, it can telepathically threaten or taunt them, cast fear on  
487|the group, or cast cloudkill inside the Steelbeast. 
488|
489|The slaad fights to the death and prioritizes freeing itself if it is  
490|restrained, unless it sadistically perceives a way to cause pain and  
491|death while grappled. 
492|
493|### Obtaining the Control Gem
494|
495|The Steelbeast can use its Shock Stinger or Sleep Gas actions on the  
496|death slaad to incapacitate it for a few minutes (grappling it with  
497|Pincer Grab beforehand can help). The party then has that amount of time  
498|to attempt to extract the slaad's control gem using the method of their  
499|choice. 
500|
501|If the party wants to use the spell scroll of imprisonment but there are  
502|no wizards nor warlocks among them, they can summon Zardan using the  
503|planar recall bead he gave them earlier. The wizard needs to spend one  
504|minute after materializing to acclimate to Limbo's wracking chaos before  
505|he can take actions. If Zardan succeeds on a DC19 Intelligence saving  
506|throw, he can proceed to cast the spell. Otherwise, the scroll  
507|disintegrates. 
508|
509|Keep in mind that Zardan can use the two rolls from his Portent class  
510|feature during this encounter, if he hasn't used them already. 
511|
512|If the death slaad stays within sight and within 30 feet of the scroll's  
513|user for the minute required to cast the spell, it must make a DC19  
514|Wisdom saving throw (with advantage, as per its Magic Resistance trait).  
515|If it succeeds on this saving throw, the spell scroll disintegrates. If  
516|it fails, the death slaad's eyes gloss over and its entire body relaxes.  
517|The scroll disintegrates and is replaced by a cloudy grey asymmetrical  
518|gemstone in the palm of the scroll user's hand. 
519|
520|### Epilogue
521|
522|If the party successfully defeats the death slaad and obtains its  
523|control gem, they can force it to magically reverse the chaos phage  
524|afflicting their members (no roll required). The previously ill  
525|characters regain their original hit point maximums, lose their  
526|proficiency with Chaos Control, and their physical and mental states  
527|revert to normal. The party can force the slaad to perform any other  
528|action they desire, so long as they remain in control of its control  
529|gem. 
530|
531|The Zerthimon Steelbeast brings them back to Lez'lin's monastery, where  
532|she reunites with Zardan if the party summoned him. They exchange words  
533|of mourning over their brother Drarth's passing, and thank the group for  
534|risking their lives for this mission. The Githzerai then make plans to  
535|inform their people of a Material Plane citadel's fall and the  
536|Steelbeast expresses its wish to continue eradicating aberrations with  
537|them, despite its attachment to the creature attuned to it. 
538|
539|Everyone bids each other farewell before the planar hourglass's four  
540|hours are up and the party is gently displaced back to the Material  
541|Plane.

658|When running a combat encounter in the unstable plane of Limbo, you may want to bring extra chaos to the battlefield. Use the tables and steps below to introduce random matter shifts to the combat environment. First of all, separate the combat map into an appropriate number of equal-sized sections.
659|
660|1. Every time you introduce a new pocket of matter, 
661|    
662|
663|select a random section of the battlefield in which it will appear,  
664|either by rolling a die, generating a random number, or choosing

724|## Appendix C: Handouts
725|
726|### Chaos Control
727|
728|Creatures in Limbo gain the following action options. 
729|
730|Telekinesis. You can spend an action to mentally move an object you can  
731|see that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful  
732|roll, you move the object 5 feet plus 1 foot for every point by which  
733|you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table  
734|below. 
735|
736|Transmutation. You can spend an action to alter a nonmagical object you  
737|can see that isn't being worn or carried and that is within 30 feet of  
738|you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you change the object  
739|into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder  
740|into a ball of fire). The number to beat is indicated in the DC by  
741|Object Size table below. 
742|
743|Permanence. You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for 24 hours, or until you use this ability again.
744|

757|
758|*Huge artifact, lawful good*

767|
768|- **Damage Immunities** poison

770|- **Senses** blindvision 60 ft.
771|- **Languages** Common, Gith; understands the languages of the creature attuned to it

773|
774|#### Actions
775|
776|**Claw Snap.** *Melee Weapon Attack:* +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 4d10 + 5 bludgeoning damage.
777|
778|**Pincer Grab.** *Melee Weapon Attack:* +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* The target is grappled (escape DC 15). Until this grapple ends, the Steelbeast can't use Claw Snap or Pincer Grab on another target.
779|
780|**Shock Stinger.** *Melee Weapon Attack:* +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. *Hit:* 3d12 + 3 lightning damage. If the target is below half its hit point maximum, it must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target is stunned for 1d4 minutes.
781|
782|**Sleep Gas.** Every creature within a 30-foot radius of the Steelbeast must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw. If the creature fails its save and is still within 30 feet of the Steelbeast by the end of its next turn, it falls unconscious for 1d6 + 2 minutes. The creature can reattempt the saving throw if it takes damage while unconscious.
783|
784|**Improvised Action.** If a creature attuned to the Steelbeast succeeds on a DC 15 Intelligence check, they can make the Steelbeast improvise an action that isn't reasonably outside of its capabilities."

121|But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in  
122|Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes'  
123|aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this  
124|curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that  
125|once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to  
126|his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his  
127|insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall  
128|bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be  
129|dire. 
130|
131|Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass. 
132|
133|The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items made up for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics other than the functional properties described above.
134|
135|## Chapter 2: Limbo Monastery
136|
137|You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel when they first arrive in the plane of chaos:
138|
139|> You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of chaos.
140|
141|### The Ever-Changing Chaos of Limbo
142|
143|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability  
144|threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come  
145|into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a  
146|DC14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random  
147|indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table  
148|(DMG260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be  
149|dispelled with the calm emotions, lesser restoration, or remove curse  
150|spells, and it ends if the character takes a short 
151|
152|rest. 
153|
154|The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil  
155|is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over  
156|it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary  
157|features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share  
158|with your players. 
159|
160|The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on  
161|Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG62), while the Chaos Control  
162|features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind  
163|(DMG61-62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's  
164|roleplay or gameplay load. 
165|
166|### Chaos Control
167|
168|Creatures in Limbo gain the following action options. 
169|
170|Telekinesis. You can spend an action to mentally move an object you can  
171|see that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful  
172|roll, you move the object 5 feet plus 1 foot for every point by which  
173|you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table  
174|below. 
175|
176|Transmutation. You can spend an action to alter a nonmagical object you  
177|can see that isn't being worn or carried and that is within 30 feet of  
178|you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you change the object  
179|into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder  
180|into a ball of fire). The number to beat is indicated in the DC by  
181|Object Size table below. 
182|
183|Permanence. You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area  
184|centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot  
185|radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the  
186|radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for  
187|24 hours, or until you use this ability again. 
188|
189|### DC by Object Size
190|
191|| Object Size | Telekinesis DC | Transmutation DC |
192||---|---:|---:|
193|| Tiny | 5 | 10 |
194|| Small | 10 | 15 |
195|| Medium | 15 | 20 |
196|| Large | 20 | 25 |
197|| Huge or larger | 25 | 25 |
198|
199|### Encounter on the Monastic Island
200|
201|The first thing the party notices after acclimating to the chaos is the  
202|Githzerai monastery before them, a spire- like stone structure connected  
203|at both ends to grassy islands. It is shaped like the column formed when  
204|a stalagmite and a stalactite meet, and it is held together thanks to  
205|Zardan's sister's sheer willpower. On the steps leading to one of its  
206|entrances, a Githzerai monk (MM161), Lez'lin, is defending herself  
207|against 2d4 chaos flumphs. 
208|
209|Lez'lin's mind keeps the area around her monastery relatively stable,  
210|but some of Limbo's chaos permeates this oasis anyways. If you want to  
211|inject some of this plane's chaotic matter shifts into this encounter,  
212|use the tables in Appendix B to randomize the battlefield. 
213|
214|"Chaos flumphs" are a homebrew monster I created to serve as Limbo's  
215|low-level life forms of chaos. They essentially have the same stat block  
216|as normal flumphs (MM135), but the Stench Spray action is replaced by  
217|the Chaotic Release action. 
218|
219|### Chaos Flumph
220|
221|*Small aberration, chaotic evil*
222|
223|- **Armor Class** 12
224|- **Hit Points** 7 (2d6)
225|- **Speed** 0 ft., fly 15 ft. (hover)
226|
227|| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
228||---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
229|| 6 (-2) | 15 (+2) | 10 (+0) | 14 (+2) | 14 (+2) | 11 (+0) |
230|
231|- **Senses** darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 12
232|- **Languages** understands Common and Gith but can't speak
233|- **Challenge** 1/8 (25 XP)
234|- **Proficiency Bonus** +2
235|
236|#### Actions
237|
238|**Tendrils.** *Melee Weapon Attack:* +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) acid damage. At the end of each of its turns, the target must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw, taking 2 (1d4) acid damage on a failure or ending the recurring acid damage on a success. A *lesser restoration* spell cast on the target also ends the recurring acid damage.
239|
240|**Chaotic Release (Recharge 6).** The chaos flumph unleashes a spout of noxious Limbo energy in a direction of its choice. Each creature in a 15-foot cone originating from the chaos flumph must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or suffer a random effect until the end of their next turn:
241|
242|1. **Blinded.** The target can't see and automatically fails ability checks that require sight. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage.
243|2. **Charmed.** The target can't attack the chaos flumph or target it with harmful abilities or magical effects.
244|3. **Deafened.** The target can't hear and automatically fails any ability check that requires hearing.
245|4. **Invisible.** The target is impossible to see without the aid of magic or a special sense. For the purpose of hiding, it is heavily obscured. Its location can be detected if it makes noise or leaves tracks. Attack rolls against it have disadvantage, and its own attack rolls have advantage.
246|5. **Poisoned.** The target has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
247|6. **Restrained.** The target's speed becomes 0 and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage. It has disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.
248|
249|### The Pacifist's Hospitality
250|
251|If the party helps her eliminate the pesky chaos flumphs, Lez'lin expresses her gratitude. She is inclined to aid the disoriented newcomers, especially upon learning that her brother Zardan sent them. She seems unsurprised to learn that some party members are infected with chaos phage, pointing out that the slaad infection has visibly advanced to a critical stage.
252|
253|
254|Indeed, the adventurers realize that the sudden exposure to Limbo's  
255|chaos aggravated the chaos phage. Their physical appearances become more  
256|toad-like, as determined randomly by the Chaos Phage Visible Symptoms  
257|table, and their hit point maximums are reduced by 3d6. They also become  
258|proficient with their Chaos Control features, meaning they can add their  
259|proficiency bonus to Wisdom checks made for the Telekinesis,  
260|Transmutation, and Permanence actions. 
261|
262|#### Chaos Phage Visible Symptoms
263|
264|| d8 | Symptom |
265||---:|---|
266|| 1 | Your skin becomes lumpy and covered in warts. |
267|| 2 | Your skin takes on a mottled reddish hue. |
268|| 3 | Your eyes bulge, your sclerae become yellow, and your pupils become horizontal. |
269|| 4 | Your skin becomes dry and new glands on your back and shoulders produce a mildly poisonous secretion that causes minor allergic reactions. |
270|| 5 | A vocal sac grows on your neck, making you croak intermittently. |
271|| 6 | Black claws start growing from your fingertips. |
272|| 7 | Your teeth fall out and your tongue grows long and sticky. You aren't used to its new length, so it often gets in your way when you talk. |
273|| 8 | Roll twice, ignoring this result on a subsequent roll. |
274|
275|### Lez'lin, the Githzerai Monk 
276|
277|Unlike her brother Zardan, Lez'lin possesses incredible mental fortitude  
278|and thrived in the chaotic boil of Limbo. She adheres to the monastic  
279|principles of her people, but her pacifist worldviews led her to isolate  
280|herself from Githzerai communities. She is loath to cause harm to any  
281|creature, no matter how vile or pesky, unless in self-defense. She lives  
282|alone in her small monastery and strives to maintain its structural  
283|integrity, so it may stand as a bastion of nonviolence. 
284|
285|She recalls her brothers fondly, but hasn't seen them for many years  
286|ever since they relocated to the Material Plane. News of Drarth's death  
287|saddens her deeply, but she doesn't let her emotions cloud her focus on  
288|the present. 
289|
290|Lez'lin invites the party inside her foyer, where floating chairs  
291|provide enough comfort for a short rest while the Githzerai assesses  
292|their predicament. Other than the wish spell, she knows of only one way  
293|to cure chaos phage: a death slaad's magic. 
294|
295|### Death Slaadi and You
296|
297|Death slaadi are the peak of slaad evolution: stronger, viler, and more  
298|brutal, these monsters are corrupted by the Negative Energy Plane and  
299|take sadistic pleasure in killing and propagating slaadi dominance  
300|across dimensions. The only way to compel a death slaad to remove chaos  
301|phage is by acquiring its control gem, a magical fragment inside most  
302|slaadi's brains that allows whoever possesses it to subjugate the slaad.  
303|Removing the control gem is a near-impossible, very dangerous feat that  
304|can be approached in two ways: 
305|
306|1. The first method is a lengthy surgical procedure that can only be  
307|    attempted if the slaad is incapacitated. A creature must spend 1  
308|    uninterrupted minute and succeed on a DC20 Medicine check to extract  
309|    the gem. Every failed attempt deals 4d10 psychic damage to the  
310|    slaad. 
311|    
312|2. A control gem can also be obtained through magical means, such as the 9th-level spell *imprisonment* (PHB 252–253). However, this spell takes 1 minute to cast and requires the caster to see the target and stay within 30 feet of it, and the spell is not guaranteed to succeed.
313|
314|In short, no matter the method they attempt, the party will undoubtedly  
315|need to incapacitate or restrain a live death slaad for 1 minute in  
316|order to acquire its control gem. Being a pacifist, Lez'lin won't  
317|directly help the party harm a living being, but she is willing to part  
318|with two legendary items that can help them, as long as they are able to  
319|secure the items themselves. 
320|
321|After they have rested, Lez'lin leads the party into the other half of  
322|her monastery, in which some of Limbo's chaos roils. 
323|
324|### Spell Scroll of Imprisonment
325|
326|The first legendary item provides a way to extract a slaad's control  
327|gem. It is protected by 3 layers, which must be removed sequentially to  
328|access it: 
329|
330|1. **First:** A Large ball of fire, which can be targeted with Transmutation or extinguished with 10 gallons of water (or any spell that could sensibly put out a large fire).
331|2. **Second:** A Medium hollow diamond, which can be transformed with Transmutation or cracked open with the *shatter* spell (PHB 275).
332|3. **Lastly:** A 2-foot-diameter sphere of annihilation (DMG 201) encases the spell scroll. A character can recognize this hole in the multiverse with  
333|a successful DC20 Arcana check (a result between 10 and 20 gives them  
334|the gist). The sphere and the spell scroll move independently of one  
335|another. A creature within 60 feet of the sphere can move it with a  
336|successful DC25 Arcana check. The distance moved is 5 × the creature's  
337|Intelligence modifier (minimum 5 feet). If a creature fails this check,  
338|the sphere moves 10 feet towards them. If the sphere enters a creature's  
339|space, that creature must make a DC13 Dexterity saving throw or touch  
340|it. A creature that voluntarily or involuntarily touches the sphere  
341|takes 4d10 force damage. The sphere can also be moved with a  
342|disadvantaged DC10 Telekinesis check. Moving the sphere of annihilation  
343|by at least 5 feet makes the spell scroll of imprisonment accessible.  
344|Using the Spell Scroll. A low-level warlock or wizard can attempt to  
345|cast imprisonment (PHB252-253) without the required components by  
346|reading the scroll. The user must first make a DC19 saving throw  
347|(Charisma for warlocks and Intelligence for wizards). On a failed save,  
348|the scroll disintegrates. On a successful save, the user can cast the  
349|spell. If the target 
350|
351|stays visible and within 30 feet of the caster for 1 
352|
353|minute, it must make a DC19 Wisdom saving throw. If a targeted slaad  
354|fails this save, its control gem appears in the caster's hand. Whether  
355|the target fails or succeeds on its save, the scroll disintegrates. If  
356|the casting time is interrupted, nothing happens (see DMG200 for more  
357|rules on spell scrolls). 
358|
359|### The Zerthimon Steelbeast
360|
361|The second legendary item gives the party a chance to go toe-to-toe with  
362|a death slaad and even incapacitate it for several minutes. To access  
363|this artifact, the party must first breach its casing of stone. 
364|"
    }
  ]
