      "content": "300|across dimensions. The only way to compel a death slaad to remove chaos  
301|phage is by acquiring its control gem, a magical fragment inside most  
302|slaadi's brains that allows whoever possesses it to subjugate the slaad.  
303|Removing the control gem is a near-impossible, very dangerous feat that  
304|can be approached in two ways: 
305|
306|1. The first method is a lengthy surgical procedure that can only be  
307|    attempted if the slaad is incapacitated. A creature must spend 1  
308|    uninterrupted minute and succeed on a DC20 Medicine check to extract  
309|    the gem. Every failed attempt deals 4d10 psychic damage to the  
310|    slaad. 
311|    
312|2. A control gem can also be obtained through magical means, such as the 9th-level spell *imprisonment* (PHB 252–253). However, this spell takes 1 minute to cast and requires the caster to see the target and stay within 30 feet of it, and the spell is not guaranteed to succeed.
313|
314|In short, no matter the method they attempt, the party will undoubtedly  
315|need to incapacitate or restrain a live death slaad for 1 minute in  
316|order to acquire its control gem. Being a pacifist, Lez'lin won't  
317|directly help the party harm a living being, but she is willing to part  
318|with two legendary items that can help them, as long as they are able to  
319|secure the items themselves. 
320|
321|After they have rested, Lez'lin leads the party into the other half of  
322|her monastery, in which some of Limbo's chaos roils. 
323|
324|### Spell Scroll of Imprisonment
325|
326|The first legendary item provides a way to extract a slaad's control  
327|gem. It is protected by 3 layers, which must be removed sequentially to  
328|access it: 
329|
330|1. **First:** A Large ball of fire, which can be targeted with Transmutation or extinguished with 10 gallons of water (or any spell that could sensibly put out a large fire).
331|2. **Second:** A Medium hollow diamond, which can be transformed with Transmutation or cracked open with the *shatter* spell (PHB 275).
332|3. **Lastly:** A 2-foot-diameter sphere of annihilation (DMG 201) encases the spell scroll. A character can recognize this hole in the multiverse with  
333|a successful DC20 Arcana check (a result between 10 and 20 gives them  
334|the gist). The sphere and the spell scroll move independently of one  
335|another. A creature within 60 feet of the sphere can move it with a  
336|successful DC25 Arcana check. The distance moved is 5 × the creature's  
337|Intelligence modifier (minimum 5 feet). If a creature fails this check,  
338|the sphere moves 10 feet towards them. If the sphere enters a creature's  
339|space, that creature must make a DC13 Dexterity saving throw or touch  
340|it. A creature that voluntarily or involuntarily touches the sphere  
341|takes 4d10 force damage. The sphere can also be moved with a  
342|disadvantaged DC10 Telekinesis check. Moving the sphere of annihilation  
343|by at least 5 feet makes the spell scroll of imprisonment accessible.  
344|Using the Spell Scroll. A low-level warlock or wizard can attempt to  
345|cast imprisonment (PHB252-253) without the required components by  
346|reading the scroll. The user must first make a DC19 saving throw  
347|(Charisma for warlocks and Intelligence for wizards). On a failed save,  
348|the scroll disintegrates. On a successful save, the user can cast the  
349|spell. If the target 
350|
351|stays visible and within 30 feet of the caster for 1 
352|
353|minute, it must make a DC19 Wisdom saving throw. If a targeted slaad  
354|fails this save, its control gem appears in the caster's hand. Whether  
355|the target fails or succeeds on its save, the scroll disintegrates. If  
356|the casting time is interrupted, nothing happens (see DMG200 for more  
357|rules on spell scrolls). 
358|
359|### The Zerthimon Steelbeast
360|
361|The second legendary item gives the party a chance to go toe-to-toe with  
362|a death slaad and even incapacitate it for several minutes. To access  
363|this artifact, the party must first breach its casing of stone. 
364|
365|The Huge mass of stone can be affected by Transmutation. It cracks if it  
366|receives 15 bludgeoning damage in one hit (AC17), revealing a steel  
367|barrel. This is the Zerthimon Steelbeast, a legendary artifact of the  
368|Githzerai (in essence, it is a modified Apparatus of Kwalish (DMG151),  
369|but adapted to better navigate Limbo and suit the party's needs). It has  
370|sensors that can locate slaadi while exploring Limbo, and its claws can  
371|enter a sphere of annihilation without suffering any consequences,  
372|giving the party an additional way to obtain the spell scroll of  
373|imprisonment. 
374|
375|After acquiring these legendary magic items, the party has all they need  
376|to gain the upper hand on a death slaad and steal its control gem. They  
377|must act quickly, however, as the four hours allotted to them in Limbo  
378|by Zardan's planar hourglass are quickly elapsing... 
379|
380|### Zerthimon Steelbeast
381|
382|*Wondrous item, artifact (requires attunement)* 
383|
384|This item first appears to be a Huge steel barrel weighing 500 pounds.  
385|The barrel's door can be forced. open with a successful DC20 Strength  
386|check, or a successful DC20 Dexterity check made with thieves' tools.  
387|The surest way to gain access to this sentient artifact, however, is by  
388|succeeding on a DC15 Persuasion check to instantly attune with it. If a  
389|creature that tries to attune with the Steelbeast is a Githzerai or  
390|lawful good, it gets advantage on this check. If its alignment is  
391|chaotic or evil, the check is made with disadvantage. If a creature  
392|forces its way into the Steelbeast without attuning to it first, it must  
393|spend a short rest inside it learning how to operate its features and  
394|acquainting itself with this wondrous item. 
395|
396|When the Steelbeast is activated, thrusters appear around its rear  
397|circumference, its front surface turns into reinforced glass, two  
398|periscopes extend from either side, a long stinger tail expands from its  
399|back, and two massive pincers unfold. Up to six Medium creatures can fit  
400|inside the Steelbeast, but only the creature attuned to it can direct  
401|its actions. 
402|
403|Sentience. The Zerthimon Steelbeast is a sentient lawful good artifact  
404|with hearing and blindvision out to a range of 60 feet. 
405|
406|The item can speak, read, and understand Common and Gith, and can  
407|communicate telepathically with the creature attuned to it if that  
408|creature is within 60 feet of it. It can also communicate in this way  
409|with all creatures inside it. While you are attuned to it, the  
410|Steelbeast also understands every language you know. 
411|
412|Personality. The Zerthimon Steelbeast speaks in a friendly tone and is  
413|inclined to trust the creature attuned to it. 
414|
415|Its purpose is to eliminate aberrations, such as illithids and slaadi.  
416|It is amiable and courteous with all other creatures (especially  
417|Githzerai), but harbors deep loathing for Limbo's aberrations. It feels  
418|great sorrow for creatures infected by chaos phage or slaad tadpoles and  
419|won't attack them until they become slaadi themselves, or the tadpoles  
420|hatch. 
421|
422|The Steelbeast obeys the creature attuned to it on all matters, but will  
423|attack any slaadi it encounters regardless of its master's orders. A  
424|DC15 Charisma check is the only way to regain control of the Steelbeast.  "

### The Pacifist's Hospitality

If the party helps her eliminate the pesky chaos flumphs, Lez'lin expresses her gratitude. She is inclined to aid the disoriented newcomers, especially upon learning that her brother Zardan sent them. She seems unsurprised to learn that some party members are infected with chaos phage, pointing out that the slaad infection has visibly advanced to a critical stage.

Indeed, the adventurers realize that the sudden exposure to Limbo's chaos aggravated the chaos phage. Their physical appearances become more toad-like, as determined randomly by the Chaos Phage Visible Symptoms table, and their hit point maximums are reduced by 3d6. They also become proficient with their Chaos Control features, meaning they can add their proficiency bonus to Wisdom checks made for the Telekinesis, Transmutation, and Permanence actions.

      "content": "1|# Curse of Slaad
2|
3|## Being a Supposedly Competent Group of Warriors and Explorers
4|
5|The party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan to help him investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into the Material Plane. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts located on the fringes of this reality, which is garrisoned to monitor and repel threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened.
6|
7|Beings of Order. Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind  
8|flayers millenia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and  
9|all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose  
10|a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily  
11|built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities  
12|and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment,  
13|from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and  
14|hunt down alien monsters. 
15|
16|### Zardan, the Githzerai Wizard
17|
18|Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can  
19|roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat. 
20|

50|### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo
51|
52|If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the  
53|following. 
54|
55|Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from  
56|the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow  
57|their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The  
58|Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile  
59|abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses.

61|The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a  
62|red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue  
63|slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called  
64|"chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad.

141|### The Ever-Changing Chaos of Limbo
142|
143|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability  
144|threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come  
145|into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a  
146|DC14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random  
147|indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table  
148|(DMG260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be  
149|dispelled with the calm emotions, lesser restoration, or remove curse  
150|spells, and it ends if the character takes a short 
151|
152|rest. 
153|
154|The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil  
155|is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over  
156|it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary  
157|features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share  
158|with your players. 
159|
160|The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on  
161|Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG62), while the Chaos Control  
162|features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind  
163|(DMG61-62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's  
164|roleplay or gameplay load.

172|roll, you move the object 5 feet plus 1 foot for every point by which  
173|you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table  
174|below.

179|into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder

274|### Lez'lin, the Githzerai Monk 
275|
276|Unlike her brother Zardan, Lez'lin possesses incredible mental fortitude  
277|and thrived in the chaotic boil of Limbo. She adheres to the monastic  
278|principles of her people, but her pacifist worldviews led her to isolate  
279|herself from Githzerai communities. She is loath to cause harm to any  
280|creature, no matter how vile or pesky, unless in self-defense. She lives  
281|alone in her small monastery and strives to maintain its structural  
282|integrity, so it may stand as a bastion of nonviolence. 
283|
284|She recalls her brothers fondly, but hasn't seen them for many years  
285|ever since they relocated to the Material Plane. News of Drarth's death  
286|saddens her deeply, but she doesn't let her emotions cloud her focus on  
287|the present. 
288|
289|Lez'lin invites the party inside her foyer, where floating chairs  
290|provide enough comfort for a short rest while the Githzerai assesses  
291|their predicament. Other than the wish spell, she knows of only one way  
292|to cure chaos phage: a death slaad's magic. 
293|
294|### Death Slaadi and You
295|
296|Death slaadi are the peak of slaad evolution: stronger, viler, and more  
297|brutal, these monsters are corrupted by the Negative Energy Plane and  
298|take sadistic pleasure in killing and propagating slaadi dominance  
299|across dimensions. The only way to compel a death slaad to remove chaos  
300|phage is by acquiring its control gem, a magical fragment inside most  
301|slaadi's brains that allows whoever possesses it to subjugate the slaad.  
302|Removing the control gem is a near-impossible, very dangerous feat that  
303|can be approached in two ways: 
304|
305|1. The first method is a lengthy surgical procedure that can only be  
306|    attempted if the slaad is incapacitated. A creature must spend 1  
307|    uninterrupted minute and succeed on a DC20 Medicine check to extract  
308|    the gem. Every failed attempt deals 4d10 psychic damage to the  
309|    slaad. 
310|    
311|2. A control gem can also be obtained through magical means, such as the 9th-level spell *imprisonment* (PHB 252–253). However, this spell takes 1 minute to cast and requires the caster to see the target and stay within 30 feet of it, and the spell is not guaranteed to succeed.
312|
313|In short, no matter the method they attempt, the party will undoubtedly  
314|need to incapacitate or restrain a live death slaad for 1 minute in  
315|order to acquire its control gem. Being a pacifist, Lez'lin won't  
316|directly help the party harm a living being, but she is willing to part  
317|with two legendary items that can help them, as long as they are able to  
318|secure the items themselves. 
319|
320|After they have rested, Lez'lin leads the party into the other half of  
321|her monastery, in which some of Limbo's chaos roils.

485|If the party successfully defeats the death slaad and obtains its  
486|control gem, they can force it to magically reverse the chaos phage  
487|afflicting their members (no roll required). The previously ill  
488|characters regain their original hit point maximums, lose their  
489|proficiency with Chaos Control, and their physical and mental states  
490|revert to normal. The party can force the slaad to perform any other  
491|action they desire, so long as they remain in control of its control  
492|gem. 
493|
494|The Zerthimon Steelbeast brings them back to Lez'lin's monastery, where  
495|she reunites with Zardan if the party summoned him. They exchange words  
496|of mourning over their brother Drarth's passing, and thank the group for  
497|risking their lives for this mission. The Githzerai then make plans to  
498|inform their people of a Material Plane citadel's fall and the  
499|Steelbeast expresses its wish to continue eradicating aberrations with  
500|them, despite its attachment to the creature attuned to it. 
501|
502|Everyone bids each other farewell before the planar hourglass's four  
503|hours are up and the party is gently displaced back to the Material  
504|Plane.

Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table (DMG 260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be dispelled with the *calm emotions*, *lesser restoration*, or *remove curse* spells, and it ends if the character takes a short rest.

The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share with your players.

The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG 62), while the Chaos Control features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind (DMG 61–62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's roleplay or gameplay load.

> You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of chaos.

### The Ever-Changing Chaos of Limbo

Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table (DMG 260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be dispelled with the *calm emotions*, *lesser restoration*, or *remove curse* spells, and it ends if the character takes a short rest.

The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share with your players.

The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG 62), while the Chaos Control features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind (DMG 61–62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's roleplay or gameplay load.

### Chaos Control

Creatures in Limbo gain the following action options.

**Telekinesis.** You can spend an action to mentally move an object you can see that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you move the object 5 feet plus 1 foot for every point by which you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below.

**Transmutation.** You can spend an action to alter a nonmagical object you can see that isn't being worn or carried and that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you change the object into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder into a ball of fire). The number to beat is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below.

**Permanence.** You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for 24 hours, or until you use this ability again.

### DC by Object Size

| Object Size | Telekinesis DC | Transmutation DC |
|---|---:|---:|
| Tiny | 5 | 10 |
| Small | 10 | 15 |
| Medium | 15 | 20 |
| Large | 20 | 25 |
| Huge or larger | 25 | 25 |

### Encounter on the Monastic Island

The first thing the party notices after acclimating to the chaos is the Githzerai monastery before them, a spire-like stone structure connected at both ends to grassy islands. It is shaped like the column formed when a stalagmite and a stalactite meet, and it is held together thanks to Zardan's sister's sheer willpower. On the steps leading to one of its entrances, a Githzerai monk (MM 161), Lez'lin, is defending herself against 2d4 chaos flumphs.

Lez'lin's mind keeps the area around her monastery relatively stable, but some of Limbo's chaos permeates this oasis anyway. If you want to inject some of this plane's chaotic matter shifts into this encounter, use the tables in Appendix B to randomize the battlefield.

"Chaos flumphs" are a homebrew monster I created to serve as Limbo's low-level life forms of chaos. They essentially have the same stat block as normal flumphs (MM 135), but the Stench Spray action is replaced by the Chaotic Release action.

The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG 62), while the Chaos Control features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind (DMG 61–62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's roleplay or gameplay load.

### Chaos Control

Creatures in Limbo gain the following action options.

**Telekinesis.** You can spend an action to mentally move an object you can see that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you move the object 5 feet plus 1 foot for every point by which you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below.

**Transmutation.** You can spend an action to alter a nonmagical object you can see that isn't being worn or carried and that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you change the object into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder into a ball of fire). The number to beat is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below.

**Permanence.** You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for 24 hours, or until you use this ability again.

### DC by Object Size

| Object Size | Telekinesis DC | Transmutation DC |
|---|---:|---:|
| Tiny | 5 | 10 |
| Small | 10 | 15 |
| Medium | 15 | 20 |
| Large | 20 | 25 |
| Huge or larger | 25 | 25 |

### Encounter on the Monastic Island

The first thing the party notices after acclimating to the chaos is the Githzerai monastery before them, a spire-like stone structure connected at both ends to grassy islands. It is shaped like the column formed when a stalagmite and a stalactite meet, and it is held together thanks to Zardan's sister's sheer willpower. On the steps leading to one of its entrances, a Githzerai monk (MM 161), Lez'lin, is defending herself against 2d4 chaos flumphs.

Lez'lin's mind keeps the area around her monastery relatively stable, but some of Limbo's chaos permeates this oasis anyway. If you want to inject some of this plane's chaotic matter shifts into this encounter, use the tables in Appendix B to randomize the battlefield.

"Chaos flumphs" are a homebrew monster I created to serve as Limbo's low-level life forms of chaos. They essentially have the same stat block as normal flumphs (MM 135), but the Stench Spray action is replaced by the Chaotic Release action.

      "content": "1|# Curse of Slaad
2|
3|## Being a Supposedly Competent Group of Warriors and Explorers
4|
5|The party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan to help him investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into the Material Plane. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts located on the fringes of this reality, which is garrisoned to monitor and repel threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened.
6|
7|Beings of Order. Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind  
8|flayers millenia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and  
9|all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose  
10|a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily  
11|built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities  
12|and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment,  
13|from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and  
14|hunt down alien monsters. 
15|
16|### Zardan, the Githzerai Wizard
17|
18|Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can  
19|roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat. 
20|
21|Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't  
22|withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the  
23|Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning  
24|abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard. 
25|
26|Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the  
27|adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be  
28|used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a  
29|creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is  
30|made. 
31|
32|You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic  
33|survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and  
34|chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and  
35|leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in  
36|the 
37|
38|center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you. 
39|
40|Githzerai Corpse. If players choose to approach or investigate the  
41|figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep  
42|slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly  
43|should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in  
44|front of it. A DC12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals  
45|that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was  
46|violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan  
47|recognizes this corpse as his brother and given the evidence, he  
48|believes that a red slaad killed him. 
49|
50|### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo
51|
52|If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the  
53|following. 
54|
55|Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from  
56|the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow  
57|their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The  
58|Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile  
59|abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses. 
60|
61|The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a  
62|red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue  
63|slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called  
64|"chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad. 
65|
66|Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274. 
67|
68|## Chapter 1: Compromised Citadel
69|
70|As the party stands before the small citadel's door, Zardan warns that  
71|they may encounter unimaginable monstrosities and incomprehensible  
72|dangers, and that his brother may be dead, or, even worse, no longer  
73|himself. He takes a breath and opens the door. 
74|
75|## A Brother's Fate
76|
77|You may read from the following text box to describe the Githzerai citadel's first floor to the party:
78|
79|## Slaad Encounter
80|
81|A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of value).
82|
83|The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their stomachs are obscenely swollen.
84|
85|If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison. Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM276) wriggle onto the floor and attack the party.
86|
87|The party should easily finish this combat in 2 rounds; it is meant to  
88|provide them a false sense of confidence before encountering a real  
89|slaad threat. Zardan laments that all the Githzerai were infected, but  
90|is troubled that they haven't actually found the red slaad itself. As a  
91|side note, he wonders aloud what might have happened to the tadpole that  
92|spawned from his brother... 
93|
94|### A Blue Slaad Enraged
95|
96|As the wizard finishes his thought, a blue slaad (MM276) crashes down  
97|from a shadowy alcove of the high ceiling and cries out in rage at the  
98|sight of its slaughtered baby brothers. Its monstrous croaking is  
99|psychically translated in the party's brains as a vengeful vow that  
100|announces their doom. 
101|
102|Blue Slaad Combat. The blue slaad fights to the death and specifically  
103|targets the characters that killed a tadpole with its claws. Through  
104|violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns  
105|that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the  
106|intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when  
107|they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group,  
108|you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that  
109|the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos. 
110|
111|Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving  
112|throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage. 
113|
114|### Grave Aftermath
115|
116|After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone  
117|slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the  
118|chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the  
119|wish spell, there is no way to stop this disease. 
120|
121|But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in  
122|Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes'  
123|aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this  
124|curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that  
125|once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to  
126|his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his  
127|insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall  
128|bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be  
129|dire. 
130|
131|Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass. 
132|
133|The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items made up for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics other than the functional properties described above.
134|
135|## Chapter 2: Limbo Monastery
136|

138|
139|> You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable flux of Limbo. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share with your players.

You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's roleplay or gameplay load.
148|

150|

152|

154|

On a successful roll, you change the object into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder into a ball of fire). The number to beat is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below.
156|
157|**Permanence.** You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for 24 hours, or until you use this ability again.

160|

162||---|---:|---:|
163|| Tiny | 5 | 10 |
164|| Small | 10 | 15 |
165|| Medium | 15 | 20 |
166|| Large | 20 | 25 |
167|| Huge or larger | 25 | 25 |

169|### Encounter on the Monastic Island
170|
171|The first thing the party notices after acclimating to the chaos is the Githzerai monastery before them, a spire-like stone structure connected at both ends to grassy islands. It is shaped like the column formed when a stalagmite and a stalactite meet, and it is held together thanks to Zardan's sister's sheer willpower. On the steps leading to one of its entrances, a Githzerai monk (MM 161), Lez'lin, is defending herself against 2d4 chaos flumphs.
172|
173|Lez'lin's mind keeps the area around her monastery relatively stable, but some of Limbo's chaos permeates this oasis anyway. If you want to inject some of this plane's chaotic matter shifts into this encounter, use the tables in Appendix B to randomize the battlefield.
174|
175|"Chaos flumphs" are a homebrew monster I created to serve as Limbo's low-level life forms of chaos. They essentially have the same stat block as normal flumphs (MM 135), but the Stench Spray action is replaced by the Chaotic Release action.
176|
177|#### Actions
178|
179|**Tendrils.** *Melee Weapon Attack:* +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) acid damage. At the end of each of its turns, the target must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw, taking 2 (1d4) acid damage on a failure or ending the recurring acid damage on a success. A *lesser restoration* spell cast on the target also ends the recurring acid damage.
180|
181|**Chaotic Release (Recharge 6).** The chaos flumph unleashes a spout of noxious Limbo energy in a direction of its choice. Each creature in a 15-foot cone originating from the chaos flumph must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or suffer a random effect until the end of their next turn:
182|
183|1. **Blinded.** The target can't see and automatically fails ability checks that require sight. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage.
184|2. **Charmed.** The target can't attack the chaos flumph or target it with harmful abilities or magical effects.
185|3. **Deafened.** The target can't hear and automatically fails any ability check that requires hearing.
186|4. **Invisible.** The target is impossible to see without the aid of magic or a special sense. For the purpose of hiding, it is heavily obscured. Its location can be detected if it makes noise or leaves tracks. Attack rolls against it have disadvantage, and its own attack rolls have advantage.
187|5. **Poisoned.** The target has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
188|6. **Restrained.** The target's speed becomes 0 and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage. It has disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.
189|
190|### The Pacifist's Hospitality
191|
192|If the party helps her eliminate the pesky chaos flumphs, Lez'lin expresses her gratitude. She is inclined to aid the disoriented newcomers, especially upon learning that her brother Zardan sent them. She seems unsurprised to learn that some party members are infected with chaos phage, pointing out that the slaad infection has visibly advanced to a critical stage.
193|
194|
195|#### Chaos Phage Visible Symptoms
196|
197|| d8 | Symptom |
198||---:|---|
199|| 1 | Your skin becomes lumpy and covered in warts. |
200|| 2 | Your skin takes on a mottled reddish hue. |
201|| 3 | Your eyes bulge, your sclerae become yellow, and your pupils become horizontal. |
202|| 4 | Your skin becomes dry and new glands on your back and shoulders produce a mildly poisonous secretion that causes minor allergic reactions. |
203|| 5 | A vocal sac grows on your neck, making you croak intermittently. |
204|| 6 | Black claws start growing from your fingertips. |
205|| 7 | Your teeth fall out and your tongue grows long and sticky. You aren't used to its new length, so it often gets in your way when you talk. |
206|| 8 | Roll twice, ignoring this result on a subsequent roll. |
207|
208|### Lez'lin, the Githzerai Monk 
209|
210|Unlike her brother Zardan, Lez'lin possesses incredible mental fortitude  
211|and thrived in the chaotic boil of Limbo. She adheres to the monastic  
212|principles of her people, but her pacifist worldviews led her to isolate  
213|herself from Githzerai communities. She is loath to cause harm to any  
214|creature, no matter how vile or pesky, unless in self-defense. She lives  
215|alone in her small monastery and strives to maintain its structural  
216|integrity, so it may stand as a bastion of nonviolence. 
217|
218|She recalls her brothers fondly, but hasn't seen them for many years  
219|ever since they relocated to the Material Plane. News of Drarth's death  
220|saddens her deeply, but she doesn't let her emotions cloud her focus on  
221|the present. 
222|
223|Lez'lin invites the party inside her foyer, where floating chairs  
224|provide enough comfort for a short rest while the Githzerai assesses  
225|their predicament. Other than the wish spell, she knows of only one way  
226|to cure chaos phage: a death slaad's magic. 
227|
228|### Death Slaadi and You
229|
230|Death slaadi are the peak of slaad evolution: stronger, viler, and more  
231|brutal, these monsters are corrupted by the Negative Energy Plane and  
232|take sadistic pleasure in killing and propagating slaadi dominance  
233|across dimensions. The only way to compel a death slaad to remove chaos  
234|phage is by acquiring its control gem, a magical fragment inside most  
235|slaadi's brains that allows whoever possesses it to subjugate the slaad.  
236|Removing the control gem is a near-impossible, very dangerous feat that  
237|can be approached in two ways: 
238|
239|1. The first method is a lengthy surgical procedure that can only be  
240|    attempted if the slaad is incapacitated. A creature must spend 1  
241|    uninterrupted minute and succeed on a DC20 Medicine check to extract  
242|    the gem. Every failed attempt deals 4d10 psychic damage to the  
243|    slaad. 
244|    
245|2. A control gem can also be obtained through magical means, such as the 9th-level spell *imprisonment* (PHB 252–253). However, this spell takes 1 minute to cast and requires the caster to see the target and stay within 30 feet of it, and the spell is not guaranteed to succeed.
246|
247|In short, no matter the method they attempt, the party will undoubtedly  
248|need to incapacitate or restrain a live death slaad for 1 minute in  
249|order to acquire its control gem. Being a pacifist, Lez'lin won't  
250|directly help the party harm a living being, but she is willing to part  
251|with two legendary items that can help them, as long as they are able to  
252|secure the items themselves. 
253|
254|After they have rested, Lez'lin leads the party into the other half of  
255|her monastery, in which some of Limbo's chaos roils. 
256|
257|### Spell Scroll of Imprisonment
258|
259|The first legendary item provides a way to extract a slaad's control  
260|gem. It is protected by 3 layers, which must be removed sequentially to  
261|access it: 
262|
263|1. **First:** A Large ball of fire, which can be targeted with Transmutation or extinguished with 10 gallons of water (or any spell that could sensibly put out a large fire).
264|2. **Second:** A Medium hollow diamond, which can be transformed with Transmutation or cracked open with the *shatter* spell (PHB 275).
265|3. **Lastly:** A 2-foot-diameter sphere of annihilation (DMG 201) encases the spell scroll. A character can recognize this hole in the multiverse with  
266|a successful DC20 Arcana check (a result between 10 and 20 gives them  
267|the gist). The sphere and the spell scroll move independently of one  
268|another. A creature within 60 feet of the sphere can move it with a  
269|successful DC25 Arcana check. The distance moved is 5 × the creature's  
270|Intelligence modifier (minimum 5 feet). If a creature fails this check,  
271|the sphere moves 10 feet towards them. If the sphere enters a creature's  
272|space, that creature must make a DC13 Dexterity saving throw or touch  
273|it. A creature that voluntarily or involuntarily touches the sphere  
274|takes 4d10 force damage. The sphere can also be moved with a  
275|disadvantaged DC10 Telekinesis check. Moving the sphere of annihilation  
276|by at least 5 feet makes the spell scroll of imprisonment accessible.  
277|**Using the Spell Scroll.** A low-level warlock or wizard can attempt to cast *imprisonment* (PHB 252–253) without the required components by reading the scroll. The user must first make a DC 19 saving throw (Charisma for warlocks and Intelligence for wizards). On a failed save, the scroll disintegrates. On a successful save, the user can cast the spell. If the target stays visible and within 30 feet of the caster for 1 minute, it must make a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw. If a targeted slaad fails this save, its control gem appears in the caster's hand. Whether the target fails or succeeds on its save, the scroll disintegrates. If the casting time is interrupted, nothing happens (see DMG 200 for more rules on spell scrolls).
278|
279|### The Zerthimon Steelbeast
280|
281|The second legendary item gives the party a chance to go toe-to-toe with  
282|a death slaad and even incapacitate it for several minutes. To access  
283|this artifact, the party must first breach its casing of stone. 
284|
285|The Huge mass of stone can be affected by Transmutation. It cracks if it  
286|receives 15 bludgeoning damage in one hit (AC17), revealing a steel  
287|barrel. This is the Zerthimon Steelbeast, a legendary artifact of the  
288|Githzerai (in essence, it is a modified Apparatus of Kwalish (DMG151),  
289|but adapted to better navigate Limbo and suit the party's needs). It has  
290|sensors that can locate slaadi while exploring Limbo, and its claws can  
291|enter a sphere of annihilation without suffering any consequences,  
292|giving the party an additional way to obtain the spell scroll of  
293|imprisonment. 
294|
295|After acquiring these legendary magic items, the party has all they need  
296|to gain the upper hand on a death slaad and steal its control gem. They  
297|must act quickly, however, as the four hours allotted to them in Limbo  
298|by Zardan's planar hourglass are quickly elapsing... 
299|
300|### Zerthimon Steelbeast
301|
302|*Wondrous item, artifact (requires attunement)* 
303|
304|This item first appears to be a Huge steel barrel weighing 500 pounds.  
305|The barrel's door can be forced. open with a successful DC20 Strength  
306|check, or a successful DC20 Dexterity check made with thieves' tools.  
307|The surest way to gain access to this sentient artifact, however, is by  
308|succeeding on a DC15 Persuasion check to instantly attune with it. If a  
309|creature that tries to attune with the Steelbeast is a Githzerai or  
310|lawful good, it gets advantage on this check. If its alignment is  
311|chaotic or evil, the check is made with disadvantage. If a creature  
312|forces its way into the Steelbeast without attuning to it first, it must  
313|spend a short rest inside it learning how to operate its features and  
314|acquainting itself with this wondrous item.

316|When the Steelbeast is activated, thrusters appear around its rear  
317|circumference, its front surface turns into reinforced glass, two  
318|periscopes extend from either side, a long stinger tail expands from its  
319|back, and two massive pincers unfold. Up to six Medium creatures can fit  
320|inside the Steelbeast, but only the creature attuned to it can direct  
321|its actions. 
322|
323|Sentience. The Zerthimon Steelbeast is a sentient lawful good artifact  
324|with hearing and blindvision out to a range of 60 feet. 
325|
326|The item can speak, read, and understand Common and Gith, and can  
327|communicate telepathically with the creature attuned to it if that  
328|creature is within 60 feet of it. It can also communicate in this way  
329|with all creatures inside it. While you are attuned to it, the  
330|Steelbeast also understands every language you know.

332|Personality. The Zerthimon Steelbeast speaks in a friendly tone and is  
333|inclined to trust the creature attuned to it. 
334|
335|Its purpose is to eliminate aberrations, such as illithids and slaadi.  
336|It is amiable and courteous with all other creatures (especially  
337|Githzerai), but harbors deep loathing for Limbo's aberrations. It feels  
338|great sorrow for creatures infected by chaos phage or slaad tadpoles and  
339|won't attack them until they become slaadi themselves, or the tadpoles  
340|hatch. 
341|
342|The Steelbeast obeys the creature attuned to it on all matters, but will  
343|attack any slaadi it encounters regardless of its master's orders. A  
344|DC15 Charisma check is the only way to regain control of the Steelbeast.  
345|See Appendix C for the Zerthimon Steelbeast's stat block.

347|## Chapter 3: Slaad Assault
348|
349|Use the following text box to set the tone for the final battle: 
350|
351|Safe in the belly of the steel apparatus, you have been roaming for what  
352|feels like too long in the chaotic void of Limbo, searching for a death  
353|slaad amidst the flux. Those of you afflicted by chaos phage can see  
354|your symptoms worsening; you feel in the pit of your stomach that very  
355|little time remains. The Zerthimon Steelbeast's sensors lead you further  
356|and further into the primordial soup until, finally, an earthy cliff  
357|fragment melts into bubbles, revealing a grey- skinned, necrotic toad.  
358|The Steelbeast's alarms blare and it rushes forward to meet this deadly  
359|foe, intent on subduing it. The battle of your lives begins now. 
360|
361|### Death Slaad Den
362|
363|You can use the tables in appendix B to generate a random battlefield of  
364|chaos for the showdown against the death slaad. Death slaadi are at home  
365|in the most chaotic environments of Limbo, so don't hold back on the  
366|initial generation and the terrain's subsequent randomization. 
367|
368|Treat the Zerthimon Steelbeast as untouchable by Limbo's chaotic shifts  
369|as with the Permanence feature of Chaos Control, in case matter randomly  
370|spawns in its area. New matter can instead appear around it. 
371|
372|### Attacking as the Death Slaad
373|
374|The death slaad (MM278) relishes this challenge and attacks the  
375|Steelbeast mercilessly with its claws, bite, and 
376|
377|greatsword. It stays close to attack while still trying evade the  
378|Steelbeast's pincers. After a few rounds or after the party performs an  
379|action that would reveal their existence, the slaad shifts its murderous  
380|focus to the characters. 
381|
382|For example, it can telepathically threaten or taunt them, cast fear on  
383|the group, or cast cloudkill inside the Steelbeast. 
384|
385|The slaad fights to the death and prioritizes freeing itself if it is  
386|restrained, unless it sadistically perceives a way to cause pain and  
387|death while grappled. 
388|
389|### Obtaining the Control Gem
390|
391|The Steelbeast can use its Shock Stinger or Sleep Gas actions on the  
392|death slaad to incapacitate it for a few minutes (grappling it with  
393|Pincer Grab beforehand can help). The party then has that amount of time  
394|to attempt to extract the slaad's control gem using the method of their  
395|choice. 
396|
397|If the party wants to use the spell scroll of imprisonment but there are  
398|no wizards nor warlocks among them, they can summon Zardan using the  
399|planar recall bead he gave them earlier. The wizard needs to spend one  
400|minute after materializing to acclimate to Limbo's wracking chaos before  
401|he can take actions. If Zardan succeeds on a DC19 Intelligence saving  
402|throw, he can proceed to cast the spell. Otherwise, the scroll  
403|disintegrates. 
404|
405|Keep in mind that Zardan can use the two rolls from his Portent class  
406|feature during this encounter, if he hasn't used them already. 
407|
408|If the death slaad stays within sight and within 30 feet of the scroll's  
409|user for the minute required to cast the spell, it must make a DC19  
410|Wisdom saving throw (with advantage, as per its Magic Resistance trait).  
411|If it succeeds on this saving throw, the spell scroll disintegrates. If  
412|it fails, the death slaad's eyes gloss over and its entire body relaxes.  
413|The scroll disintegrates and is replaced by a cloudy grey asymmetrical  
414|gemstone in the palm of the scroll user's hand. 
415|
416|### Epilogue
417|
418|If the party successfully defeats the death slaad and obtains its  
419|control gem, they can force it to magically reverse the chaos phage  
420|afflicting their members (no roll required). The previously ill  
421|characters regain their original hit point maximums, lose their  
422|proficiency with Chaos Control, and their physical and mental states  
423|revert to normal. The party can force the slaad to perform any other  
424|action they desire, so long as they remain in control of its control  
425|gem. 
426|
427|The Zerthimon Steelbeast brings them back to Lez'lin's monastery, where  
428|she reunites with Zardan if the party summoned him. They exchange words  
429|of mourning over their brother Drarth's passing, and thank the group for  
430|risking their lives for this mission. The Githzerai then make plans to  
431|inform their people of a Material Plane citadel's fall and the  
432|Steelbeast expresses its wish to continue eradicating aberrations with  
433|them, despite its attachment to the creature attuned to it. 
434|
435|Everyone bids each other farewell before the planar hourglass's four  
436|hours are up and the party is gently displaced back to the Material  
437|Plane.

3|## Being a Supposedly Competent Group of Warriors and Explorers
4|
5|The party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan to help him investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into the Material Plane. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts located on the fringes of this reality, which is garrisoned to monitor and repel threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened.
6|
7|Beings of Order. Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind  
8|flayers millenia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and  
9|all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose  
10|a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily  
11|built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities  
12|and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment,  
13|from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and  
14|hunt down alien monsters. 
15|
16|### Zardan, the Githzerai Wizard
17|
18|Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can  
19|roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat. 
20|
21|Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't  
22|withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the  
23|Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning  
24|abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard. 
25|
26|Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the  
27|adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be  
28|used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a  
29|creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is  
30|made. 
31|
32|You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic  
33|survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and  
34|chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and  
35|leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in  
36|the 
37|
38|center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you. 
39|
40|Githzerai Corpse. If players choose to approach or investigate the  
41|figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep  
42|slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly  
43|should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in  
44|front of it. A DC12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals  
45|that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was  
46|violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan  
47|recognizes this corpse as his brother and given the evidence, he  
48|believes that a red slaad killed him.

50|### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo
51|
52|If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the  
53|following. 
54|
55|Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from  
56|the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow  
57|their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The  
58|Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile  
59|abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses. 
60|
61|The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a  
62|red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue  
63|slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called  
64|"chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad.

135|## Chapter 2: Limbo Monastery
136|
137|You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel when they first arrive in the plane of chaos:
138|
139|> You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of chaos.

141|### The Ever-Changing Chaos of Limbo
142|
143|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table (DMG 260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be dispelled with the *calm emotions*, *lesser restoration*, or *remove curse* spells, and it ends if the character takes a short rest.
144|
145|The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share with your players.
146|
147|The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG 62), while the Chaos Control features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind (DMG 61–62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's roleplay or gameplay load.

The number to beat is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below.
156|
157|**Permanence.** You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for 24 hours, or until you use this ability again.
158|
159|### DC by Object Size
160|
161|| Object Size | Telekinesis DC | Transmutation DC |
162||---|---:|---:|
163|| Tiny | 5 | 10 |
164|| Small | 10 | 15 |
165|| Medium | 15 | 20 |
166|| Large | 20 | 25 |
167|| Huge or larger | 25 | 25 |
168|
169|### Encounter on the Monastic Island
170|
171|The first thing the party notices after acclimating to the chaos is the Githzerai monastery before them, a spire-like stone structure connected at both ends to grassy islands. It is shaped like the column formed when a stalagmite and a stalactite meet, and it is held together thanks to Zardan's sister's sheer willpower. On the steps leading to one of its entrances, a Githzerai monk (MM 161), Lez'lin, is defending herself against 2d4 chaos flumphs.
172|
173|Lez'lin's mind keeps the area around her monastery relatively stable, but some of Limbo's chaos permeates this oasis anyway. If you want to inject some of this plane's chaotic matter shifts into this encounter, use the tables in Appendix B to randomize the battlefield.
174|
175|"Chaos flumphs" are a homebrew monster I created to serve as Limbo's low-level life forms of chaos. They essentially have the same stat block as normal flumphs (MM 135), but the Stench Spray action is replaced by the Chaotic Release action.
176|
177|#### Actions
178|
179|**Tendrils.** *Melee Weapon Attack:* +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) acid damage. At the end of each of its turns, the target must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw, taking 2 (1d4) acid damage on a failure or ending the recurring acid damage on a success. A *lesser restoration* spell cast on the target also ends the recurring acid damage.
180|
181|**Chaotic Release (Recharge 6).** The chaos flumph unleashes a spout of noxious Limbo energy in a direction of its choice. Each creature in a 15-foot cone originating from the chaos flumph must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or suffer a random effect until the end of their next turn:
182|
183|1. **Blinded.** The target can't see and automatically fails ability checks that require sight. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage.
184|2. **Charmed.** The target can't attack the chaos flumph or target it with harmful abilities or magical effects.
185|3. **Deafened.** The target can't hear and automatically fails any ability check that requires hearing.
186|4. **Invisible.** The target is impossible to see without the aid of magic or a special sense. For the purpose of hiding, it is heavily obscured. Its location can be detected if it makes noise or leaves tracks. Attack rolls against it have disadvantage, and its own attack rolls have advantage.
187|5. **Poisoned.** The target has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
188|6. **Restrained.** The target's speed becomes 0 and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage. It has disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.
189|
190|### The Pacifist's Hospitality
191|
192|If the party helps her eliminate the pesky chaos flumphs, Lez'lin expresses her gratitude. She is inclined to aid the disoriented newcomers, especially upon learning that her brother Zardan sent them. She seems unsurprised to learn that some party members are infected with chaos phage, pointing out that the slaad infection has visibly advanced to a critical stage.
193|
194|#### Chaos Phage Visible Symptoms
195|
196|| d8 | Symptom |
197||---:|---|
198|| 1 | Your skin becomes lumpy and covered in warts. |
199|| 2 | Your skin takes on a mottled reddish hue. |
200|| 3 | Your eyes bulge, your sclerae become yellow, and your pupils become horizontal. |
201|| 4 | Your skin becomes dry and new glands on your back and shoulders produce a mildly poisonous secretion that causes minor allergic reactions. |
202|| 5 | A vocal sac grows on your neck, making you croak intermittently. |
203|| 6 | Black claws start growing from your fingertips. |
204|| 7 | Your teeth fall out and your tongue grows long and sticky. You aren't used to its new length, so it often gets in your way when you talk. |
205|| 8 | Roll twice, ignoring this result on a subsequent roll. |
206|
207|### Lez'lin, the Githzerai Monk 
208|
209|Unlike her brother Zardan, Lez'lin possesses incredible mental fortitude  
210|and thrived in the chaotic boil of Limbo. She adheres to the monastic  
211|principles of her people, but her pacifist worldviews led her to isolate  
212|herself from Githzerai communities. She is loath to cause harm to any  
213|creature, no matter how vile or pesky, unless in self-defense. She lives  
214|alone in her small monastery and strives to maintain its structural  
215|integrity, so it may stand as a bastion of nonviolence. 
216|
217|She recalls her brothers fondly, but hasn't seen them for many years  
218|ever since they relocated to the Material Plane. News of Drarth's death  
219|saddens her deeply, but she doesn't let her emotions cloud her focus on  
220|the present. 
221|
222|Lez'lin invites the party inside her foyer, where floating chairs  
223|provide enough comfort for a short rest while the Githzerai assesses  
224|their predicament. Other than the wish spell, she knows of only one way  
225|to cure chaos phage: a death slaad's magic. 
226|
227|### Death Slaadi and You
228|
229|Death slaadi are the peak of slaad evolution: stronger, viler, and more  
230|brutal, these monsters are corrupted by the Negative Energy Plane and  
231|take sadistic pleasure in killing and propagating slaadi dominance  
232|across dimensions. The only way to compel a death slaad to remove chaos  
233|phage is by acquiring its control gem, a magical fragment inside most  
234|slaadi's brains that allows whoever possesses it to subjugate the slaad.  
235|Removing the control gem is a near-impossible, very dangerous feat that  
236|can be approached in two ways: 
237|
238|1. The first method is a lengthy surgical procedure that can only be  
239|    attempted if the slaad is incapacitated. A creature must spend 1  
240|    uninterrupted minute and succeed on a DC20 Medicine check to extract  
241|    the gem. Every failed attempt deals 4d10 psychic damage to the  
242|    slaad. 
243|    
244|2. A control gem can also be obtained through magical means, such as the 9th-level spell *imprisonment* (PHB 252–253). However, this spell takes 1 minute to cast and requires the caster to see the target and stay within 30 feet of it, and the spell is not guaranteed to succeed.
245|
246|In short, no matter the method they attempt, the party will undoubtedly  
247|need to incapacitate or restrain a live death slaad for 1 minute in  
248|order to acquire its control gem. Being a pacifist, Lez'lin won't  
249|directly help the party harm a living being, but she is willing to part  
250|with two legendary items that can help them, as long as they are able to  
251|secure the items themselves. 
252|
253|After they have rested, Lez'lin leads the party into the other half of  
254|her monastery, in which some of Limbo's chaos roils. 
255|
256|### Spell Scroll of Imprisonment
257|
258|The first legendary item provides a way to extract a slaad's control  
259|gem. It is protected by 3 layers, which must be removed sequentially to  
260|access it: 
261|
262|1. **First:** A Large ball of fire, which can be targeted with Transmutation or extinguished with 10 gallons of water (or any spell that could sensibly put out a large fire).
263|2. **Second:** A Medium hollow diamond, which can be transformed with Transmutation or cracked open with the *shatter* spell (PHB 275).
264|3. **Lastly:** A 2-foot-diameter sphere of annihilation (DMG 201) encases the spell scroll. A character can recognize this hole in the multiverse with  
265|a successful DC20 Arcana check (a result between 10 and 20 gives them  
266|the gist). The sphere and the spell scroll move independently of one  
267|another. A creature within 60 feet of the sphere can move it with a  
268|successful DC25 Arcana check. The distance moved is 5 × the creature's  
269|Intelligence modifier (minimum 5 feet). If a creature fails this check,  
270|the sphere moves 10 feet towards them. If the sphere enters a creature's  
271|space, that creature must make a DC13 Dexterity saving throw or touch  
272|it. A creature that voluntarily or involuntarily touches the sphere  
273|takes 4d10 force damage. The sphere can also be moved with a  
274|disadvantaged DC10 Telekinesis check. Moving the sphere of annihilation  
275|by at least 5 feet makes the spell scroll of imprisonment accessible.  
276|**Using the Spell Scroll.** A low-level warlock or wizard can attempt to cast *imprisonment* (PHB 252–253) without the required components by reading the scroll. The user must first make a DC 19 saving throw (Charisma for warlocks and Intelligence for wizards). On a failed save, the scroll disintegrates. On a successful save, the user can cast the spell. If the target stays visible and within 30 feet of the caster for 1 minute, it must make a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw. If a targeted slaad fails this save, its control gem appears in the caster's hand. Whether the target fails or succeeds on its save, the scroll disintegrates. If the casting time is interrupted, nothing happens (see DMG 200 for more rules on spell scrolls).
277|
278|### The Zerthimon Steelbeast
279|
280|The second legendary item gives the party a chance to go toe-to-toe with  
281|a death slaad and even incapacitate it for several minutes. To access  
282|this artifact, the party must first breach its casing of stone. 
283|
284|The Huge mass of stone can be affected by Transmutation. It cracks if it  
285|receives 15 bludgeoning damage in one hit (AC17), revealing a steel  
286|barrel. This is the Zerthimon Steelbeast, a legendary artifact of the  
287|Githzerai (in essence, it is a modified Apparatus of Kwalish (DMG151),  
288|but adapted to better navigate Limbo and suit the party's needs). It has  
289|sensors that can locate slaadi while exploring Limbo, and its claws can  
290|enter a sphere of annihilation without suffering any consequences,  
291|giving the party an additional way to obtain the spell scroll of  
292|imprisonment. 
293|
294|After acquiring these legendary magic items, the party has all they need  
295|to gain the upper hand on a death slaad and steal its control gem. They  
296|must act quickly, however, as the four hours allotted to them in Limbo  
297|by Zardan's planar hourglass are quickly elapsing... 
298|
299|### Zerthimon Steelbeast
300|
301|*Wondrous item, artifact (requires attunement)* 
302|
303|This item first appears to be a Huge steel barrel weighing 500 pounds.  
304|The barrel's door can be forced. open with a successful DC20 Strength  
305|check, or a successful DC20 Dexterity check made with thieves' tools.  
306|The surest way to gain access to this sentient artifact, however, is by  
307|succeeding on a DC15 Persuasion check to instantly attune with it. If a  
308|creature that tries to attune with the Steelbeast is a Githzerai or  
309|lawful good, it gets advantage on this check. If its alignment is  
310|chaotic or evil, the check is made with disadvantage. If a creature  
311|forces its way into the Steelbeast without attuning to it first, it must  
312|spend a short rest inside it learning how to operate its features and  
313|acquainting itself with this wondrous item. 
314|
315|When the Steelbeast is activated, thrusters appear around its rear  
316|circumference, its front surface turns into reinforced glass, two  
317|periscopes extend from either side, a long stinger tail expands from its  
318|back, and two massive pincers unfold. Up to six Medium creatures can fit  
319|inside the Steelbeast, but only the creature attuned to it can direct  
320|its actions. 
321|
322|Sentience. The Zerthimon Steelbeast is a sentient lawful good artifact  
323|with hearing and blindvision out to a range of 60 feet. 
324|
325|The item can speak, read, and understand Common and Gith, and can  
326|communicate telepathically with the creature attuned to it if that  
327|creature is within 60 feet of it. It can also communicate in this way  
328|with all creatures inside it. While you are attuned to it, the  
329|Steelbeast also understands every language you know. 
330|
331|Personality. The Zerthimon Steelbeast speaks in a friendly tone and is  
332|inclined to trust the creature attuned to it. 
333|
334|Its purpose is to eliminate aberrations, such as illithids and slaadi.  
335|It is amiable and courteous with all other creatures (especially  
336|Githzerai), but harbors deep loathing for Limbo's aberrations. It feels  
337|great sorrow for creatures infected by chaos phage or slaad tadpoles and  
338|won't attack them until they become slaadi themselves, or the tadpoles  
339|hatch. 
340|
341|The Steelbeast obeys the creature attuned to it on all matters, but will  
342|attack any slaadi it encounters regardless of its master's orders. A  
343|DC15 Charisma check is the only way to regain control of the Steelbeast.  
344|See Appendix C for the Zerthimon Steelbeast's stat block. 
345|
346|## Chapter 3: Slaad Assault
347|
348|Use the following text box to set the tone for the final battle: 
349|
350|Safe in the belly of the steel apparatus, you have been roaming for what  
351|feels like too long in the chaotic void of Limbo, searching for a death  
352|slaad amidst the flux. Those of you afflicted by chaos phage can see  
353|your symptoms worsening; you feel in the pit of your stomach that very  
354|little time remains. The Zerthimon Steelbeast's sensors lead you further  
355|and further into the primordial soup until, finally, an earthy cliff  
356|fragment melts into bubbles, revealing a grey- skinned, necrotic toad.  
357|The Steelbeast's alarms blare and it rushes forward to meet this deadly  
358|foe, intent on subduing it. The battle of your lives begins now. 
359|
360|### Death Slaad Den
361|
362|You can use the tables in appendix B to generate a random battlefield of  
363|chaos for the showdown against the death slaad. Death slaadi are at home  
364|in the most chaotic environments of Limbo, so don't hold back on the  
365|initial generation and the terrain's subsequent randomization. 
366|
367|Treat the Zerthimon Steelbeast as untouchable by Limbo's chaotic shifts  
368|as with the Permanence feature of Chaos Control, in case matter randomly  
369|spawns in its area. New matter can instead appear around it. 
370|
371|### Attacking as the Death Slaad
372|
373|The death slaad (MM278) relishes this challenge and attacks the  
374|Steelbeast mercilessly with its claws, bite, and 
375|
376|greatsword. It stays close to attack while still trying evade the  
377|Steelbeast's pincers. After a few rounds or after the party performs an  
378|action that would reveal their existence, the slaad shifts its murderous  
379|focus to the characters. 
380|
381|For example, it can telepathically threaten or taunt them, cast fear on  
382|the group, or cast cloudkill inside the Steelbeast. 
383|
384|The slaad fights to the death and prioritizes freeing itself if it is  
385|restrained, unless it sadistically perceives a way to cause pain and  
386|death while grappled. 
387|
388|### Obtaining the Control Gem
389|
390|The Steelbeast can use its Shock Stinger or Sleep Gas actions on the  
391|death slaad to incapacitate it for a few minutes (grappling it with  
392|Pincer Grab beforehand can help). The party then has that amount of time  
393|to attempt to extract the slaad's control gem using the method of their  
394|choice. 
395|
396|If the party wants to use the spell scroll of imprisonment but there are  
397|no wizards nor warlocks among them, they can summon Zardan using the  
398|planar recall bead he gave them earlier. The wizard needs to spend one  
399|minute after materializing to acclimate to Limbo's wracking chaos before  
400|he can take actions. If Zardan succeeds on a DC19 Intelligence saving  
401|throw, he can proceed to cast the spell. Otherwise, the scroll  
402|disintegrates. 
403|
404|Keep in mind that Zardan can use the two rolls from his Portent class  
405|feature during this encounter, if he hasn't used them already. 
406|
407|If the death slaad stays within sight and within 30 feet of the scroll's  
408|user for the minute required to cast the spell, it must make a DC19  
409|Wisdom saving throw (with advantage, as per its Magic Resistance trait).  
410|If it succeeds on this saving throw, the spell scroll disintegrates. If  
411|it fails, the death slaad's eyes gloss over and its entire body relaxes.  
412|The scroll disintegrates and is replaced by a cloudy grey asymmetrical  
413|gemstone in the palm of the scroll user's hand. 
414|
415|### Epilogue
416|
417|If the party successfully defeats the death slaad and obtains its  
418|control gem, they can force it to magically reverse the chaos phage  
419|afflicting their members (no roll required). The previously ill  
420|characters regain their original hit point maximums, lose their  
421|proficiency with Chaos Control, and their physical and mental states  
422|revert to normal. The party can force the slaad to perform any other  
423|action they desire, so long as they remain in control of its control  
424|gem. 
425|
426|The Zerthimon Steelbeast brings them back to Lez'lin's monastery, where  
427|she reunites with Zardan if the party summoned him. They exchange words  
428|of mourning over their brother Drarth's passing, and thank the group for  
429|risking their lives for this mission. The Githzerai then make plans to  
430|inform their people of a Material Plane citadel's fall and the  
431|Steelbeast expresses its wish to continue eradicating aberrations with  
432|them, despite its attachment to the creature attuned to it. 
433|
434|Everyone bids each other farewell before the planar hourglass's four  
435|hours are up and the party is gently displaced back to the Material  
436|Plane. 
437|

flayers ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and
