      "hasMoreBelow": true,
      "nextStartLine": 141,
      "content": "1|# Curse of Slaad
2|
3|## Being a Supposedly Competent Group of Warriors and Explorers
4|
5|The party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan to help him investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into the Material Plane. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts located on the fringes of this reality, which is garrisoned to monitor and repel threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened.
6|
7|Beings of Order. Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind flayers millenia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment, from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and hunt down alien monsters.
8|
9|### Zardan, the Githzerai Wizard
10|
11|Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can  
12|roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat. 
13|
14|Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't  
15|withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the  
16|Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning  
17|abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard. 
18|
19|Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the  
20|adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be  
21|used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a  
22|creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is  
23|made. 
24|
25|You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic  
26|survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and  
27|chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and  
28|leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in  
29|the 
30|
31|center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you. 
32|
33|Githzerai Corpse. If players choose to approach or investigate the  
34|figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep  
35|slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly  
36|should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in  
37|front of it. A DC12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals  
38|that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was  
39|violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan  
40|recognizes this corpse as his brother and given the evidence, he  
41|believes that a red slaad killed him. 
42|
43|### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo
44|
45|If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the  
46|following. 
47|
48|Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from  
49|the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow  
50|their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The  
51|Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile  
52|abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses. 
53|
54|The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a  
55|red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue  
56|slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called  
57|"chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad. 
58|
59|Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274. 
60|
61|## Chapter 1: Compromised Citadel
62|
63|As the party stands before the small citadel's door, Zardan warns that  
64|they may encounter unimaginable monstrosities and incomprehensible  
65|dangers, and that his brother may be dead, or, even worse, no longer  
66|himself. He takes a breath and opens the door. 
67|
68|## A Brother's Fate
69|
70|You may read from the following text box to describe the Githzerai citadel's first floor to the party:
71|
72|## Slaad Encounter
73|
74|A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of value).
75|
76|The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their stomachs are obscenely swollen.
77|
78|If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison. Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM276) wriggle onto the floor and attack the party.
79|
80|The party should easily finish this combat in 2 rounds; it is meant to  
81|provide them a false sense of confidence before encountering a real  
82|slaad threat. Zardan laments that all the Githzerai were infected, but  
83|is troubled that they haven't actually found the red slaad itself. As a  
84|side note, he wonders aloud what might have happened to the tadpole that  
85|spawned from his brother... 
86|
87|### A Blue Slaad Enraged
88|
89|As the wizard finishes his thought, a blue slaad (MM276) crashes down  
90|from a shadowy alcove of the high ceiling and cries out in rage at the  
91|sight of its slaughtered baby brothers. Its monstrous croaking is  
92|psychically translated in the party's brains as a vengeful vow that  
93|announces their doom. 
94|
95|Blue Slaad Combat. The blue slaad fights to the death and specifically  
96|targets the characters that killed a tadpole with its claws. Through  
97|violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns  
98|that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the  
99|intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when  
100|they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group,  
101|you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that  
102|the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos. 
103|
104|Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving  
105|throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage. 
106|
107|### Grave Aftermath
108|
109|After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone  
110|slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the  
111|chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the  
112|wish spell, there is no way to stop this disease. 
113|
114|But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in  
115|Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes'  
116|aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this  
117|curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that  
118|once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to  
119|his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his  
120|insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall  
121|bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be  
122|dire. 
123|
124|Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass. 
125|
126|The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items made up for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics other than the functional properties described above.
127|
128|## Chapter 2: Limbo Monastery
129|
130|You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel when they first arrive in the plane of chaos:
131|
132|> You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of chaos.
133|
134|### The Ever-Changing Chaos of Limbo
135|
136|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table (DMG 260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share with your players.

You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's roleplay or gameplay load."

Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat.

Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard.

Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is made.

You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in the center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you.

**Githzerai Corpse.** If players choose to approach or investigate the figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in front of it. A DC 12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan recognizes this corpse as his brother and, given the evidence, believes that a red slaad killed him.

### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo

      "content": "1|# Curse of Slaad
2|
3|## Being a Supposedly Competent Group of Warriors and Explorers
4|
5|The party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan to help him investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into the Material Plane. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts located on the fringes of this reality, which is garrisoned to monitor and repel threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened.
6|
7|Beings of Order. Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind flayers millenia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment, from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and hunt down alien monsters.
8|
9|### Zardan, the Githzerai Wizard
10|
11|Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat.
12|
13|Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard.
14|
15|Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is made.
16|
17|You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in the center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you.
18|
19|**Githzerai Corpse.** If players choose to approach or investigate the figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in front of it. A DC 12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan recognizes this corpse as his brother and, given the evidence, believes that a red slaad killed him.
20|
21|### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo
22|
23|### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo
24|
25|If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the  
26|following. 
27|
28|Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from  
29|the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow  
30|their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The  
31|Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile  
32|abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses. 
33|
34|The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a  
35|red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue  
36|slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called  
37|"chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad. 
38|
39|Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274. 
40|
41|## Chapter 1: Compromised Citadel
42|
43|As the party stands before the small citadel's door, Zardan warns that  
44|they may encounter unimaginable monstrosities and incomprehensible  
45|dangers, and that his brother may be dead, or, even worse, no longer  
46|himself. He takes a breath and opens the door. 
47|
48|## A Brother's Fate
49|
50|You may read from the following text box to describe the Githzerai citadel's first floor to the party:
51|
52|## Slaad Encounter
53|
54|A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of value).
55|
56|The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their stomachs are obscenely swollen.
57|
58|If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison. Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM276) wriggle onto the floor and attack the party.
59|
60|The party should easily finish this combat in 2 rounds; it is meant to  
61|provide them a false sense of confidence before encountering a real  
62|slaad threat. Zardan laments that all the Githzerai were infected, but  
63|is troubled that they haven't actually found the red slaad itself. As a  
64|side note, he wonders aloud what might have happened to the tadpole that  
65|spawned from his brother... 
66|
67|### A Blue Slaad Enraged
68|
69|As the wizard finishes his thought, a blue slaad (MM276) crashes down  
70|from a shadowy alcove of the high ceiling and cries out in rage at the  
71|sight of its slaughtered baby brothers. Its monstrous croaking is  
72|psychically translated in the party's brains as a vengeful vow that  
73|announces their doom. 
74|
75|Blue Slaad Combat. The blue slaad fights to the death and specifically  
76|targets the characters that killed a tadpole with its claws. Through  
77|violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns  
78|that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the  
79|intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when  
80|they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group,  
81|you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that  
82|the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos. 
83|
84|Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving  
85|throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage. 
86|
87|### Grave Aftermath
88|
89|After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone  
90|slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the  
91|chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the  
92|wish spell, there is no way to stop this disease. 
93|
94|But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in  
95|Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes'  
96|aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this  
97|curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that  
98|once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to  
99|his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his  
100|insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall  
101|bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be  
102|dire. 
103|
104|Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass. 
105|
106|The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items made up for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics other than the functional properties described above.
107|
108|## Chapter 2: Limbo Monastery
109|
110|You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel when they first arrive in the plane of chaos:
111|
112|> You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of chaos.
113|
114|### The Ever-Changing Chaos of Limbo
115|
116|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table (DMG 260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be dispelled with the *calm emotions*, *lesser restoration*, or *remove curse* spells, and it ends if the character takes a short rest.
117|
118|The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share with your players.
119|
120|The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG 62), while the Chaos Control features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind (DMG 61–62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's roleplay or gameplay load.
121|
122|### Chaos Control
123|
124|Creatures in Limbo gain the following action options.
125|
126|**Telekinesis.** You can spend an action to mentally move an object you can see that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you move the object 5 feet plus 1 foot for every point by which you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below.
127|
128|**Transmutation.** You can spend an action to alter a nonmagical object you can see that isn't being worn or carried and that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you change the object into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder into a ball of fire). The number to beat is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below.
129|
130|**Permanence.** You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for 24 hours, or until you use this ability again.
131|
132|### DC by Object Size
133|
134|| Object Size | Telekinesis DC | Transmutation DC |
135||---|---:|---:|
136|| Tiny | 5 | 10 |
137|| Small | 10 | 15 |
138|| Medium | 15 | 20 |
139|| Large | 20 | 25 |
140|| Huge or larger | 25 | 25 |
141|
142|### Encounter on the Monastic Island
143|
144|The first thing the party notices after acclimating to the chaos is the Githzerai monastery before them, a spire-like stone structure connected at both ends to grassy islands. It is shaped like the column formed when a stalagmite and a stalactite meet, and it is held together thanks to Zardan's sister's sheer willpower. On the steps leading to one of its entrances, a Githzerai monk (MM 161), Lez'lin, is defending herself against 2d4 chaos flumphs.
145|
146|Lez'lin's mind keeps the area around her monastery relatively stable, but some of Limbo's chaos permeates this oasis anyway. If you want to inject some of this plane's chaotic matter shifts into this encounter, use the tables in Appendix B to randomize the battlefield.
147|
148|"Chaos flumphs" are a homebrew monster I created to serve as Limbo's low-level life forms of chaos. They essentially have the same stat block as normal flumphs (MM 135), but the Stench Spray action is replaced by the Chaotic Release action.
149|
150|#### Actions
151|
152|**Tendrils.** *Melee Weapon Attack:* +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) acid damage. At the end of each of its turns, the target must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw, taking 2 (1d4) acid damage on a failure or ending the recurring acid damage on a success. A *lesser restoration* spell cast on the target also ends the recurring acid damage.
153|
154|**Chaotic Release (Recharge 6).** The chaos flumph unleashes a spout of noxious Limbo energy in a direction of its choice. Each creature in a 15-foot cone originating from the chaos flumph must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or suffer a random effect until the end of their next turn:
155|
156|1. **Blinded.** The target can't see and automatically fails ability checks that require sight. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage.
157|2. **Charmed.** The target can't attack the chaos flumph or target it with harmful abilities or magical effects.
158|3. **Deafened.** The target can't hear and automatically fails any ability check that requires hearing.
159|4. **Invisible.** The target is impossible to see without the aid of magic or a special sense. For the purpose of hiding, it is heavily obscured. Its location can be detected if it makes noise or leaves tracks. Attack rolls against it have disadvantage, and its own attack rolls have advantage.
160|5. **Poisoned.** The target has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
161|6. **Restrained.** The target's speed becomes 0 and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage. It has disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.
162|
163|### The Pacifist's Hospitality
164|
165|If the party helps her eliminate the pesky chaos flumphs, Lez'lin expresses her gratitude. She is inclined to aid the disoriented newcomers, especially upon learning that her brother Zardan sent them. She seems unsurprised to learn that some party members are infected with chaos phage, pointing out that the slaad infection has visibly advanced to a critical stage.
166|
167|#### Chaos Phage Visible Symptoms
168|
169|| d8 | Symptom |
170||---:|---|
171|| 1 | Your skin becomes lumpy and covered in warts. |
172|| 2 | Your skin takes on a mottled reddish hue. |
173|| 3 | Your eyes bulge, your sclerae become yellow, and your pupils become horizontal. |
174|| 4 | Your skin becomes dry and new glands on your back and shoulders produce a mildly poisonous secretion that causes minor allergic reactions. |
175|| 5 | A vocal sac grows on your neck, making you croak intermittently. |
176|| 6 | Black claws start growing from your fingertips. |
177|| 7 | Your teeth fall out and your tongue grows long and sticky. You aren't used to its new length, so it often gets in your way when you talk. |
178|| 8 | Roll twice, ignoring this result on a subsequent roll. |
179|
180|### Lez'lin, the Githzerai Monk 
181|
182|Unlike her brother Zardan, Lez'lin possesses incredible mental fortitude  
183|and thrived in the chaotic boil of Limbo. She adheres to the monastic  
184|principles of her people, but her pacifist worldviews led her to isolate  
185|herself from Githzerai communities. She is loath to cause harm to any  
186|creature, no matter how vile or pesky, unless in self-defense. She lives  
187|alone in her small monastery and strives to maintain its structural  
188|integrity, so it may stand as a bastion of nonviolence. 
189|
190|She recalls her brothers fondly, but hasn't seen them for many years  
191|ever since they relocated to the Material Plane. News of Drarth's death  
192|saddens her deeply, but she doesn't let her emotions cloud her focus on  
193|the present. 
194|
195|Lez'lin invites the party inside her foyer, where floating chairs  
196|provide enough comfort for a short rest while the Githzerai assesses  
197|their predicament. Other than the wish spell, she knows of only one way  
198|to cure chaos phage: a death slaad's magic. 
199|
200|### Death Slaadi and You
201|
202|Death slaadi are the peak of slaad evolution: stronger, viler, and more  
203|brutal, these monsters are corrupted by the Negative Energy Plane and  
204|take sadistic pleasure in killing and propagating slaadi dominance  
205|across dimensions. The only way to compel a death slaad to remove chaos  
206|phage is by acquiring its control gem, a magical fragment inside most  
207|slaadi's brains that allows whoever possesses it to subjugate the slaad.  
208|Removing the control gem is a near-impossible, very dangerous feat that  
209|can be approached in two ways: 
210|
211|1. The first method is a lengthy surgical procedure that can only be  
212|    attempted if the slaad is incapacitated. A creature must spend 1  
213|    uninterrupted minute and succeed on a DC20 Medicine check to extract  
214|    the gem. Every failed attempt deals 4d10 psychic damage to the  
215|    slaad. 
216|    
217|2. A control gem can also be obtained through magical means, such as the 9th-level spell *imprisonment* (PHB 252–253). However, this spell takes 1 minute to cast and requires the caster to see the target and stay within 30 feet of it, and the spell is not guaranteed to succeed.
218|
219|In short, no matter the method they attempt, the party will undoubtedly  
220|need to incapacitate or restrain a live death slaad for 1 minute in  
221|order to acquire its control gem. Being a pacifist, Lez'lin won't  
222|directly help the party harm a living being, but she is willing to part  
223|with two legendary items that can help them, as long as they are able to  
224|secure the items themselves. 
225|
226|After they have rested, Lez'lin leads the party into the other half of  
227|her monastery, in which some of Limbo's chaos roils. 
228|
229|### Spell Scroll of Imprisonment
230|
231|The first legendary item provides a way to extract a slaad's control  
232|gem. It is protected by 3 layers, which must be removed sequentially to  
233|access it: 
234|
235|1. **First:** A Large ball of fire, which can be targeted with Transmutation or extinguished with 10 gallons of water (or any spell that could sensibly put out a large fire).
236|2. **Second:** A Medium hollow diamond, which can be transformed with Transmutation or cracked open with the *shatter* spell (PHB 275).
237|3. **Lastly:** A 2-foot-diameter sphere of annihilation (DMG 201) encases the spell scroll. A character can recognize this hole in the multiverse with  
238|a successful DC20 Arcana check (a result between 10 and 20 gives them  
239|the gist). The sphere and the spell scroll move independently of one  
240|another. A creature within 60 feet of the sphere can move it with a  
241|successful DC25 Arcana check. The distance moved is 5 × the creature's  
242|Intelligence modifier (minimum 5 feet). If a creature fails this check,  
243|the sphere moves 10 feet towards them. If the sphere enters a creature's  
244|space, that creature must make a DC13 Dexterity saving throw or touch  
245|it. A creature that voluntarily or involuntarily touches the sphere  
246|takes 4d10 force damage. The sphere can also be moved with a  
247|disadvantaged DC10 Telekinesis check. Moving the sphere of annihilation  
248|by at least 5 feet makes the spell scroll of imprisonment accessible.  
249|**Using the Spell Scroll.** A low-level warlock or wizard can attempt to cast *imprisonment* (PHB 252–253) without the required components by reading the scroll. The user must first make a DC 19 saving throw (Charisma for warlocks and Intelligence for wizards). On a failed save, the scroll disintegrates. On a successful save, the user can cast the spell. If the target stays visible and within 30 feet of the caster for 1 minute, it must make a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw. If a targeted slaad fails this save, its control gem appears in the caster's hand. Whether the target fails or succeeds on its save, the scroll disintegrates. If the casting time is interrupted, nothing happens (see DMG 200 for more rules on spell scrolls).
250|
251|### The Zerthimon Steelbeast
252|
253|The second legendary item gives the party a chance to go toe-to-toe with  
254|a death slaad and even incapacitate it for several minutes. To access  
255|this artifact, the party must first breach its casing of stone. 
256|
257|The Huge mass of stone can be affected by Transmutation. It cracks if it  
258|receives 15 bludgeoning damage in one hit (AC17), revealing a steel  
259|barrel. This is the Zerthimon Steelbeast, a legendary artifact of the  
260|Githzerai (in essence, it is a modified Apparatus of Kwalish (DMG151),  
261|but adapted to better navigate Limbo and suit the party's needs). It has  
262|sensors that can locate slaadi while exploring Limbo, and its claws can  
263|enter a sphere of annihilation without suffering any consequences,  
264|giving the party an additional way to obtain the spell scroll of  
265|imprisonment. 
266|
267|After acquiring these legendary magic items, the party has all they need  
268|to gain the upper hand on a death slaad and steal its control gem. They  
269|must act quickly, however, as the four hours allotted to them in Limbo  
270|by Zardan's planar hourglass are quickly elapsing... 
271|
272|### Zerthimon Steelbeast
273|
274|*Wondrous item, artifact (requires attunement)* 
275|
276|This item first appears to be a Huge steel barrel weighing 500 pounds.  
277|The barrel's door can be forced. open with a successful DC20 Strength  
278|check, or a successful DC20 Dexterity check made with thieves' tools.  
279|The surest way to gain access to this sentient artifact, however, is by  
280|succeeding on a DC15 Persuasion check to instantly attune with it. If a  
281|creature that tries to attune with the Steelbeast is a Githzerai or  
282|lawful good, it gets advantage on this check. If its alignment is  
283|chaotic or evil, the check is made with disadvantage. If a creature  
284|forces its way into the Steelbeast without attuning to it first, it must  
285|spend a short rest inside it learning how to operate its features and  
286|acquainting itself with this wondrous item. 
287|
288|When the Steelbeast is activated, thrusters appear around its rear  
289|circumference, its front surface turns into reinforced glass, two  
290|periscopes extend from either side, a long stinger tail expands from its  
291|back, and two massive pincers unfold. Up to six Medium creatures can fit  
292|inside the Steelbeast, but only the creature attuned to it can direct  
293|its actions. 
294|
295|Sentience. The Zerthimon Steelbeast is a sentient lawful good artifact  
296|with hearing and blindvision out to a range of 60 feet. 
297|
298|The item can speak, read, and understand Common and Gith, and can  
299|communicate telepathically with the creature attuned to it if that  
300|creature is within 60 feet of it. It can also communicate in this way  
301|with all creatures inside it. While you are attuned to it, the  
302|Steelbeast also understands every language you know. 
303|
304|Personality. The Zerthimon Steelbeast speaks in a friendly tone and is  
305|inclined to trust the creature attuned to it. 
306|
307|Its purpose is to eliminate aberrations, such as illithids and slaadi.  
308|It is amiable and courteous with all other creatures (especially  
309|Githzerai), but harbors deep loathing for Limbo's aberrations. It feels  
310|great sorrow for creatures infected by chaos phage or slaad tadpoles and  
311|won't attack them until they become slaadi themselves, or the tadpoles  
312|hatch. 
313|
314|The Steelbeast obeys the creature attuned to it on all matters, but will  
315|attack any slaadi it encounters regardless of its master's orders. A  
316|DC15 Charisma check is the only way to regain control of the Steelbeast.  
317|See Appendix C for the Zerthimon Steelbeast's stat block. 
318|
319|## Chapter 3: Slaad Assault
320|
321|Use the following text box to set the tone for the final battle: 
322|
323|Safe in the belly of the steel apparatus, you have been roaming for what  
324|feels like too long in the chaotic void of Limbo, searching for a death  
325|slaad amidst the flux. Those of you afflicted by chaos phage can see  
326|your symptoms worsening; you feel in the pit of your stomach that very  
327|little time remains. The Zerthimon Steelbeast's sensors lead you further  
328|and further into the primordial soup until, finally, an earthy cliff  
329|fragment melts into bubbles, revealing a grey- skinned, necrotic toad.  
330|The Steelbeast's alarms blare and it rushes forward to meet this deadly  
331|foe, intent on subduing it. The battle of your lives begins now. 
332|
333|### Death Slaad Den
334|
335|You can use the tables in appendix B to generate a random battlefield of  
336|chaos for the showdown against the death slaad. Death slaadi are at home  
337|in the most chaotic environments of Limbo, so don't hold back on the  
338|initial generation and the terrain's subsequent randomization. 
339|
340|Treat the Zerthimon Steelbeast as untouchable by Limbo's chaotic shifts  
341|as with the Permanence feature of Chaos Control, in case matter randomly  
342|spawns in its area. New matter can instead appear around it. 
343|
344|### Attacking as the Death Slaad
345|
346|The death slaad (MM278) relishes this challenge and attacks the  
347|Steelbeast mercilessly with its claws, bite, and 
348|
349|greatsword. It stays close to attack while still trying evade the  
350|Steelbeast's pincers. After a few rounds or after the party performs an  
351|action that would reveal their existence, the slaad shifts its murderous  
352|focus to the characters. 
353|
354|For example, it can telepathically threaten or taunt them, cast fear on  
355|the group, or cast cloudkill inside the Steelbeast. 
356|
357|The slaad fights to the death and prioritizes freeing itself if it is  
358|restrained, unless it sadistically perceives a way to cause pain and  
359|death while grappled. 
360|
361|### Obtaining the Control Gem
362|
363|The Steelbeast can use its Shock Stinger or Sleep Gas actions on the  
364|death slaad to incapacitate it for a few minutes (grappling it with  
365|Pincer Grab beforehand can help). The party then has that amount of time  
366|to attempt to extract the slaad's control gem using the method of their  
367|choice. 
368|
369|If the party wants to use the spell scroll of imprisonment but there are  
370|no wizards nor warlocks among them, they can summon Zardan using the  
371|planar recall bead he gave them earlier. The wizard needs to spend one  
372|minute after materializing to acclimate to Limbo's wracking chaos before  
373|he can take actions. If Zardan succeeds on a DC19 Intelligence saving  
374|throw, he can proceed to cast the spell. Otherwise, the scroll  
375|disintegrates. 
376|
377|Keep in mind that Zardan can use the two rolls from his Portent class  
378|feature during this encounter, if he hasn't used them already. 
379|
380|If the death slaad stays within sight and within 30 feet of the scroll's  
381|user for the minute required to cast the spell, it must make a DC19  
382|Wisdom saving throw (with advantage, as per its Magic Resistance trait).  
383|If it succeeds on this saving throw, the spell scroll disintegrates. If  
384|it fails, the death slaad's eyes gloss over and its entire body relaxes.  
385|The scroll disintegrates and is replaced by a cloudy grey asymmetrical  
386|gemstone in the palm of the scroll user's hand. 
387|
388|### Epilogue
389|
390|If the party successfully defeats the death slaad and obtains its  
391|control gem, they can force it to magically reverse the chaos phage  
392|afflicting their members (no roll required). The previously ill  
393|characters regain their original hit point maximums, lose their  
394|proficiency with Chaos Control, and their physical and mental states  
395|revert to normal. The party can force the slaad to perform any other  
396|action they desire, so long as they remain in control of its control  
397|gem. 
398|
399|The Zerthimon Steelbeast brings them back to Lez'lin's monastery, where  
400|she reunites with Zardan if the party summoned him. They exchange words  
401|of mourning over their brother Drarth's passing, and thank the group for  
402|risking their lives for this mission. The Githzerai then make plans to  
403|inform their people of a Material Plane citadel's fall and the  
404|Steelbeast expresses its wish to continue eradicating aberrations with  
405|them, despite its attachment to the creature attuned to it. 
406|
407|Everyone bids each other farewell before the planar hourglass's four  
408|hours are up and the party is gently displaced back to the Material  
409|Plane. 
410|

524|## Appendix B: Chaotic Environments
525|
526|When running a combat encounter in the unstable plane of Limbo, you may want to bring extra chaos to the battlefield. Use the tables and steps below to introduce random matter shifts to the combat environment. First of all, separate the combat map into an appropriate number of equal-sized sections.
527|
528|1. Every time you introduce a new pocket of matter, 
529|    
530|
531|select a random section of the battlefield in which it will appear,  
532|either by rolling a die, generating a random number, or choosing  
533|yourself. 
534|
535|2. Roll on the Size of New Matter table. 
536|    
537|3. Roll on the Type of New Matter table.

539|

541|new matter you are rolling for replaces it. If the matter would spawn in

592|### Chaos Control
593|

595|

597|see that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful

599|you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table  
600|below. 
601|
602|Transmutation. You can spend an action to alter a nonmagical object you  
603|can see that isn't being worn or carried and that is within 30 feet of  
604|you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you change the object  
605|into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder  
606|into a ball of fire). The number to beat is indicated in the DC by  
607|Object Size table below. 
608|
609|Permanence. You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for 24 hours, or until you use this ability again.

      "content": "1|# Curse of Slaad
2|
3|## Being a Supposedly Competent Group of Warriors and Explorers
4|
5|The party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan to help him investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into the Material Plane. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts located on the fringes of this reality, which is garrisoned to monitor and repel threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened.
6|
7|Beings of Order. Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind flayers millenia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment, from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and hunt down alien monsters.
8|
9|### Zardan, the Githzerai Wizard
10|
11|Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat.
12|
13|Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard.
14|
15|Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is made.
16|
17|You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in the center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you.
18|
19|**Githzerai Corpse.** If players choose to approach or investigate the figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in front of it. A DC 12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan recognizes this corpse as his brother and, given the evidence, believes that a red slaad killed him.
20|
21|### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo
22|
23|If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the  
24|following. 
25|
26|Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from  
27|the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow  
28|their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The  
29|Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile  
30|abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses. 
31|
32|The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a  
33|red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue  
34|slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called  
35|"chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad. 
36|
37|Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274. 
38|
39|## Chapter 1: Compromised Citadel
40|
41|As the party stands before the small citadel's door, Zardan warns that  
42|they may encounter unimaginable monstrosities and incomprehensible  
43|dangers, and that his brother may be dead, or, even worse, no longer  
44|himself. He takes a breath and opens the door. 
45|
46|## A Brother's Fate
47|
48|You may read from the following text box to describe the Githzerai citadel's first floor to the party:
49|
50|## Slaad Encounter
51|
52|A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of value).
53|
54|The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their stomachs are obscenely swollen.
55|
56|If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison. Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM276) wriggle onto the floor and attack the party.
57|
58|The party should easily finish this combat in 2 rounds; it is meant to  
59|provide them a false sense of confidence before encountering a real  
60|slaad threat. Zardan laments that all the Githzerai were infected, but  
61|is troubled that they haven't actually found the red slaad itself. As a  
62|side note, he wonders aloud what might have happened to the tadpole that  
63|spawned from his brother... 
64|
65|### A Blue Slaad Enraged
66|
67|As the wizard finishes his thought, a blue slaad (MM276) crashes down  
68|from a shadowy alcove of the high ceiling and cries out in rage at the  
69|sight of its slaughtered baby brothers. Its monstrous croaking is  
70|psychically translated in the party's brains as a vengeful vow that  
71|announces their doom. 
72|
73|Blue Slaad Combat. The blue slaad fights to the death and specifically  
74|targets the characters that killed a tadpole with its claws. Through  
75|violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns  
76|that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the  
77|intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when  
78|they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group,  
79|you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that  
80|the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos. 
81|
82|Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving  
83|throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage. 
84|
85|### Grave Aftermath
86|
87|After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone  
88|slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the  
89|chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the  
90|wish spell, there is no way to stop this disease. 
91|
92|But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in  
93|Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes'  
94|aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this  
95|curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that  
96|once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to  
97|his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his  
98|insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall  
99|bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be  
100|dire. 
101|
102|Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass. 
103|
104|The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items made up for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics other than the functional properties described above.
105|
106|## Chapter 2: Limbo Monastery
107|
108|You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel when they first arrive in the plane of chaos:
109|
110|> You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of chaos.
111|
112|### The Ever-Changing Chaos of Limbo
113|
114|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table (DMG 260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be dispelled with the *calm emotions*, *lesser restoration*, or *remove curse* spells, and it ends if the character takes a short rest.
115|
116|The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share with your players.
117|
118|The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG 62), while the Chaos Control features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind (DMG 61–62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's roleplay or gameplay load.
119|
120|### Chaos Control
121|
122|Creatures in Limbo gain the following action options.
123|

201|brutal, these monsters are corrupted by the Negative Energy Plane and  
202|take sadistic pleasure in killing and propagating slaadi dominance

The user must first make a DC 19 saving throw (Charisma for warlocks and Intelligence for wizards). On a failed save, the scroll disintegrates. On a successful save, the user can cast the spell. If the target stays visible and within 30 feet of the caster for 1 minute, it must make a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw. If a targeted slaad fails this save, its control gem appears in the caster's hand. Whether the target fails or succeeds on its save, the scroll disintegrates. If the casting time is interrupted, nothing happens (see DMG 200 for more rules on spell scrolls).

318|
319|Use the following text box to set the tone for the final battle: 
320|
321|Safe in the belly of the steel apparatus, you have been roaming for what  
322|feels like too long in the chaotic void of Limbo, searching for a death  
323|slaad amidst the flux. Those of you afflicted by chaos phage can see  
324|your symptoms worsening; you feel in the pit of your stomach that very

      "content": "140|### Encounter on the Monastic Island
141|
142|The first thing the party notices after acclimating to the chaos is the Githzerai monastery before them, a spire-like stone structure connected at both ends to grassy islands. It is shaped like the column formed when a stalagmite and a stalactite meet, and it is held together thanks to Zardan's sister's sheer willpower. On the steps leading to one of its entrances, a Githzerai monk (MM 161), Lez'lin, is defending herself against 2d4 chaos flumphs.
143|
144|Lez'lin's mind keeps the area around her monastery relatively stable, but some of Limbo's chaos permeates this oasis anyway. If you want to inject some of this plane's chaotic matter shifts into this encounter, use the tables in Appendix B to randomize the battlefield.
145|
146|"Chaos flumphs" are a homebrew monster I created to serve as Limbo's low-level life forms of chaos. They essentially have the same stat block as normal flumphs (MM 135), but the Stench Spray action is replaced by the Chaotic Release action.
147|
148|#### Actions
149|
150|**Tendrils.** *Melee Weapon Attack:* +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) acid damage. At the end of each of its turns, the target must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw, taking 2 (1d4) acid damage on a failure or ending the recurring acid damage on a success. A *lesser restoration* spell cast on the target also ends the recurring acid damage.
151|
152|**Chaotic Release (Recharge 6).** The chaos flumph unleashes a spout of noxious Limbo energy in a direction of its choice. Each creature in a 15-foot cone originating from the chaos flumph must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or suffer a random effect until the end of their next turn:
153|
154|1. **Blinded.** The target can't see and automatically fails ability checks that require sight. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage.
155|2. **Charmed.** The target can't attack the chaos flumph or target it with harmful abilities or magical effects.
156|3. **Deafened.** The target can't hear and automatically fails any ability check that requires hearing.
157|4. **Invisible.** The target is impossible to see without the aid of magic or a special sense. For the purpose of hiding, it is heavily obscured. Its location can be detected if it makes noise or leaves tracks. Attack rolls against it have disadvantage, and its own attack rolls have advantage.
158|5. **Poisoned.** The target has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
159|6. **Restrained.** The target's speed becomes 0 and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage. It has disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.
160|
161|### The Pacifist's Hospitality
162|
163|If the party helps her eliminate the pesky chaos flumphs, Lez'lin expresses her gratitude. She is inclined to aid the disoriented newcomers, especially upon learning that her brother Zardan sent them. She seems unsurprised to learn that some party members are infected with chaos phage, pointing out that the slaad infection has visibly advanced to a critical stage.

178|### Lez'lin, the Githzerai Monk 
179|
180|Unlike her brother Zardan, Lez'lin possesses incredible mental fortitude

If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the following.

Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses.

The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called "chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad.

Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274.

      "content": "1|# Curse of Slaad
2|
3|## Being a Supposedly Competent Group of Warriors and Explorers
4|
5|The party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan to help him investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into the Material Plane. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts located on the fringes of this reality, which is garrisoned to monitor and repel threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened.
6|
7|Beings of Order. Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind flayers millenia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment, from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and hunt down alien monsters.
8|
9|### Zardan, the Githzerai Wizard
10|
11|Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat.
12|
13|Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard.
14|
15|Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is made.
16|
17|You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in the center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you.
18|
19|**Githzerai Corpse.** If players choose to approach or investigate the figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in front of it. A DC 12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan recognizes this corpse as his brother and, given the evidence, believes that a red slaad killed him.
20|
21|### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo
22|
23|If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the following.
24|
25|Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses.
26|
27|The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called "chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad.
28|
29|Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274.
30|
31|## Chapter 1: Compromised Citadel
32|
33|As the party stands before the small citadel's door, Zardan warns that  
34|they may encounter unimaginable monstrosities and incomprehensible  
35|dangers, and that his brother may be dead, or, even worse, no longer  
36|himself. He takes a breath and opens the door. 
37|
38|## A Brother's Fate
39|
40|You may read from the following text box to describe the Githzerai citadel's first floor to the party:
41|
42|## Slaad Encounter
43|
44|A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of value).
45|
46|The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their stomachs are obscenely swollen.
47|
48|If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison. Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM276) wriggle onto the floor and attack the party.
49|
50|The party should easily finish this combat in 2 rounds; it is meant to  
51|provide them a false sense of confidence before encountering a real  
52|slaad threat. Zardan laments that all the Githzerai were infected, but  
53|is troubled that they haven't actually found the red slaad itself. As a  
54|side note, he wonders aloud what might have happened to the tadpole that  
55|spawned from his brother... 
56|
57|### A Blue Slaad Enraged
58|
59|As the wizard finishes his thought, a blue slaad (MM276) crashes down  
60|from a shadowy alcove of the high ceiling and cries out in rage at the  
61|sight of its slaughtered baby brothers. Its monstrous croaking is  
62|psychically translated in the party's brains as a vengeful vow that  
63|announces their doom. 
64|
65|Blue Slaad Combat. The blue slaad fights to the death and specifically  
66|targets the characters that killed a tadpole with its claws. Through  
67|violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns  
68|that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the  
69|intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when  
70|they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group,  
71|you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that  
72|the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos. 
73|
74|Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving  
75|throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage. 
76|
77|### Grave Aftermath
78|
79|After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone  
80|slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the  
81|chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the  
82|wish spell, there is no way to stop this disease. 
83|
84|But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in  
85|Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes'  
86|aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this  
87|curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that  
88|once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to  
89|his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his  
90|insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall  
91|bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be  
92|dire. 
93|
94|Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass. 
95|
96|The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items made up for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics other than the functional properties described above.
97|
98|## Chapter 2: Limbo Monastery
99|
100|You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel when they first arrive in the plane of chaos:
101|
102|> You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of chaos.
103|
104|### The Ever-Changing Chaos of Limbo
105|
106|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table (DMG 260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be dispelled with the *calm emotions*, *lesser restoration*, or *remove curse* spells, and it ends if the character takes a short rest.
107|
108|The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share with your players.
109|
110|The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG 62), while the Chaos Control features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind (DMG 61–62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's roleplay or gameplay load."
    }
  ]

As the party stands before the small citadel's door, Zardan warns that they may encounter unimaginable monstrosities and incomprehensible dangers, and that his brother may be dead, or, even worse, no longer himself. He takes a breath and opens the door.

## A Brother's Fate

You may read from the following text box to describe the Githzerai citadel's first floor to the party:

## Slaad Encounter

A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of value).

The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their stomachs are obscenely swollen.

If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison. Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM 276) wriggle onto the floor and attack the party.

The party should easily finish this combat in 2 rounds; it is meant to provide them a false sense of confidence before encountering a real slaad threat. Zardan laments that all the Githzerai were infected, but is troubled that they haven't actually found the red slaad itself. As a side note, he wonders aloud what might have happened to the tadpole that spawned from his brother...

### A Blue Slaad Enraged

As the wizard finishes his thought, a blue slaad (MM 276) crashes down from a shadowy alcove of the high ceiling and cries out in rage at the sight of its slaughtered baby brothers. Its monstrous croaking is psychically translated in the party's brains as a vengeful vow that announces their doom.

Blue Slaad Combat. The blue slaad fights to the death and specifically targets the characters that killed a tadpole with its claws. Through violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group, you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos.

Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage.

41|A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of value).
42|
43|The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their stomachs are obscenely swollen.
44|
45|If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison. Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM 276) wriggle onto the floor and attack the party.
46|
47|The party should easily finish this combat in 2 rounds; it is meant to provide them a false sense of confidence before encountering a real slaad threat. Zardan laments that all the Githzerai were infected, but is troubled that they haven't actually found the red slaad itself. As a side note, he wonders aloud what might have happened to the tadpole that spawned from his brother...
48|
49|### A Blue Slaad Enraged
50|
51|As the wizard finishes his thought, a blue slaad (MM 276) crashes down from a shadowy alcove of the high ceiling and cries out in rage at the sight of its slaughtered baby brothers. Its monstrous croaking is psychically translated in the party's brains as a vengeful vow that announces their doom.
52|
53|Blue Slaad Combat. The blue slaad fights to the death and specifically targets the characters that killed a tadpole with its claws. Through violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group, you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos.
54|
55|Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage.

77|### Grave Aftermath
78|
79|After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone  
80|slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the  
81|chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the  
82|wish spell, there is no way to stop this disease. 
83|
84|But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in  
85|Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes'  
86|aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this  
87|curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that  
88|once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to  
89|his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his  
90|insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall  
91|bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be  
92|dire. 
93|
94|Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass. 
95|
96|The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items made up for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics other than the functional properties described above.

98|## Chapter 2: Limbo Monastery
99|
100|You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel when they first arrive in the plane of chaos:
101|
102|> You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of chaos.
103|
104|### The Ever-Changing Chaos of Limbo
105|
106|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table (DMG 260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be dispelled with the *calm emotions*, *lesser restoration*, or *remove curse* spells, and it ends if the character takes a short rest.
107|
108|The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share with your players.
109|
110|The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG 62), while the Chaos Control features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind (DMG 61–62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's roleplay or gameplay load.
111|
112|### Chaos Control
113|
114|Creatures in Limbo gain the following action options.
115|
116|**Telekinesis.** You can spend an action to mentally move an object you can see that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you move the object 5 feet plus 1 foot for every point by which you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below.
117|
118|**Transmutation.** You can spend an action to alter a nonmagical object you can see that isn't being worn or carried and that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you change the object into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder into a ball of fire). The number to beat is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below.
119|
120|**Permanence.** You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for 24 hours, or until you use this ability again.
121|

123|

127|| Small | 10 | 15 |
128|| Medium | 15 | 20 |
129|| Large | 20 | 25 |
130|| Huge or larger | 25 | 25 |

132|### Encounter on the Monastic Island
133|
134|The first thing the party notices after acclimating to the chaos is the Githzerai monastery before them, a spire-like stone structure connected at both ends to grassy islands. It is shaped like the column formed when a stalagmite and a stalactite meet, and it is held together thanks to Zardan's sister's sheer willpower. On the steps leading to one of its entrances, a Githzerai monk (MM 161), Lez'lin, is defending herself against 2d4 chaos flumphs.
135|
136|Lez'lin's mind keeps the area around her monastery relatively stable, but some of Limbo's chaos permeates this oasis anyway. If you want to inject some of this plane's chaotic matter shifts into this encounter, use the tables in Appendix B to randomize the battlefield.
137|
138|"Chaos flumphs" are a homebrew monster I created to serve as Limbo's low-level life forms of chaos. They essentially have the same stat block as normal flumphs (MM 135), but the Stench Spray action is replaced by the Chaotic Release action.
139|
140|#### Actions
141|
142|**Tendrils.** *Melee Weapon Attack:* +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) acid damage. At the end of each of its turns, the target must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw, taking 2 (1d4) acid damage on a failure or ending the recurring acid damage on a success. A *lesser restoration* spell cast on the target also ends the recurring acid damage.
143|
144|**Chaotic Release (Recharge 6).** The chaos flumph unleashes a spout of noxious Limbo energy in a direction of its choice. Each creature in a 15-foot cone originating from the chaos flumph must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or suffer a random effect until the end of their next turn:
145|
146|1. **Blinded.** The target can't see and automatically fails ability checks that require sight. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage.
147|2. **Charmed.** The target can't attack the chaos flumph or target it with harmful abilities or magical effects.
148|3. **Deafened.** The target can't hear and automatically fails any ability check that requires hearing.
149|4. **Invisible.** The target is impossible to see without the aid of magic or a special sense. For the purpose of hiding, it is heavily obscured. Its location can be detected if it makes noise or leaves tracks. Attack rolls against it have disadvantage, and its own attack rolls have advantage.
150|5. **Poisoned.** The target has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
151|6. **Restrained.** The target's speed becomes 0 and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage. It has disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.
152|
153|### The Pacifist's Hospitality
154|
155|If the party helps her eliminate the pesky chaos flumphs, Lez'lin expresses her gratitude. She is inclined to aid the disoriented newcomers, especially upon learning that her brother Zardan sent them. She seems unsurprised to learn that some party members are infected with chaos phage, pointing out that the slaad infection has visibly advanced to a critical stage.
