170|### Lez'lin, the Githzerai Monk 
171|
172|Unlike her brother Zardan, Lez'lin possesses incredible mental fortitude  
173|and thrived in the chaotic boil of Limbo. She adheres to the monastic  
174|principles of her people, but her pacifist worldviews led her to isolate  
175|herself from Githzerai communities. She is loath to cause harm to any  
176|creature, no matter how vile or pesky, unless in self-defense. She lives  
177|alone in her small monastery and strives to maintain its structural  
178|integrity, so it may stand as a bastion of nonviolence. 
179|
180|She recalls her brothers fondly, but hasn't seen them for many years  
181|ever since they relocated to the Material Plane. News of Drarth's death  
182|saddens her deeply, but she doesn't let her emotions cloud her focus on  
183|the present. 
184|
185|Lez'lin invites the party inside her foyer, where floating chairs  
186|provide enough comfort for a short rest while the Githzerai assesses  
187|their predicament. Other than the wish spell, she knows of only one way  
188|to cure chaos phage: a death slaad's magic. 
189|
190|### Death Slaadi and You
191|
192|Death slaadi are the peak of slaad evolution: stronger, viler, and more  
193|brutal, these monsters are corrupted by the Negative Energy Plane and  
194|take sadistic pleasure in killing and propagating slaadi dominance  
195|across dimensions. The only way to compel a death slaad to remove chaos  
196|phage is by acquiring its control gem, a magical fragment inside most  
197|slaadi's brains that allows whoever possesses it to subjugate the slaad.  
198|Removing the control gem is a near-impossible, very dangerous feat that  
199|can be approached in two ways: 
200|
201|1. The first method is a lengthy surgical procedure that can only be  
202|    attempted if the slaad is incapacitated. A creature must spend 1  
203|    uninterrupted minute and succeed on a DC20 Medicine check to extract  
204|    the gem. Every failed attempt deals 4d10 psychic damage to the  
205|    slaad. 
206|    
207|2. A control gem can also be obtained through magical means, such as the 9th-level spell *imprisonment* (PHB 252–253). However, this spell takes 1 minute to cast and requires the caster to see the target and stay within 30 feet of it, and the spell is not guaranteed to succeed.
208|
209|In short, no matter the method they attempt, the party will undoubtedly  
210|need to incapacitate or restrain a live death slaad for 1 minute in  
211|order to acquire its control gem. Being a pacifist, Lez'lin won't  
212|directly help the party harm a living being, but she is willing to part  
213|with two legendary items that can help them, as long as they are able to  
214|secure the items themselves. 
215|
216|After they have rested, Lez'lin leads the party into the other half of  
217|her monastery, in which some of Limbo's chaos roils. 
218|
219|### Spell Scroll of Imprisonment
220|
221|The first legendary item provides a way to extract a slaad's control  
222|gem. It is protected by 3 layers, which must be removed sequentially to  
223|access it: 
224|
225|1. **First:** A Large ball of fire, which can be targeted with Transmutation or extinguished with 10 gallons of water (or any spell that could sensibly put out a large fire).
226|2. **Second:** A Medium hollow diamond, which can be transformed with Transmutation or cracked open with the *shatter* spell (PHB 275).
227|3. **Lastly:** A 2-foot-diameter sphere of annihilation (DMG 201) encases the spell scroll. A character can recognize this hole in the multiverse with  
228|a successful DC20 Arcana check (a result between 10 and 20 gives them  
229|the gist). The sphere and the spell scroll move independently of one  
230|another. A creature within 60 feet of the sphere can move it with a  
231|successful DC25 Arcana check. The distance moved is 5 × the creature's  
232|Intelligence modifier (minimum 5 feet). If a creature fails this check,  
233|the sphere moves 10 feet towards them. If the sphere enters a creature's  
234|space, that creature must make a DC13 Dexterity saving throw or touch  
235|it. A creature that voluntarily or involuntarily touches the sphere  
236|takes 4d10 force damage. The sphere can also be moved with a  
237|disadvantaged DC10 Telekinesis check. Moving the sphere of annihilation  
238|by at least 5 feet makes the spell scroll of imprisonment accessible.  
239|**Using the Spell Scroll.** A low-level warlock or wizard can attempt to cast *imprisonment* (PHB 252–253) without the required components by reading the scroll. The user must first make a DC 19 saving throw (Charisma for warlocks and Intelligence for wizards). On a failed save, the scroll disintegrates. On a successful save, the user can cast the spell. If the target stays visible and within 30 feet of the caster for 1 minute, it must make a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw. If a targeted slaad fails this save, its control gem appears in the caster's hand. Whether the target fails or succeeds on its save, the scroll disintegrates. If the casting time is interrupted, nothing happens (see DMG 200 for more rules on spell scrolls).
240|
241|### The Zerthimon Steelbeast
242|
243|The second legendary item gives the party a chance to go toe-to-toe with  
244|a death slaad and even incapacitate it for several minutes. To access  
245|this artifact, the party must first breach its casing of stone. 
246|
247|The Huge mass of stone can be affected by Transmutation. It cracks if it  
248|receives 15 bludgeoning damage in one hit (AC17), revealing a steel  
249|barrel. This is the Zerthimon Steelbeast, a legendary artifact of the  
250|Githzerai (in essence, it is a modified Apparatus of Kwalish (DMG151),  
251|but adapted to better navigate Limbo and suit the party's needs). It has  
252|sensors that can locate slaadi while exploring Limbo, and its claws can  
253|enter a sphere of annihilation without suffering any consequences,  
254|giving the party an additional way to obtain the spell scroll of  
255|imprisonment. 
256|
257|After acquiring these legendary magic items, the party has all they need  
258|to gain the upper hand on a death slaad and steal its control gem. They  
259|must act quickly, however, as the four hours allotted to them in Limbo  
260|by Zardan's planar hourglass are quickly elapsing... 
261|
262|### Zerthimon Steelbeast
263|
264|*Wondrous item, artifact (requires attunement)* 
265|
266|This item first appears to be a Huge steel barrel weighing 500 pounds.  
267|The barrel's door can be forced. open with a successful DC20 Strength  
268|check, or a successful DC20 Dexterity check made with thieves' tools.  
269|The surest way to gain access to this sentient artifact, however, is by  
270|succeeding on a DC15 Persuasion check to instantly attune with it. If a  
271|creature that tries to attune with the Steelbeast is a Githzerai or  
272|lawful good, it gets advantage on this check. If its alignment is  
273|chaotic or evil, the check is made with disadvantage. If a creature  
274|forces its way into the Steelbeast without attuning to it first, it must  
275|spend a short rest inside it learning how to operate its features and  
276|acquainting itself with this wondrous item. 
277|
278|When the Steelbeast is activated, thrusters appear around its rear  
279|circumference, its front surface turns into reinforced glass, two  
280|periscopes extend from either side, a long stinger tail expands from its  
281|back, and two massive pincers unfold. Up to six Medium creatures can fit  
282|inside the Steelbeast, but only the creature attuned to it can direct  
283|its actions. 
284|
285|Sentience. The Zerthimon Steelbeast is a sentient lawful good artifact  
286|with hearing and blindvision out to a range of 60 feet. 
287|
288|The item can speak, read, and understand Common and Gith, and can  
289|communicate telepathically with the creature attuned to it if that  
290|creature is within 60 feet of it. It can also communicate in this way  
291|with all creatures inside it. While you are attuned to it, the  
292|Steelbeast also understands every language you know. 
293|
294|Personality. The Zerthimon Steelbeast speaks in a friendly tone and is  
295|inclined to trust the creature attuned to it. 
296|
297|Its purpose is to eliminate aberrations, such as illithids and slaadi.  
298|It is amiable and courteous with all other creatures (especially  
299|Githzerai), but harbors deep loathing for Limbo's aberrations. It feels  
300|great sorrow for creatures infected by chaos phage or slaad tadpoles and  
301|won't attack them until they become slaadi themselves, or the tadpoles  
302|hatch. 
303|
304|The Steelbeast obeys the creature attuned to it on all matters, but will  
305|attack any slaadi it encounters regardless of its master's orders. A  
306|DC15 Charisma check is the only way to regain control of the Steelbeast.  
307|See Appendix C for the Zerthimon Steelbeast's stat block.

309|## Chapter 3: Slaad Assault
310|
311|Use the following text box to set the tone for the final battle: 
312|
313|Safe in the belly of the steel apparatus, you have been roaming for what  
314|feels like too long in the chaotic void of Limbo, searching for a death  
315|slaad amidst the flux. Those of you afflicted by chaos phage can see  
316|your symptoms worsening; you feel in the pit of your stomach that very  
317|little time remains. The Zerthimon Steelbeast's sensors lead you further  
318|and further into the primordial soup until, finally, an earthy cliff  
319|fragment melts into bubbles, revealing a grey- skinned, necrotic toad.  
320|The Steelbeast's alarms blare and it rushes forward to meet this deadly  
321|foe, intent on subduing it. The battle of your lives begins now. 
322|
323|### Death Slaad Den
324|
325|You can use the tables in appendix B to generate a random battlefield of  
326|chaos for the showdown against the death slaad. Death slaadi are at home  
327|in the most chaotic environments of Limbo, so don't hold back on the  
328|initial generation and the terrain's subsequent randomization. 
329|
330|Treat the Zerthimon Steelbeast as untouchable by Limbo's chaotic shifts  
331|as with the Permanence feature of Chaos Control, in case matter randomly  
332|spawns in its area. New matter can instead appear around it. 
333|
334|### Attacking as the Death Slaad
335|
336|The death slaad (MM278) relishes this challenge and attacks the  
337|Steelbeast mercilessly with its claws, bite, and 
338|
339|greatsword. It stays close to attack while still trying evade the  
340|Steelbeast's pincers. After a few rounds or after the party performs an  
341|action that would reveal their existence, the slaad shifts its murderous  
342|focus to the characters. 
343|
344|For example, it can telepathically threaten or taunt them, cast fear on  
345|the group, or cast cloudkill inside the Steelbeast. 
346|
347|The slaad fights to the death and prioritizes freeing itself if it is  
348|restrained, unless it sadistically perceives a way to cause pain and  
349|death while grappled. 
350|
351|### Obtaining the Control Gem
352|
353|The Steelbeast can use its Shock Stinger or Sleep Gas actions on the  
354|death slaad to incapacitate it for a few minutes (grappling it with  
355|Pincer Grab beforehand can help). The party then has that amount of time  
356|to attempt to extract the slaad's control gem using the method of their  
357|choice. 
358|
359|If the party wants to use the spell scroll of imprisonment but there are  
360|no wizards nor warlocks among them, they can summon Zardan using the  
361|planar recall bead he gave them earlier. The wizard needs to spend one  
362|minute after materializing to acclimate to Limbo's wracking chaos before  
363|he can take actions. If Zardan succeeds on a DC19 Intelligence saving  
364|throw, he can proceed to cast the spell. Otherwise, the scroll  
365|disintegrates. 
366|
367|Keep in mind that Zardan can use the two rolls from his Portent class  
368|feature during this encounter, if he hasn't used them already. 
369|
370|If the death slaad stays within sight and within 30 feet of the scroll's  
371|user for the minute required to cast the spell, it must make a DC19  
372|Wisdom saving throw (with advantage, as per its Magic Resistance trait).  
373|If it succeeds on this saving throw, the spell scroll disintegrates. If  
374|it fails, the death slaad's eyes gloss over and its entire body relaxes.  
375|The scroll disintegrates and is replaced by a cloudy grey asymmetrical  
376|gemstone in the palm of the scroll user's hand. 
377|
378|### Epilogue
379|
380|If the party successfully defeats the death slaad and obtains its  
381|control gem, they can force it to magically reverse the chaos phage  
382|afflicting their members (no roll required). The previously ill  
383|characters regain their original hit point maximums, lose their  
384|proficiency with Chaos Control, and their physical and mental states  
385|revert to normal. The party can force the slaad to perform any other  
386|action they desire, so long as they remain in control of its control  
387|gem. 
388|
389|The Zerthimon Steelbeast brings them back to Lez'lin's monastery, where  
390|she reunites with Zardan if the party summoned him. They exchange words  
391|of mourning over their brother Drarth's passing, and thank the group for  
392|risking their lives for this mission. The Githzerai then make plans to  
393|inform their people of a Material Plane citadel's fall and the  
394|Steelbeast expresses its wish to continue eradicating aberrations with  
395|them, despite its attachment to the creature attuned to it. 
396|
397|Everyone bids each other farewell before the planar hourglass's four  
398|hours are up and the party is gently displaced back to the Material  
399|Plane.

516|When running a combat encounter in the unstable plane of Limbo, you may want to bring extra chaos to the battlefield. 518|1. Every time you introduce a new pocket of matter, 
519|    
520|

522|either by rolling a die, generating a random number, or choosing  
523|yourself.

### Grave Aftermath

After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the *wish* spell, there is no way to stop this disease.

But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes' aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be dire.

Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass.

The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items made up for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics other than the functional properties described above.

# Curse of Slaad

## Being a Supposedly Competent Group of Warriors and Explorers

The party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan to help him investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into the Material Plane. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts located on the fringes of this reality, which is garrisoned to monitor and repel threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened.

Beings of Order. Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind flayers millenia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment, from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and hunt down alien monsters.

### Zardan, the Githzerai Wizard

Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat.

Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard.

Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is made.

You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in the center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you.

**Githzerai Corpse.** If players choose to approach or investigate the figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in front of it. A DC 12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan recognizes this corpse as his brother and, given the evidence, believes that a red slaad killed him.

### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo

If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the following.

Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses.

The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called "chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad.

Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274.

## Chapter 1: Compromised Citadel

As the party stands before the small citadel's door, Zardan warns that they may encounter unimaginable monstrosities and incomprehensible dangers, and that his brother may be dead, or, even worse, no longer himself. He takes a breath and opens the door.

## A Brother's Fate

You may read from the following text box to describe the Githzerai citadel's first floor to the party:

## Slaad Encounter

A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of value).

The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their stomachs are obscenely swollen.

If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison. Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM 276) wriggle onto the floor and attack the party.

The party should easily finish this combat in 2 rounds; it is meant to provide them a false sense of confidence before encountering a real slaad threat. Zardan laments that all the Githzerai were infected, but is troubled that they haven't actually found the red slaad itself. As a side note, he wonders aloud what might have happened to the tadpole that spawned from his brother...

### A Blue Slaad Enraged

As the wizard finishes his thought, a blue slaad (MM 276) crashes down from a shadowy alcove of the high ceiling and cries out in rage at the sight of its slaughtered baby brothers. Its monstrous croaking is psychically translated in the party's brains as a vengeful vow that announces their doom.

Blue Slaad Combat. The blue slaad fights to the death and specifically targets the characters that killed a tadpole with its claws. Through violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group, you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos.

Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage.

### Grave Aftermath

After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the *wish* spell, there is no way to stop this disease.

But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes' aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be dire.

Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass.

The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items made up for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics other than the functional properties described above.

A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of value).

The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their stomachs are obscenely swollen.

If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison. Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM 276) wriggle onto the floor and attack the party.

The party should easily finish this combat in 2 rounds; it is meant to provide them a false sense of confidence before encountering a real slaad threat. Zardan laments that all the Githzerai were infected, but is troubled that they haven't actually found the red slaad itself. As a side note, he wonders aloud what might have happened to the tadpole that spawned from his brother...

### A Blue Slaad Enraged

As the wizard finishes his thought, a blue slaad (MM 276) crashes down from a shadowy alcove of the high ceiling and cries out in rage at the sight of its slaughtered baby brothers. Its monstrous croaking is psychically translated in the party's brains as a vengeful vow that announces their doom.

Blue Slaad Combat. The blue slaad fights to the death and specifically targets the characters that killed a tadpole with its claws. Through violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group, you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos.

Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage.

### Grave Aftermath

After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the *wish* spell, there is no way to stop this disease.

But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes' aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be dire.

Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass.

The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items made up for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics other than the functional properties described above.

## Being a Supposedly Competent Group of Warriors and Explorers

The party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan to help him investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into the Material Plane. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts located on the fringes of this reality, which is garrisoned to monitor and repel threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened.

Beings of Order. Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind flayers millenia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment, from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and hunt down alien monsters.

### Zardan, the Githzerai Wizard

Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat.

Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard.

Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is made.

You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in the center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you.

**Githzerai Corpse.** If players choose to approach or investigate the figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses.

The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called "chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad.

Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274.

## Chapter 1: Compromised Citadel

**Tendrils.** *Melee Weapon Attack:* +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) acid damage. At the end of each of its turns, the target must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw, taking 2 (1d4) acid damage on a failure or ending the recurring acid damage on a success. A *lesser restoration* spell cast on the target also ends the recurring acid damage.

**Chaotic Release (Recharge 6).** The chaos flumph unleashes a spout of noxious Limbo energy in a direction of its choice. Each creature in a 15-foot cone originating from the chaos flumph must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or suffer a random effect until the end of their next turn:

1. **Blinded.** The target can't see and automatically fails ability checks that require sight. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage.
2. **Charmed.** The target can't attack the chaos flumph or target it with harmful abilities or magical effects.
3. **Deafened.** The target can't hear and automatically fails any ability check that requires hearing.
4. **Invisible.** The target is impossible to see without the aid of magic or a special sense. For the purpose of hiding, it is heavily obscured. Its location can be detected if it makes noise or leaves tracks. Attack rolls against it have disadvantage, and its own attack rolls have advantage.
5. **Poisoned.** The target has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
6. **Restrained.** The target's speed becomes 0 and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage. It has disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.

48|# Description
49|
50|> _“Bleugh. I must admit, I enjoyed mein breakfast much less on ze way owt zahn on the ze vay in. Vhere iz zhat putrified korpse?”_
51|> 
52|> _— [[Humperdink]], Queasy_
53|
54|When you smell the scent of rotting flesh in the jungle, it means one of three things: Undead abound, something didn’t finish its meal, or there’s a rafflesia nearby. When the flesh-eating deadwater amoeba finds a rafflesia, it hijacks the smelly-yet-innocent plant, converting it into a vessel of necrotic disease: a deadwater rafflesia.
55|
56|**_Eau de Corpse._** Though rare, the greatest threat a typical rafflesia plant poses to a jungle wanderer is nausea induced by its gut-churning perfume: the scent of rotting flesh. It’s a strategy evolved to attract its pollinators—typically carrion-eating beetles—to enter the plant’s flower and become covered in pollen. However, when a magical, flesh-eating amoeba takes residence in a rafflesia, the once-harmless plant changes into a stalking predator.
57|
58|**_Bite-Size._** Detritivores make up most of a deadwater rafflesia’s diet. Drawn in by the scent of rotting flesh, tiny beetles and scavengers enter the plant’s flower looking for a snack, only to become the meal of the waiting amoeba. Smaller fleshy creatures like slugs and jungle mice can be consumed quickly, while larger hardier ones, like beetles and millipedes, act as carriers, taking the amoeba to the next rafflesia before they too succumb to the flesh-eating microbe
59|
60|**_Patient Hunter._** When it rains in the jungle, the amoeba induces the rafflesia to turn its flowers upwards, converting them into water-capturing buckets. After the rain, while the rafflesia’s scent is muted, the water is an enticing resource for larger creatures like apes, deer, and explorers. An agonising and prolonged death awaits the creature after drinking the microbe-laden water, as the amoeba eats the imbiber from the inside out.
61|
62|However, there’s always a chance of recovery, and this is where the deadwater rafflesia’s secondary hunting strategy comes into play. Deadwater rafflesia are animate plants and, after infecting a creature, uproot themselves to follow their victim. At its weakest moment, they strike with root and claw, rending their prey until it can be fed to the waiting amoeba inside their flower.",

103|### ENCOUNTER ON THE MONASTIC ISLAND 
104|
105|The first thing the party notices after acclimating to the chaos is the Githzerai monastery before them, a spire- like stone structure connected at both ends to grassy islands. It is shaped like the column formed when a stalagmite and a stalactite meet, and it is held together thanks to Zardan's sister's sheer willpower. On the steps leading to one of its entrances, a **Githzerai monk** (MM161), Lez'lin, is defending herself against 2d4 **chaos flumphs**. 
106|
107|Lez'lin's mind keeps the area around her monastery relatively stable, but some of Limbo's chaos permeates this oasis anyways. If you want to inject some of this plane's chaotic matter shifts into this encounter, use the tables in Appendix B to randomize the battlefield.

150|
151|**Tendrils.** *Melee Weapon Attack:* +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) acid damage. At the end of each of its turns, the target must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw, taking 2 (1d4) acid damage on a failure or ending the recurring acid damage on a success. A *lesser restoration* spell cast on the target also ends the recurring acid damage.
152|
153|**Chaotic Release (Recharge 6).** The chaos flumph unleashes a spout of noxious Limbo energy in a direction of its choice. Each creature in a 15-foot cone originating from the chaos flumph must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or suffer a random effect until the end of their next turn:
154|
155|1. **Blinded.** The target can't see and automatically fails ability checks that require sight. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage.

1. Blinded. The target can't see and automatically fails ability checks that require sight. Attack rolls against them have advantage, and their own attack rolls have disadvantage. 

2. Charmed. The target can't attack the chaos flumph or target 

it with harmful abilities or magical effects. 

3. Deafened. The target can't hear and automatically fails any 

ability check that requires hearing. 

4. Invisible. The target is impossible to see without the aid of 

magic or a special sense. For the purpose of hiding, they are heavily obscured. Their location can be detected if they make noise or leave tracks. Attack rolls against them have disadvantage, and their own attack rolls have advantage. 5. Poisoned. The target has disadvantage on attack rolls and 

ability checks. 

6. Restrained. The target's speed becomes 0 and they can't 

benefit from any bonus to their speed. Attack rolls against them have advantage, and their own attack rolls have disadvantage. They have disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.

### Zerthimon Steelbeast

*Huge artifact, lawful good*

- **Armor Class** 20
- **Hit Points** 150
- **Speed** 30 ft., fly (hover)

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 20 (+5) | 6 (-2) | 10 (+0) | 16 (+3) | 12 (+1) | 10 (+0) |

- **Damage Immunities** poison
- **Condition Immunities** blinded, poisoned, prone
- **Senses** blindvision 60 ft.
- **Languages** Common, Gith; understands the languages of the creature attuned to it
- **Proficiency Bonus** +4

#### Actions

**Claw Snap.** *Melee Weapon Attack:* +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 4d10 + 5 bludgeoning damage.

**Pincer Grab.** *Melee Weapon Attack:* +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* The target is grappled (escape DC 15). Until this grapple ends, the Steelbeast can't use Claw Snap or Pincer Grab on another target.

**Shock Stinger.** *Melee Weapon Attack:* +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. *Hit:* 3d12 + 3 lightning damage. If the target is below half its hit point maximum, it must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target is stunned for 1d4 minutes.

**Sleep Gas.** Every creature within a 30-foot radius of the Steelbeast must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw. If the creature fails its save and is still within 30 feet of the Steelbeast by the end of its next turn, it falls unconscious for 1d6 + 2 minutes. The creature can reattempt the saving throw if it takes damage while unconscious.

**Improvised Action.** If a creature attuned to the Steelbeast succeeds on a DC 15 Intelligence check, they can make the Steelbeast improvise an action that isn't reasonably outside of its capabilities.

2|title: History of Stickyickistan
3|---
4|
5|Stickyickistan is an island on the planet of [[Mythmos]], shrouded in magic and home to one of the largest economies in the realms. Its wealth is built primarily on the cultivation and export of [[Arcannabis]], along with trade in [[Arcanite]] and other resources. The island’s size and distance from other landmasses are difficult to measure. Even the most sophisticated magic and technology fails beyond a certain distance from its shores.
6|
7|The waters around Stickyickistan form a region much like a magical Bermuda Triangle. Pilots and sailors report violent weather, distorted horizons, impossible currents, and terrifying creatures from above and below. Vast deposits of [[Arcanite]] beneath [[Mount Zooka]] have warped time, space, and the Weave around the island, producing these phenomena and making accurate maps difficult to create. Stickyickistan can be seen from [[Lumytholarispace]] and appears on maps of Mythmos, but it always looks smaller than it seems when approached.
8|
9|

10|*This map is not to scale, and does not include all regions.*
11|# Modern Stickyickistan
12|
13|Stickyickistan is a city-state built around the active [[Mount Zooka]], whose obsidian slopes and glowing Arcanite veins dominate the island’s skyline. Approximately 27 million people live across a dense network of terraced districts connected by bridges, roads, canals, lifts, and industrial transit lines. The Capitol stands on [[Nevercough Island]], a small landmass sheltered within the [[Percolat Inlet]]. The climate is generally tropical, with hot, humid weather across the urban core. Farther inland, desertification has created increasingly arid regions, a legacy of [[Human Colonialism]] and industrialization.
14|
15|The city rises in layers around the volcano. Wealthy residences climb into the jungle, where enchanted gardens and fortified estates overlook the ocean. Beneath them, poorer settlements cling to the mountainside in a haze of ash, smoke, brimstone, and sulfur. Above these districts, the [[Industrial Zone]] follows the crater’s rim and extends into the mountain through mines, foundries, refineries, and [[Magitech]] workshops.
16|
17|[[Mount Zooka]] is an active [[Arcanite]] Cone, a rare volcano formed above rich deposits of raw Arcanite. Its slopes are black and glassy, marked by glowing veins of molten rock and slow-moving lava flows. Violent eruptions scatter volcanic stone, magma, and chunks of raw Arcanite across the island. Miners, magitech engineers, alchemists, and bounty hunters maintain dangerous outposts along the crater’s rim, searching for ore, magical artifacts, and volatile energy. The Dwarves of [[Bongstad]] have carved a fortified settlement into the mountain’s base, using its heat to power their forges.
18|
19|Arcanite fuels much of Stickyickistan’s wealth and technology. Once extracted and purified, it can be worked into weapons, armor, artifacts, and industrial systems. The [[Nevercough Tribunal]] and [[The Seekers of the Vein]] operate mines and outposts around the crater, while [[Tokenheim Extractions Inc.]] and other industrial concerns process the ore and produce much of the city-state’s Magitech. Waste from the [[Industrial Zone]] feeds salvage operations at [[Seekers' Scrapyard]] and is collected by groups such as [[The Seekers of the Vein]], [[Zooka Mire Collective]], and [[The Iron Sovereign]].
20|
21|The island’s soil is rich in nutrients and infused with Arcanite. Flora and fauna grow with unusual fertility and magical potency, especially in [[North Booftown]], the agricultural heartland. [[Astallon Acres]] lies along the wetlands bordering the [[Zooka Mire]], where [[Ezra Astallon]] pays farm workers unusually well and resolves local problems with money. [[Arcannabis]] remains the city-state’s primary export, while Arcanite, magebred animals, and other natural resources provide additional wealth.
22|
23|Since the arrival of Human colonists, [[Alcohol]] has been outlawed because the government considers it a threat to the Arcannabis market. [[Zooka Malt]], a beverage made from Arcannabis buds, has become the principal alternative to traditional ale. The city’s merchants sell countless infused varieties, from cheap street brews to carefully aged drinks served in the private lounges of [[Bobo Bush Estates]].
24|
25|[[Nevercough Island]] is the seat of political power and old money. At its heart stands the [[Capitol Building]], where Chief Magistrate [[Dabnar Nevercough]] rules through courts that dispense justice and corruption in equal measure. The island also contains the [[Grand Arcanum Library]], the [[Nevercough Museum]], elite magical academies such as [[N.E.R.D]], high-end boutiques, apothecaries, and specialty Magitech shops. The former settlement of [[Nevercough City]] remains the name commonly used for the island and its historic urban core.
26|
27|The [[Ashen Citadel]] rises over Nevercough Island as the headquarters of the [[Ashen Shadow Society]], Stickyickistan’s most infamous bounty-hunting guild. Its dark stone walls, Magitech barriers, arcane wards, training facilities, forges, laboratories, archives, and holding cells make it both fortress and command center. Few outsiders enter without a contract, and fewer leave without becoming part of someone else’s case file.
28|
29|South of Nevercough Island and north of the volcano lies [[Lower South Booftown]], commonly called [[Booftown]]. This middle-class district is known for family-owned shops, public parks, and relatively stable neighborhoods. A slow-moving river of thick, dark lava separates it from [[Upper South Booftown]], known as [[The Ashtray]].
30|
31|The Ashtray is a smoke-blackened district of crooked tenements, ash-slick alleys, rooftop walkways, hidden grow rooms, and half-legal additions built over generations. Its native [[Halfling|halfling]] population is large, but it also shelters outcasts, fugitives, smugglers, mercenaries, failed apprentices, and anyone too useful, desperate, or dangerous to fit elsewhere. The [[Mandem on Booftown]] and [[Cough City Crew]] fight over Arcannabis, underground fighting, protection rackets, gambling, bootlegged Alcohol, and black-market Magitech. Neither gang fully controls the district. The Sootsteps connect rooftops and exterior stairways, the Cinder Courts host dice games and informal trials, and [[The Black Stalls]] sell stolen goods, poisons, counterfeit papers, and illegal Magitech parts. To outsiders, the district is dangerous. To locals, it is home.
32|
33|To the east of the volcano lies [[Bobo Bush Estates]], where merchant lords, arcane industrialists, politicians, and retired crime bosses live in lavish villas protected by enchanted gardens and high-security Magitech. Deals worth more than a kingdom’s treasury are made over fine Arcannabis and aged Zooka Malt. Espionage, blackmail, and silent assassinations decide more than elections ever do.
34|
35|North Booftown is the center of food production and Arcannabis cultivation. Its volcanic soil produces crops that grow larger, faster, and stronger than those found elsewhere. The region also belongs to [[House Northbourne]], the least powerful noble house in the [[Nevercough Tribunal]]. Publicly, the Northbournes dominate animal breeding, training, and handling. They own [[The North Booftown Downs]] and founded the [[Handler’s Guild]], whose expertise includes prized racehorses, exotic creatures, and [[Magebred Animals]].
36|
37|In criminal circles, the Northbournes are called [[The Norfies]]. The family does not use the name, since it can imply criminal affiliations and attract the attention of the [[Nevercough Tribunal]] or the [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]]. Behind their respectable public image, the Norfies control much of the city-state’s illicit Alcohol trade, manipulate racing odds and outcomes, operate gambling syndicates, and host underground fighting rings. Their agents and intermediaries preserve the noble family’s plausible deniability.
38|
39|On the western side of the city, [[Bongstad]] is a Dwarven settlement carved into Mount Zooka. Its maze of tunnels, bridges, terraces, and magitech pipes carries molten slag and processed Arcanite between refineries and forges. Bongstad combines old Dwarven traditions with Arcannabis-fueled invention. Miners and blacksmiths share the settlement with inventors, alchemists, and experimental herbalists. Visitors are advised to bring a strong constitution, a high tolerance for Zooka Malt, and no outstanding gambling debts.
40|
41|Beneath the city lies [[The Undercity Osslurraggath]], an underground metropolis ignored by the urban elite and denied official recognition by the Nevercough Tribunal. It is home to [[The Mortuary]], the [[Dungsweepers]], exiles, criminals, and people the surface city would rather forget. Its provisional government has little legal authority, but it governs the people who live below. Osslurraggath began as bone vaults and necropolis tunnels before collapsing into deeper Underdark channels, creating a refuge for the poor, the diseased, the dead, and the unwanted. The [[Heralds of Dust]] established a philosophy of decay there.
42|
43|Beyond the city lies [[The Outback]], a largely unexplored wilderness where civilization gives way to ancient ruins, arcane forests, hidden rivers, swamps, bogs, mountains, beaches, and magical anomalies. [[Springwood]] is a massive naturalized park and sacred woodland that remains in an impossible state of spring. Its settlements include [[Kerning’s Crossing]], known for apothecaries and its reliance on the [[Solarium Botanica]]. 
44|
45|Farther out, [[Doobius House]] remains a humble frontier village inhabited mainly by indigenous [[Twothirdlings]] and a few full Halflings. Its former importance came from its role as the Gate to the Outback and from the military workshops established there during Elyrian expansion. The [[Grim Forest]] borders the village, its history preserved mainly through indigenous oral traditions. The forest contains hostile plants and undead, while an ancient awakened radiant tree guards its edge.
46|
47|The Outback also contains [[Zooka Mire]], a swamp just beyond the city limits where the [[Zooka Mire Collective]] operates, and the distant [[Molten Maw]], an underground volcanic city inhabited mainly by [[Duergar]] and [[Svirfneblin]]. Molten Maw’s Veins are semi-intelligent rivers of magical lava, while [[The Silt Road]] moves contraband, monster parts, forbidden magic, fugitives, and secrets beneath surface authorities. The Outback’s raw magic, combined with Mount Zooka’s influence, has made Stickyickistan a hotspot in the multiverse. For bounty hunters, smugglers, prospectors, and treasure seekers, its wilderness promises lost knowledge and untapped power. It also promises that something dangerous is always waiting beyond the city’s last road.
48|
49|# Past Stickyickistan
50|
51|Stickyickistan did not always have its current tropical climate. In earlier ages, the island maintained a more balanced pattern of hot and cold regions, as well as arid and humid zones. The northern part once held an ice cap, while the south resembled a Mediterranean climate more than a Caribbean one. Industrialization caused severe climate change. Rising temperatures melted the ice cap and turned some old-growth forests into desert. Recent conservation efforts have slowed the damage, but much of the original landscape has been lost.
52|
53|## [[Human Colonialism]]
54|
55|Long ago, the island’s humanoid inhabitants were small communities of [[Halflings]], [[Eladrin]], [[Goblins]], and [[Lizardfolk]]. Many followed a polytheistic faith devoted to [[The Three Sisters]], lived in close relationship with the land, and respected the creatures that shared it. The island flourished, its soil was fertile, and its forests teemed with life.
56|
57|That balance was disrupted when ambitious Human settlers arrived. Seeking control of the island’s resources, they treated the Halflings as obstacles and launched a violent invasion. The settlers established [[Nevercough City]] on what they called [[Nevercough Island]], forming the nation that would eventually become Stickyickistan.
58|
59|The Halflings resisted, but they were outnumbered and outmatched. Their leaders eventually negotiated for survival. The resulting pact granted them a protected enclave in what is now [[Upper South Booftown]] and acknowledged their right to participate in the new nation’s prosperity.
60|
61|The settlers later discovered [[Arcannabis]], an extraordinary plant whose magical properties became the foundation of the island’s economy. Properly cultivated, Arcannabis could heighten the senses, expand magical abilities, and reveal visions of unseen realms. [[Arcannabis Cultivation]] became a specialized tradition passed from generation to generation, and merchants soon traveled from distant lands to purchase the crop.
62|
63|Economic prosperity did not erase the divisions created by colonization. Human settlers and Halfling communities continued to live with distrust, cultural conflict, and unequal access to power. Over time, their traditions and technologies blended into a distinctive culture of music, art, food, and festivals. This cultural exchange created a shared identity, but racial tensions never disappeared entirely.
64|
65|Stickyickistan’s modern identity is therefore built on both coexistence and unresolved history. Its architecture, markets, and festivals reflect the fusion of Halfling traditions with Human innovation, while the island’s political institutions continue to bear the marks of conquest and resistance.
66|
67|## The Doobius House Resistance
68|
69|Stickyickistan was once a nation with several population centers rather than a single city-state. The main [[Human]] settlement on [[Nevercough Island]] was [[Nevercough City]], named for its patriarchal noble family. Across the [[Percolat Inlet]], [[Bongstad]] was carved into the base of [[Mount Zooka]]. The native [[Halfling]] reserve occupied land between a great lava river and the mountain’s slopes, where the terrain was barely habitable.
70|
71|Farther inland, [[Doobius House]] was founded by [[Duke Doobius Highblade]] as the “Gate to the Outback.” The frontier settlement attracted adventurers, prospectors, artificers, and others willing to live beyond the protection of the coastal communities. At its height, Doobius House rivaled [[Nevercough City]] and became famous for producing arcane ballistae and nature-infused war machines.
72|
73|Its frontier role gave Doobius House an unusual population. Elyrian settlers, native Halflings, craftspeople, hunters, and exiles lived beside one another, though not as equals. The Highblades claimed the land and profited from its workshops, while the Twothirdlings and other native communities supplied much of the local knowledge, labor, and military experience that kept the settlement alive.
74|
75|When [[Duke Doobius Highblade]] died, his Human heirs inherited the family’s formal authority and attempted to preserve the old order. The [[Twothirdlings]], who heavily outnumbered the Elyrian population around Doobius House, rejected that arrangement. Led by [[Jimmyjock Labingi]], the duke’s disinherited Twothirdling son, they seized the estate and surrounding settlement. They declared that Doobius House belonged to the people who had made it livable and defended it.
76|
77|Jimmyjock formed a provisional government and began negotiations with the Elyrian nobility of [[Nevercough City]]. The negotiations quickly failed. The nobles refused to recognize the Twothirdlings’ claim, while Jimmyjock refused to surrender the land or accept an arrangement that would leave his mother’s people subject to the family that had rejected him.
78|
79|## The [[Arcane Civil War]]
80|

1|A being of tempestuous laughter and boundless charisma, **Zahur al-Nasira** is more than just a Djinni Prince. He is the **Master of Mayhem**, the **Architect of Anarchy**, and the **Undisputed Host** of the most exhilarating game show in all the multiverse: **The League of Labyrinthia!**
2|
3|This one of my (Chase) DM alter egos. I like to imagine I become Zahur when I am behind the  screen. A true chaotic neutral, his domain exists within the plane of [[Limbo]]. A magnificent palace of marble, golden, and lapis lazuli held together by Zahur's will over the chaotic nature of Limbo. He is originally from the inner Elemental Plane of Air.
4|
5|

6|### **Appearance & Attire**
7|
8|Zahur’s form is as mutable as the winds. His body shimmers between solid and ethereal, his deep blue skin streaked with arcs of crackling lightning. His robes, woven from storm clouds and embroidered with golden filigree, billow even when there is no breeze. A crown of swirling mist and gemstones sits atop his head, and his piercing silver eyes gleam with mischief and wisdom.
9|

2|
3|An underground metropolis that is a part of the city of [[Stickyickistan]], but it is the underbelly of the city where [[The Mortuary]] is located, and where the [[Dungsweepers]] toil. Home to many undesirables, the elites of the city above mostly ignore the happenings of this under city. the under city has it's own provisional government, but holds no authority in the eyes of the Nevercough Tribunal.
4|
5|The Nevercough Tribunal refuses to acknowledge Osslurraggath, but every noble knows their waste doesn’t vanish by magic — it _goes somewhere._
6|
7|- When Stickyickistan grew into a great metropolis, the [[Nevercough Tribunal]] needed a place for the poor, the diseased, and the dishonored dead. They built vast **bone vaults** beneath the city to serve as its necropolis.
8|- These vaults eventually collapsed into deeper Underdark channels. What should have been a tomb became a **threshold**, spilling with refuse, plague-bodies, and exiles.
9|- Into this void stepped the **[[Heralds of Dust]]** — led by **[[Factol Skall]]**. They declared that all life in Stickyickistan was already death, and that Osslurraggath would be the sanctum where this truth was embraced.
10|The name Osslurraggath comes from the common word "Ossuary", and the Drow word "lurraggath" meaning love.

8|

15|## Chapter 1: Compromised Citadel
16|
17|As the party stands before the small citadel's door, Zardan warns that they may encounter unimaginable monstrosities and incomprehensible dangers, and that his brother may be dead, or, even worse, no longer himself. He takes a breath and opens the door.
18|
19|## A Brother's Fate
20|
21|You may read from the following text box to describe the Githzerai citadel's first floor to the party:
22|
23|> [!Read Aloud]
24|> You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in the center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you.
25|
26|**Githzerai Corpse.** If players choose to approach or investigate the figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in front of it. A DC 12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan recognizes this corpse as his brother and, given the evidence, believes that a red slaad killed him.
27|
28|### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo
29|
30|If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the following.
31|
32|Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses.
33|
34|The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called "chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad.
35|
36|Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274.
37|
38|## Slaad Encounter
39|
40|A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of value).
41|
42|The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their stomachs are obscenely swollen.
43|
44|If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison. Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM 276) wriggle onto the floor and attack the party.
45|
46|The party should easily finish this combat in 2 rounds; it is meant to provide them a false sense of confidence before encountering a real slaad threat. Zardan laments that all the Githzerai were infected, but is troubled that they haven't actually found the red slaad itself. As a side note, he wonders aloud what might have happened to the tadpole that spawned from his brother...
47|
48|### A Blue Slaad Enraged
49|
50|As the wizard finishes his thought, a blue slaad (MM 276) crashes down from a shadowy alcove of the high ceiling and cries out in rage at the sight of its slaughtered baby brothers. Its monstrous croaking is psychically translated in the party's brains as a vengeful vow that announces their doom.
51|
52|Blue Slaad Combat. The blue slaad fights to the death and specifically targets the characters that killed a tadpole with its claws. Through violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group, you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos.
53|
54|Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage.

# Curse of Slaad

*A Tier 1 [[Free League of Stickyickistan]] adventure for four to five 3rd-level characters*

## Being a Supposedly Competent Group of Warriors and Explorers

The adventure begins at the [[FLS Guildhall]] on [[Nevercough Island]], where a public contract has been posted for a planar investigation. The job is backed by [[N.E.R.D]], whose planar-studies faculty wants the party to investigate a failed research outpost beyond the city. The Free League considers the assignment a monster hunt; N.E.R.D considers it a field study; everyone else considers it an opportunity to avoid filling out the correct paperwork.

The party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan, a visiting planar-studies researcher associated with [[N.E.R.D]], to investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into [[Stickyickistan]]. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts in [[The Outback]], near the unstable magical wetlands of [[Zooka Mire]]. The outpost monitors planar disturbances and repels threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened.

**Beings of Order.** Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind flayers millennia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment, from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and hunt down alien monsters. N.E.R.D's scholars believe the Githzerai outpost was established near Zooka Mire because Mount Zooka's [[Arcanite]] deposits distort the Weave and make the region a useful early-warning station for planar breaches.

### Zardan, the Githzerai Wizard

Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat. He is brilliant, underfunded, and deeply uncomfortable with the way N.E.R.D students describe his work as "applied catastrophe."

Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard. His research at N.E.R.D focuses on planar boundaries, aberration incursions, and methods of safely extracting useful information from dangerous creatures.

Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is made.

Through violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group, you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos.
59|
60|Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage.
61|
62|### Grave Aftermath
63|
64|After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the *wish* spell, there is no way to stop this disease.
65|
66|But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes' aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be dire.
67|
68|Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass.
69|
70|The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items made up for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics other than the functional properties described above.

72|## CHAPTER 2: LIMBO MONASTERY
73|
74|**You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel when they first arrive in the plane of chaos:**
75|
76|> [!Read Aloud]
77|> You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound 
78|> 
79|> by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of chaos.
80|
81|### THE EVER-CHANGING CHAOS OF LIMBO
82|
83|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a DC14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table (DMG260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be dispelled with the calm emotions, lesser restoration, or remove curse spells, and it ends if the character takes a short rest. 
84|
85|The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share with your players. 
86|
87|>The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG62), while the Chaos Control features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind (DMG61-62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's roleplay or gameplay load.
88|
89|>**CHAOS CONTROL**
90|>
91|>Creatures in Limbo gain the following action options. 
92|>
93|>**Telekinesis**. You can spend an action to mentally move an object you can see that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you move the object 5 feet plus 1 foot for every point by which you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below. 
94|>
95|>**Transmutation**. You can spend an action to alter a nonmagical object you can see that isn't being worn or carried and that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you change the object into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder into a ball of fire). The number to beat is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below. 
96|>
97|>**Permanence**. You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for 24 hours, or until you use this ability again.

163|### The Pacifist's Hospitality
164|
165|If the party helps her eliminate the pesky chaos flumphs, Lez'lin expresses her gratitude. She is inclined to aid the disoriented newcomers, especially upon learning that her brother Zardan sent them. She seems unsurprised to learn that some party members are infected with chaos phage, pointing out that the slaad infection has visibly advanced to a critical stage.
166|
167|Indeed, the adventurers realize that the sudden exposure to Limbo's chaos aggravated the chaos phage. Their physical appearances become more toad-like, as determined randomly by the Chaos Phage Visible Symptoms table, and their hit point maximums are reduced by 3d6. They also become proficient with their Chaos Control features, meaning they can add their proficiency bonus to Wisdom checks made for the Telekinesis, Transmutation, and Permanence actions.

182|> **Lez'lin, the Githzerai Monk** 
183|> 
184|> Unlike her brother Zardan, Lez'lin possesses incredible mental fortitude  
185|> and thrived in the chaotic boil of Limbo. She adheres to the monastic  
186|> principles of her people, but her pacifist worldviews led her to isolate  
187|> herself from Githzerai communities. She is loath to cause harm to any  
188|> creature, no matter how vile or pesky, unless in self-defense. She lives  
189|> alone in her small monastery and strives to maintain its structural  
190|> integrity, so it may stand as a bastion of nonviolence. 
191|> 
192|> She recalls her brothers fondly, but hasn't seen them for many years  
193|> ever since they relocated to the Material Plane. News of Drarth's death  
194|> saddens her deeply, but she doesn't let her emotions cloud her focus on  
195|> the present. 
196| 
197|Lez'lin invites the party inside her foyer, where floating chairs provide enough comfort for a short rest while the Githzerai assesses their predicament. Other than the wish spell, she knows of only one way to cure chaos phage: a death slaad's magic. 
198|
199|### Death Slaadi and You
200|
201|Death slaadi are the peak of slaad evolution: stronger, viler, and more  
202|brutal, these monsters are corrupted by the Negative Energy Plane and  
203|take sadistic pleasure in killing and propagating slaadi dominance  
204|across dimensions. The only way to compel a death slaad to remove chaos  
205|phage is by acquiring its control gem, a magical fragment inside most  
206|slaadi's brains that allows whoever possesses it to subjugate the slaad.  
207|Removing the control gem is a near-impossible, very dangerous feat that  
208|can be approached in two ways: 
209|
210|1. The first method is a lengthy surgical procedure that can only be attempted if the slaad is incapacitated. A creature must spend 1 uninterrupted minute and succeed on a DC20 Medicine check to extract the gem. Every failed attempt deals 4d10 psychic damage to the slaad. 
211|2. A control gem can also be obtained through magical means, such as the 9th-level spell *imprisonment* (PHB 252–253). However, this spell takes 1 minute to cast and requires the caster to see the target and stay within 30 feet of it, and the spell is not guaranteed to succeed.
212|
213|In short, no matter the method they attempt, the party will undoubtedly  
214|need to incapacitate or restrain a live death slaad for 1 minute in  
215|order to acquire its control gem. Being a pacifist, Lez'lin won't  
216|directly help the party harm a living being, but she is willing to part  
217|with two legendary items that can help them, as long as they are able to  
218|secure the items themselves. 
219|
220|After they have rested, Lez'lin leads the party into the other half of  
221|her monastery, in which some of Limbo's chaos roils. 
222|
223|### Spell Scroll of Imprisonment
224|
225|The first legendary item provides a way to extract a slaad's control  
226|gem. It is protected by 3 layers, which must be removed sequentially to  
227|access it: 
228|
229|1. **First:** A Large ball of fire, which can be targeted with Transmutation or extinguished with 10 gallons of water (or any spell that could sensibly put out a large fire).
230|2. **Second:** A Medium hollow diamond, which can be transformed with Transmutation or cracked open with the *shatter* spell (PHB 275).
231|3. **Lastly:** A 2-foot-diameter sphere of annihilation (DMG 201) encases the spell scroll. A character can recognize this hole in the multiverse with a successful DC20 Arcana check (a result between 10 and 20 gives them the gist). The sphere and the spell scroll move independently of one another. A creature within 60 feet of the sphere can move it with a successful DC25 Arcana check. The distance moved is 5 × the creature's Intelligence modifier (minimum 5 feet). If a creature fails this check, the sphere moves 10 feet towards them. If the sphere enters a creature's space, that creature must make a DC13 Dexterity saving throw or touch it. A creature that voluntarily or involuntarily touches the sphere takes 4d10 force damage. The sphere can also be moved with a disadvantaged DC10 Telekinesis check. Moving the sphere of annihilation by at least 5 feet makes the spell scroll of imprisonment accessible. 
232|
233|**Using the Spell Scroll.** A low-level warlock or wizard can attempt to cast *imprisonment* (PHB 252–253) without the required components by reading the scroll. The user must first make a DC 19 saving throw (Charisma for warlocks and Intelligence for wizards). On a failed save, the scroll disintegrates. On a successful save, the user can cast the spell. If the target stays visible and within 30 feet of the caster for 1 minute, it must make a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw. If a targeted slaad fails this save, its control gem appears in the caster's hand. Whether the target fails or succeeds on its save, the scroll disintegrates. If the casting time is interrupted, nothing happens (see DMG 200 for more rules on spell scrolls).

508|## Appendix B: Chaotic Environments
509|
510|When running a combat encounter in the unstable plane of Limbo, you may want to bring extra chaos to the battlefield. Use the tables and steps below to introduce random matter shifts to the combat environment. First of all, separate the combat map into an appropriate number of equal-sized sections.
511|
512|1. Every time you introduce a new pocket of matter, select a random section of the battlefield in which it will appear, either by rolling a die, generating a random number, or choosing yourself. 
513|2. Roll on the Size of New Matter table. 
514|3. Roll on the Type of New Matter table. 
515|
516|If the selected section of the battlefield already contains matter, the new matter you are rolling for replaces it. If the matter would spawn in a creature's space, that creature is pushed into the nearest empty space.
