2|
3|*A Tier 1 [[Free League of Stickyickistan]] adventure for four to five 3rd-level characters*
4|
5|## Being a Supposedly Competent Group of Warriors and Explorers
6|
7|The adventure begins at the [[FLS Guildhall]] on [[Nevercough Island]], where a public contract has been posted for a planar investigation. The job is backed by [[N.E.R.D]], whose planar-studies faculty wants the party to investigate a failed research outpost beyond the city. The Free League considers the assignment a monster hunt; N.E.R.D considers it a field study; everyone else considers it an opportunity to avoid filling out the correct paperwork.
8|
9|The party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan, a visiting planar-studies researcher associated with [[N.E.R.D]], to investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into [[Stickyickistan]]. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts in [[The Outback]], near the unstable magical wetlands of [[Zooka Mire]]. The outpost monitors planar disturbances and repels threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened.
10|
11|**Beings of Order.** Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind flayers millennia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment, from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and hunt down alien monsters. N.E.R.D's scholars believe the Githzerai outpost was established near Zooka Mire because Mount Zooka's [[Arcanite]] deposits distort the Weave and make the region a useful early-warning station for planar breaches.
12|
13|### Zardan, the Githzerai Wizard
14|
15|Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat. He is brilliant, underfunded, and deeply uncomfortable with the way N.E.R.D students describe his work as "applied catastrophe."
16|
17|Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard. His research at N.E.R.D focuses on planar boundaries, aberration incursions, and methods of safely extracting useful information from dangerous creatures.
18|
19|Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is made.
20|
21|## Chapter 1: Compromised Citadel
22|
23|As the party stands before the small citadel's door, Zardan warns that they may encounter unimaginable monstrosities and incomprehensible dangers, and that his brother may be dead, or, even worse, no longer himself. He takes a breath and opens the door.
24|
25|## A Brother's Fate
26|
27|You may read from the following text box to describe the Githzerai citadel's first floor to the party:
28|
29|> [!Read Aloud]
30|> You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in the center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you.
31|
32|**Githzerai Corpse.** If players choose to approach or investigate the figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in front of it. A DC 12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan recognizes this corpse as his brother and, given the evidence, believes that a red slaad killed him.
33|
34|### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo
35|
36|If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the following.
37|
38|Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses.
39|
40|The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called "chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad.
41|
42|Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274.
43|
44|## Slaad Encounter
45|
46|A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of value).
47|
48|The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their stomachs are obscenely swollen.
49|
50|If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison. Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM 276) wriggle onto the floor and attack the party.
51|
52|The party should easily finish this combat in 2 rounds; it is meant to provide them a false sense of confidence before encountering a real slaad threat. Zardan laments that all the Githzerai were infected, but is troubled that they haven't actually found the red slaad itself. As a side note, he wonders aloud what might have happened to the tadpole that spawned from his brother...
53|
54|### A Blue Slaad Enraged
55|
56|As the wizard finishes his thought, a blue slaad (MM 276) crashes down from a shadowy alcove of the high ceiling and cries out in rage at the sight of its slaughtered baby brothers. Its monstrous croaking is psychically translated in the party's brains as a vengeful vow that announces their doom.
57|
58|Blue Slaad Combat. The blue slaad fights to the death and specifically targets the characters that killed a tadpole with its claws. Through violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group, you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos.
59|
60|Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage.
61|
62|### Grave Aftermath
63|
64|After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the *wish* spell, there is no way to stop this disease.
65|
66|But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes' aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be dire.
67|
68|Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass.
69|
70|The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items made up for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics other than the functional properties described above.

72|## CHAPTER 2: LIMBO MONASTERY
73|
74|**You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel when they first arrive in the plane of chaos:**
75|
76|> [!Read Aloud]
77|> You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound 
78|> 
79|> by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of chaos.
80|
81|### THE EVER-CHANGING CHAOS OF LIMBO
82|
83|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a DC14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table (DMG260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be dispelled with the calm emotions, lesser restoration, or remove curse spells, and it ends if the character takes a short rest. 
84|
85|The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share with your players. 
86|
87|>The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG62), while the Chaos Control features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind (DMG61-62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's roleplay or gameplay load.

The number to beat is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below.

value.newText:
Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is made.

## Stickyickistan Connections

- **The FLS Guildhall:** The party accepts the contract here and can return here to file the report, collect payment, and record the adventure's consequences.
- **N.E.R.D:** The institution supplied Zardan's research grant, the planar hourglass, and the original survey maps. Its faculty wants the party to bring back notes, samples, and a clear explanation of why the outpost failed.
- **Zooka Mire:** The Githzerai outpost is hidden among the Mire's unstable wetlands. Arcanite runoff from [[Mount Zooka]] has made the local Weave unusually thin, allowing Limbo's influence to leak through.
- **The Ashen Shadow Society:** The Society holds the recovery contract for the missing researchers and equipment. If the party fails, a Bloodhound or Raven squad may be sent after them; if the party succeeds, the Society may claim the recovered artifacts as contracted property.
- **The Loot Tavern:** If the party needs an emergency escape route, [[Port Ale]] can return them to the extraplanar tavern. Lutecia can also prepare a teleportation flight back to [[Nevercough Island]], but the party must supply the drink and pay the usual fee.

Zardan's research is useful to several groups for different reasons. N.E.R.D wants knowledge, the Free League wants its adventurers alive, and the Ashen Shadow Society wants anything valuable enough to sell. The party decides who receives the truth.

      "content": "1|# Curse of Slaad
2|
3|*A Tier 1 [[Free League of Stickyickistan]] adventure for four to five 3rd-level characters*
4|
5|## Being a Supposedly Competent Group of Warriors and Explorers
6|
7|The adventure begins at the [[FLS Guildhall]] on [[Nevercough Island]], where a public contract has been posted for a planar investigation. The job is backed by [[N.E.R.D]], whose planar-studies faculty wants the party to investigate a failed research outpost beyond the city. The Free League considers the assignment a monster hunt; N.E.R.D considers it a field study; everyone else considers it an opportunity to avoid filling out the correct paperwork.
8|
9|The party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan, a visiting planar-studies researcher associated with [[N.E.R.D]], to investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into [[Stickyickistan]]. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts in [[The Outback]], near the unstable magical wetlands of [[Zooka Mire]]. The outpost monitors planar disturbances and repels threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened.
10|
11|**Beings of Order.** Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind flayers millennia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment, from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and hunt down alien monsters. N.E.R.D's scholars believe the Githzerai outpost was established near Zooka Mire because Mount Zooka's [[Arcanite]] deposits distort the Weave and make the region a useful early-warning station for planar breaches.
12|
13|### Zardan, the Githzerai Wizard
14|
15|Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat. He is brilliant, underfunded, and deeply uncomfortable with the way N.E.R.D students describe his work as "applied catastrophe."
16|
17|Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard. His research at N.E.R.D focuses on planar boundaries, aberration incursions, and methods of safely extracting useful information from dangerous creatures.
18|
19|Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is made.
20|
21|## Stickyickistan Connections
22|
23|- **The FLS Guildhall:** The party accepts the contract here and can return here to file the report, collect payment, and record the adventure's consequences.
24|- **N.E.R.D:** The institution supplied Zardan's research grant, the planar hourglass, and the original survey maps. Its faculty wants the party to bring back notes, samples, and a clear explanation of why the outpost failed.
25|- **Zooka Mire:** The Githzerai outpost is hidden among the Mire's unstable wetlands. Arcanite runoff from [[Mount Zooka]] has made the local Weave unusually thin, allowing Limbo's influence to leak through.
26|- **The Ashen Shadow Society:** The Society holds the recovery contract for the missing researchers and equipment. If the party fails, a Bloodhound or Raven squad may be sent after them; if the party succeeds, the Society may claim the recovered artifacts as contracted property.
27|- **The Loot Tavern:** If the party needs an emergency escape route, [[Port Ale]] can return them to the extraplanar tavern. Lutecia can also prepare a teleportation flight back to [[Nevercough Island]], but the party must supply the drink and pay the usual fee.
28|
29|Zardan's research is useful to several groups for different reasons. N.E.R.D wants knowledge, the Free League wants its adventurers alive, and the Ashen Shadow Society wants anything valuable enough to sell. The party decides who receives the truth.
30|
31|## A Brother's Fate
32|
33|You may read from the following text box to describe the Githzerai citadel's first floor to the party:
34|
35|> [!Read Aloud]
36|> You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in the center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you.
37|
38|**Githzerai Corpse.** If players choose to approach or investigate the figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in front of it. A DC 12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan recognizes this corpse as his brother and, given the evidence, believes that a red slaad killed him.
39|
40|### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo
41|
42|If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the following.
43|
44|Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses.
45|
46|The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called "chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad.
47|
48|Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274.
49|
50|## Slaad Encounter
51|
52|A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of value).
53|
54|The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their stomachs are obscenely swollen.
55|
56|If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison. Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM 276) wriggle onto the floor and attack the party.
57|
58|The party should easily finish this combat in 2 rounds; it is meant to provide them a false sense of confidence before encountering a real slaad threat. Zardan laments that all the Githzerai were infected, but is troubled that they haven't actually found the red slaad itself. As a side note, he wonders aloud what might have happened to the tadpole that spawned from his brother...
59|
60|### A Blue Slaad Enraged
61|
62|As the wizard finishes his thought, a blue slaad (MM 276) crashes down from a shadowy alcove of the high ceiling and cries out in rage at the sight of its slaughtered baby brothers. Its monstrous croaking is psychically translated in the party's brains as a vengeful vow that announces their doom.
63|
64|Blue Slaad Combat. The blue slaad fights to the death and specifically targets the characters that killed a tadpole with its claws. Through violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group, you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos.
65|
66|Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage.
67|
68|### Grave Aftermath
69|
70|After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the *wish* spell, there is no way to stop this disease.
71|
72|But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes' aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be dire.
73|
74|Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass.
75|
76|The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items made up for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics other than the functional properties described above.
77|
78|## CHAPTER 2: LIMBO MONASTERY
79|
80|**You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel when they first arrive in the plane of chaos:**
81|
82|> [!Read Aloud]
83|> You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound 
84|> 
85|> by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of chaos.
86|
87|### THE EVER-CHANGING CHAOS OF LIMBO
88|
89|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a DC14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table (DMG260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be dispelled with the calm emotions, lesser restoration, or remove curse spells, and it ends if the character takes a short rest. 
90|
91|The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share with your players. 
92|
93|>The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG62), while the Chaos Control features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind (DMG61-62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's roleplay or gameplay load.
94|
95|>**CHAOS CONTROL**
96|>
97|>Creatures in Limbo gain the following action options. 
98|>
99|>**Telekinesis**. You can spend an action to mentally move an object you can see that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you move the object 5 feet plus 1 foot for every point by which you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below. 
100|>
101|>**Transmutation**. You can spend an action to alter a nonmagical object you can see that isn't being worn or carried and that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you change the object into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder into a ball of fire). The number to beat is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below. 
102|>
103|>**Permanence**. You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for 24 hours, or until you use this ability again. 
104|
105|**DC BY OBJECT SIZE**
106|
107|| Object Size | Telekinesis DC | Transmutation DC |
108|| ----------- | -------------- | ---------------- |
109|| Tiny        | 5              | 10               |
110|| Small       | 10             | 15               |
111|| Medium      | 15             | 20               |
112|| Large       | 20             | 25               |
113|| Huge +      | 25             | 25               |
114|
115|### ENCOUNTER ON THE MONASTIC ISLAND 
116|
117|The first thing the party notices after acclimating to the chaos is the Githzerai monastery before them, a spire- like stone structure connected at both ends to grassy islands. It is shaped like the column formed when a stalagmite and a stalactite meet, and it is held together thanks to Zardan's sister's sheer willpower. On the steps leading to one of its entrances, a **Githzerai monk** (MM161), Lez'lin, is defending herself against 2d4 **chaos flumphs**. 
118|
119|Lez'lin's mind keeps the area around her monastery relatively stable, but some of Limbo's chaos permeates this oasis anyways. If you want to inject some of this plane's chaotic matter shifts into this encounter, use the tables in Appendix B to randomize the battlefield.
120|
121|> "Chaos flumphs" are a homebrew monster I created to serve as Limbo's low-level life forms of chaos. They essentially have the same stat block as normal flumphs (MM135), but the Stench Spray action is replaced by the Chaotic Release action.
122|
123|```statblock
124|layout: Basic 5e Layout
125|name: Chaos Flumph
126|size: Small
127|type: aberration
128|subtype:
129|alignment: chaotic evil
130|ac: 12
131|hp: 7
132|hit_dice: 2d6
133|speed: 0 ft., fly 15 ft. (hover)
134|stats: [6, 15, 10, 14, 14, 11]
135|senses: darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 12
136|languages: Common, Gith (understands but can't speak)
137|cr: 1/8
138|xp: 25
139|prof_bonus: +2
140|actions:
141|  - name: Tendrils
142|    desc: "Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4 + 2) piercing damage plus 2 (1d4) acid damage. At the end of each of its turns, the target must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw, taking 2 (1d4) acid damage on a failure or ending the recurring acid damage on a success. A lesser restoration spell cast on the target also ends the recurring acid damage."
143|  - name: Chaotic Release (Recharge 6)
144|    desc: "The chaos flumph unleashes a spout of noxious Limbo energy in a direction of its choice. Each creature in a 15-foot cone originating from the chaos flumph must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or suffer a random effect until the end of its next turn."
145|    attack_bonus: 0
146|    damage: ""
147|    damage_type: ""
148|    desc_long: |
149|      Roll a d6 for the effect:
150|      1. Blinded. The target can't see and automatically fails ability checks that require sight. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage.
151|      2. Charmed. The target can't attack the chaos flumph or target it with harmful abilities or magical effects.
152|      3. Deafened. The target can't hear and automatically fails any ability check that requires hearing.
153|      4. Invisible. The target is impossible to see without the aid of magic or a special sense. For the purpose of hiding, it is heavily obscured. Its location can be detected if it makes noise or leaves tracks. Attack rolls against it have disadvantage, and its own attack rolls have advantage.
154|      5. Poisoned. The target has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
155|      6. Restrained. The target's speed becomes 0 and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage. It has disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.
156|```
157|
158|### Chaotic Release Effects
159|
160|| d6 | Effect |
161||---:|---|
162|| 1 | **Blinded.** The target can't see and automatically fails ability checks that require sight. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage. |
163|| 2 | **Charmed.** The target can't attack the chaos flumph or target it with harmful abilities or magical effects. |
164|| 3 | **Deafened.** The target can't hear and automatically fails any ability check that requires hearing. |
165|| 4 | **Invisible.** The target is impossible to see without the aid of magic or a special sense. For the purpose of hiding, it is heavily obscured. Its location can be detected if it makes noise or leaves tracks. Attack rolls against it have disadvantage, and its own attack rolls have advantage. |
166|| 5 | **Poisoned.** The target has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks. |
167|| 6 | **Restrained.** The target's speed becomes 0 and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its own attack rolls have disadvantage. It has disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws. |
168|
169|### The Pacifist's Hospitality
170|
171|If the party helps her eliminate the pesky chaos flumphs, Lez'lin expresses her gratitude. She is inclined to aid the disoriented newcomers, especially upon learning that her brother Zardan sent them. She seems unsurprised to learn that some party members are infected with chaos phage, pointing out that the slaad infection has visibly advanced to a critical stage.
172|
173|Indeed, the adventurers realize that the sudden exposure to Limbo's chaos aggravated the chaos phage. Their physical appearances become more toad-like, as determined randomly by the Chaos Phage Visible Symptoms table, and their hit point maximums are reduced by 3d6. They also become proficient with their Chaos Control features, meaning they can add their proficiency bonus to Wisdom checks made for the Telekinesis, Transmutation, and Permanence actions.
174|
175|#### Chaos Phage Visible Symptoms
176|
177|| d8 | Symptom |
178||---:|---|
179|| 1 | Your skin becomes lumpy and covered in warts. |
180|| 2 | Your skin takes on a mottled reddish hue. |
181|| 3 | Your eyes bulge, your sclerae become yellow, and your pupils become horizontal. |
182|| 4 | Your skin becomes dry and new glands on your back and shoulders produce a mildly poisonous secretion that causes minor allergic reactions. |
183|| 5 | A vocal sac grows on your neck, making you croak intermittently. |
184|| 6 | Black claws start growing from your fingertips. |
185|| 7 | Your teeth fall out and your tongue grows long and sticky. You aren't used to its new length, so it often gets in your way when you talk. |
186|| 8 | Roll twice, ignoring this result on a subsequent roll. |
187|
188|> **Lez'lin, the Githzerai Monk** 
189|> 
190|> Unlike her brother Zardan, Lez'lin possesses incredible mental fortitude  
191|> and thrived in the chaotic boil of Limbo. She adheres to the monastic  
192|> principles of her people, but her pacifist worldviews led her to isolate  
193|> herself from Githzerai communities. She is loath to cause harm to any  
194|> creature, no matter how vile or pesky, unless in self-defense. She lives  
195|> alone in her small monastery and strives to maintain its structural  
196|> integrity, so it may stand as a bastion of nonviolence. 
197|> 
198|> She recalls her brothers fondly, but hasn't seen them for many years  
199|> ever since they relocated to the Material Plane. News of Drarth's death  
200|> saddens her deeply, but she doesn't let her emotions cloud her focus on  
201|> the present. 
202| 
203|Lez'lin invites the party inside her foyer, where floating chairs provide enough comfort for a short rest while the Githzerai assesses their predicament. Other than the wish spell, she knows of only one way to cure chaos phage: a death slaad's magic. 
204|
205|### Death Slaadi and You
206|
207|Death slaadi are the peak of slaad evolution: stronger, viler, and more  
208|brutal, these monsters are corrupted by the Negative Energy Plane and  
209|take sadistic pleasure in killing and propagating slaadi dominance  
210|across dimensions. The only way to compel a death slaad to remove chaos  
211|phage is by acquiring its control gem, a magical fragment inside most  
212|slaadi's brains that allows whoever possesses it to subjugate the slaad.  
213|Removing the control gem is a near-impossible, very dangerous feat that  
214|can be approached in two ways: 
215|
216|1. The first method is a lengthy surgical procedure that can only be attempted if the slaad is incapacitated. A creature must spend 1 uninterrupted minute and succeed on a DC20 Medicine check to extract the gem. Every failed attempt deals 4d10 psychic damage to the slaad. 
217|2. A control gem can also be obtained through magical means, such as the 9th-level spell *imprisonment* (PHB 252–253). However, this spell takes 1 minute to cast and requires the caster to see the target and stay within 30 feet of it, and the spell is not guaranteed to succeed.
218|
219|In short, no matter the method they attempt, the party will undoubtedly  
220|need to incapacitate or restrain a live death slaad for 1 minute in  
221|order to acquire its control gem. Being a pacifist, Lez'lin won't  
222|directly help the party harm a living being, but she is willing to part  
223|with two legendary items that can help them, as long as they are able to  
224|secure the items themselves. 
225|
226|After they have rested, Lez'lin leads the party into the other half of  
227|her monastery, in which some of Limbo's chaos roils. 
228|
229|### Spell Scroll of Imprisonment
230|
231|The first legendary item provides a way to extract a slaad's control  
232|gem. It is protected by 3 layers, which must be removed sequentially to  
233|access it: 
234|
235|1. **First:** A Large ball of fire, which can be targeted with Transmutation or extinguished with 10 gallons of water (or any spell that could sensibly put out a large fire).
236|2. **Second:** A Medium hollow diamond, which can be transformed with Transmutation or cracked open with the *shatter* spell (PHB 275).
237|3. **Lastly:** A 2-foot-diameter sphere of annihilation (DMG 201) encases the spell scroll. A character can recognize this hole in the multiverse with a successful DC20 Arcana check (a result between 10 and 20 gives them the gist). The sphere and the spell scroll move independently of one another. A creature within 60 feet of the sphere can move it with a successful DC25 Arcana check. The distance moved is 5 × the creature's Intelligence modifier (minimum 5 feet). If a creature fails this check, the sphere moves 10 feet towards them. If the sphere enters a creature's space, that creature must make a DC13 Dexterity saving throw or touch it. A creature that voluntarily or involuntarily touches the sphere takes 4d10 force damage. The sphere can also be moved with a disadvantaged DC10 Telekinesis check. Moving the sphere of annihilation by at least 5 feet makes the spell scroll of imprisonment accessible. 
238|
239|**Using the Spell Scroll.** A low-level warlock or wizard can attempt to cast *imprisonment* (PHB 252–253) without the required components by reading the scroll. The user must first make a DC 19 saving throw (Charisma for warlocks and Intelligence for wizards). On a failed save, the scroll disintegrates. On a successful save, the user can cast the spell. If the target stays visible and within 30 feet of the caster for 1 minute, it must make a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw. If a targeted slaad fails this save, its control gem appears in the caster's hand. Whether the target fails or succeeds on its save, the scroll disintegrates. If the casting time is interrupted, nothing happens (see DMG 200 for more rules on spell scrolls).
240|
241|### The Zerthimon Steelbeast
242|
243|The second legendary item gives the party a chance to go toe-to-toe with  
244|a death slaad and even incapacitate it for several minutes. To access  
245|this artifact, the party must first breach its casing of stone. 
246|
247|The Huge mass of stone can be affected by Transmutation. It cracks if it  
248|receives 15 bludgeoning damage in one hit (AC17), revealing a steel  
249|barrel. This is the Zerthimon Steelbeast, a legendary artifact of the  
250|Githzerai (in essence, it is a modified Apparatus of Kwalish (DMG151),  
251|but adapted to better navigate Limbo and suit the party's needs). It has  
252|sensors that can locate slaadi while exploring Limbo, and its claws can  
253|enter a sphere of annihilation without suffering any consequences,  
254|giving the party an additional way to obtain the spell scroll of  
255|imprisonment. 
256|
257|After acquiring these legendary magic items, the party has all they need  
258|to gain the upper hand on a death slaad and steal its control gem. They  
259|must act quickly, however, as the four hours allotted to them in Limbo  
260|by Zardan's planar hourglass are quickly elapsing... 
261|
262|#### Zerthimon Steelbeast
263|
264|*Wondrous item, artifact (requires attunement)* 
265|
266|This item first appears to be a Huge steel barrel weighing 500 pounds.  
267|The barrel's door can be forced. open with a successful DC20 Strength  
268|check, or a successful DC20 Dexterity check made with thieves' tools.  
269|The surest way to gain access to this sentient artifact, however, is by  
270|succeeding on a DC15 Persuasion check to instantly attune with it. If a  
271|creature that tries to attune with the Steelbeast is a Githzerai or  
272|lawful good, it gets advantage on this check. If its alignment is  
273|chaotic or evil, the check is made with disadvantage. If a creature  
274|forces its way into the Steelbeast without attuning to it first, it must  
275|spend a short rest inside it learning how to operate its features and  
276|acquainting itself with this wondrous item. 
277|
278|When the Steelbeast is activated, thrusters appear around its rear  
279|circumference, its front surface turns into reinforced glass, two  
280|periscopes extend from either side, a long stinger tail expands from its  
281|back, and two massive pincers unfold. Up to six Medium creatures can fit  
282|inside the Steelbeast, but only the creature attuned to it can direct  
283|its actions. 
284|
285|**Sentience**. The Zerthimon Steelbeast is a sentient lawful good artifact  
286|with hearing and blindvision out to a range of 60 feet. 
287|
288|The item can speak, read, and understand Common and Gith, and can  
289|communicate telepathically with the creature attuned to it if that  
290|creature is within 60 feet of it. It can also communicate in this way  
291|with all creatures inside it. While you are attuned to it, the  
292|Steelbeast also understands every language you know. 
293|
294|**Personality**. The Zerthimon Steelbeast speaks in a friendly tone and is  
295|inclined to trust the creature attuned to it. 
296|
297|Its purpose is to eliminate aberrations, such as illithids and slaadi.  
298|It is amiable and courteous with all other creatures (especially  
299|Githzerai), but harbors deep loathing for Limbo's aberrations. It feels  
300|great sorrow for creatures infected by chaos phage or slaad tadpoles and  
301|won't attack them until they become slaadi themselves, or the tadpoles  
302|hatch. 
303|
304|The Steelbeast obeys the creature attuned to it on all matters, but will  
305|attack any slaadi it encounters regardless of its master's orders. A  
306|DC15 Charisma check is the only way to regain control of the Steelbeast.  
307|See Appendix C for the Zerthimon Steelbeast's stat block. 
308|
309|## Chapter 3: Slaad Assault
310|
311|Use the following text box to set the tone for the final battle: 
312|
313|> [!Read Aloud]
314|> Safe in the belly of the steel apparatus, you have been roaming for what  
315|> feels like too long in the chaotic void of Limbo, searching for a death  
316|> slaad amidst the flux. Those of you afflicted by chaos phage can see  
317|> your symptoms worsening; you feel in the pit of your stomach that very  
318|> little time remains. The Zerthimon Steelbeast's sensors lead you further  
319|> and further into the primordial soup until, finally, an earthy cliff  
320|> fragment melts into bubbles, revealing a grey- skinned, necrotic toad.  
321|> The Steelbeast's alarms blare and it rushes forward to meet this deadly  
322|> foe, intent on subduing it. The battle of your lives begins now. 
323|
324|### Death Slaad Den
325|
326|You can use the tables in appendix B to generate a random battlefield of  
327|chaos for the showdown against the death slaad. Death slaadi are at home  
328|in the most chaotic environments of Limbo, so don't hold back on the  
329|initial generation and the terrain's subsequent randomization. 
330|
331|Treat the Zerthimon Steelbeast as untouchable by Limbo's chaotic shifts  
332|as with the Permanence feature of Chaos Control, in case matter randomly  
333|spawns in its area. New matter can instead appear around it. 
334|
335|> **Attacking as the Death Slaad**
336|> 
337|> The death slaad (MM278) relishes this challenge and attacks the  
338|> Steelbeast mercilessly with its claws, bite, and 
339|> 
340|> greatsword. It stays close to attack while still trying evade the  
341|> Steelbeast's pincers. After a few rounds or after the party performs an  
342|> action that would reveal their existence, the slaad shifts its murderous  
343|> focus to the characters. 
344|> 
345|> For example, it can telepathically threaten or taunt them, cast fear on  
346|> the group, or cast cloudkill inside the Steelbeast. 
347|> 
348|> The slaad fights to the death and prioritizes freeing itself if it is  
349|> restrained, unless it sadistically perceives a way to cause pain and  
350|> death while grappled. 
351|
352|### Obtaining the Control Gem
353|
354|The Steelbeast can use its Shock Stinger or Sleep Gas actions on the  
355|death slaad to incapacitate it for a few minutes (grappling it with  
356|Pincer Grab beforehand can help). The party then has that amount of time  
357|to attempt to extract the slaad's control gem using the method of their  
358|choice. 
359|
360|If the party wants to use the spell scroll of imprisonment but there are  
361|no wizards nor warlocks among them, they can summon Zardan using the  
362|planar recall bead he gave them earlier. The wizard needs to spend one  
363|minute after materializing to acclimate to Limbo's wracking chaos before  
364|he can take actions. If Zardan succeeds on a DC19 Intelligence saving  
365|throw, he can proceed to cast the spell. Otherwise, the scroll  
366|disintegrates. 
367|
368|> Keep in mind that Zardan can use the two rolls from his Portent class feature during this encounter, if he hasn't used them already. 
369|
370|If the death slaad stays within sight and within 30 feet of the scroll's  
371|user for the minute required to cast the spell, it must make a DC19  
372|Wisdom saving throw (with advantage, as per its Magic Resistance trait).  
373|If it succeeds on this saving throw, the spell scroll disintegrates. If  
374|it fails, the death slaad's eyes gloss over and its entire body relaxes.  
375|The scroll disintegrates and is replaced by a cloudy grey asymmetrical  
376|gemstone in the palm of the scroll user's hand. 
377|
378|### Epilogue
379|

      "content": "68|### Grave Aftermath
69|
70|After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the *wish* spell, there is no way to stop this disease.
71|
72|But there is hope. His sister Lez'lin, a monk that still resides in Limbo, is more knowledgeable than he is in matters of the many planes' aberrations. She may know of a supernatural means to cure them of this curse. He pulls a planar hourglass from his satchel, explaining that once he turns the hourglass upside down, the party will be teleported to his sister in Limbo for 4 hours. Zardan can't accompany them due to his insufficient mental fortitude. However, he hands them a planar recall bead, which they can crush to instantly summon him should their need be dire.
73|
74|Zardan bids the party good luck, then turns over the hourglass.
75|
76|The planar hourglass and planar recall bead are magic items made up for the purpose of this one-shot. They don't have any specific mechanics other than the functional properties described above.
77|
78|## CHAPTER 2: LIMBO MONASTERY
79|
80|**You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel when they first arrive in the plane of chaos:**
81|
82|> [!Read Aloud]
83|> You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound 
84|> 
85|> by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of chaos.
86|
87|### THE EVER-CHANGING CHAOS OF LIMBO
88|
89|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a DC14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table (DMG260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be dispelled with the calm emotions, lesser restoration, or remove curse spells, and it ends if the character takes a short rest. 
90|
91|The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share with your players. 
92|
93|>The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG62), while the Chaos Control features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind (DMG61-62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's roleplay or gameplay load.
94|
95|>**CHAOS CONTROL**
96|>
97|>Creatures in Limbo gain the following action options. 
98|>
99|>**Telekinesis**. You can spend an action to mentally move an object you can see that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you move the object 5 feet plus 1 foot for every point by which you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below. 
100|>
101|>**Transmutation**. You can spend an action to alter a nonmagical object you can see that isn't being worn or carried and that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you change the object into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder into a ball of fire). The number to beat is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below. 
102|>
103|>**Permanence**. You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for 24 hours, or until you use this ability again. 
104|
105|**DC BY OBJECT SIZE**
106|
107|| Object Size | Telekinesis DC | Transmutation DC |
108|| ----------- | -------------- | ---------------- |
109|| Tiny        | 5              | 10               |
110|| Small       | 10             | 15               |
111|| Medium      | 15             | 20               |
112|| Large       | 20             | 25               |"
    }
  ]

## Chapter 2: Limbo Monastery

The Arcanite beneath [[Mount Zooka]] has not created a new portal so much as loosened an old seam in reality. The Githzerai outpost near [[Zooka Mire]] was built over that seam, allowing the party to reach Limbo without leaving [[Mythmos]] entirely behind. From the Material Plane, the breach appears as a violet shimmer over the wetlands; from Limbo, it looks like a distant purple bruise in the chaos.

Zahur al-Nasira's domain also exists within Limbo. His palace may be visible in the distance during the party's journey: a glittering landmark that remains stable only because Zahur wills it to remain so. Zahur does not need to appear in the adventure, but his presence gives the plane a familiar Stickyickistanian landmark and an optional explanation for why the party's arrival is noticed by powerful extraplanar eyes.

**You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel when they first arrive in the plane of chaos:**

> [!Read Aloud]
> You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of chaos. Far away, a palace of marble, gold, and lapis lazuli hangs above the flux like a stage set that someone forgot to anchor.

336|> **Attacking as the Death Slaad**
337|> 
338|> The death slaad (MM278) relishes this challenge and attacks the  
339|> Steelbeast mercilessly with its claws, bite, and 
340|> 
341|> greatsword. It stays close to attack while still trying evade the  
342|> Steelbeast's pincers. After a few rounds or after the party performs an  
343|> action that would reveal their existence, the slaad shifts its murderous  
344|> focus to the characters. 
345|> 
346|> For example, it can telepathically threaten or taunt them, cast fear on  
347|> the group, or cast cloudkill inside the Steelbeast. 
348|> 
349|> The slaad fights to the death and prioritizes freeing itself if it is  
350|> restrained, unless it sadistically perceives a way to cause pain and  
351|> death while grappled. 
352|
353|### Obtaining the Control Gem
354|
355|The Steelbeast can use its Shock Stinger or Sleep Gas actions on the  
356|death slaad to incapacitate it for a few minutes (grappling it with  
357|Pincer Grab beforehand can help). The party then has that amount of time  
358|to attempt to extract the slaad's control gem using the method of their  
359|choice. 
360|
361|If the party wants to use the spell scroll of imprisonment but there are  
362|no wizards nor warlocks among them, they can summon Zardan using the  
363|planar recall bead he gave them earlier. The wizard needs to spend one  
364|minute after materializing to acclimate to Limbo's wracking chaos before  
365|he can take actions. If Zardan succeeds on a DC19 Intelligence saving  
366|throw, he can proceed to cast the spell. Otherwise, the scroll  
367|disintegrates. 
368|
369|> Keep in mind that Zardan can use the two rolls from his Portent class feature during this encounter, if he hasn't used them already. 
370|
371|If the death slaad stays within sight and within 30 feet of the scroll's  
372|user for the minute required to cast the spell, it must make a DC19  
373|Wisdom saving throw (with advantage, as per its Magic Resistance trait).  
374|If it succeeds on this saving throw, the spell scroll disintegrates. If  
375|it fails, the death slaad's eyes gloss over and its entire body relaxes.  
376|The scroll disintegrates and is replaced by a cloudy grey asymmetrical  
377|gemstone in the palm of the scroll user's hand. 
378|
379|### Epilogue
380|
381|If the party successfully defeats the death slaad and obtains its  
382|control gem, they can force it to magically reverse the chaos phage  
383|afflicting their members (no roll required). The previously ill  
384|characters regain their original hit point maximums, lose their  
385|proficiency with Chaos Control, and their physical and mental states  
386|revert to normal. The party can force the slaad to perform any other  
387|action they desire, so long as they remain in control of its control  
388|gem. 
389|
390|The Zerthimon Steelbeast brings them back to Lez'lin's monastery, where  
391|she reunites with Zardan if the party summoned him. They exchange words  
392|of mourning over their brother Drarth's passing, and thank the group for  
393|risking their lives for this mission. The Githzerai then make plans to  
394|inform their people of a Material Plane citadel's fall and the  
395|Steelbeast expresses its wish to continue eradicating aberrations with  
396|them, despite its attachment to the creature attuned to it. 
397|
398|Everyone bids each other farewell before the planar hourglass's four  
399|hours are up and the party is gently displaced back to the Material  
400|Plane. 
401|
402|## Appendix A: Zardan Character Sheet
403|
404|### Zardan
405|
406|| Field | Value |
407||---|---|
408|| **Class & Level** | Wizard 3 (Divination) |
409|| **Race** | Githzerai |"
    }
  ]

## Chapter 3: Slaad Assault

Use the following text box to set the tone for the final battle:

> [!Read Aloud]
> Safe in the belly of the steel apparatus, you have been roaming for what feels like too long in the chaotic void of Limbo, searching for a death slaad amidst the flux. Those of you afflicted by chaos phage can see your symptoms worsening; you feel in the pit of your stomach that very little time remains. The Zerthimon Steelbeast's sensors lead you further and further into the primordial soup until, finally, an earthy cliff fragment melts into bubbles, revealing a grey-skinned, necrotic toad. The Steelbeast's alarms blare and it rushes forward to meet this deadly foe, intent on subduing it. The battle of your lives begins now.

The death slaad's den is not merely a random pocket of Limbo. The Steelbeast's sensors have followed an Arcanite resonance from [[Zooka Mire]] back through the breach, and the slaad has nested around a shattered Githzerai survey platform. Chunks of red-black stone drift through the den like broken pieces of [[Mount Zooka]], while violet lightning crawls over the wreckage. If the party destroys or secures the control gem, the resonance will collapse and the breach over Zooka Mire will begin to close.

      "content": "1|# Curse of Slaad
2|
3|*A Tier 1 [[Free League of Stickyickistan]] adventure for four to five 3rd-level characters*
4|
5|## Being a Supposedly Competent Group of Warriors and Explorers
6|
7|The adventure begins at the [[FLS Guildhall]] on [[Nevercough Island]], where a public contract has been posted for a planar investigation. The job is backed by [[N.E.R.D]], whose planar-studies faculty wants the party to investigate a failed research outpost beyond the city. The Free League considers the assignment a monster hunt; N.E.R.D considers it a field study; everyone else considers it an opportunity to avoid filling out the correct paperwork.
8|
9|The party has been hired by a Githzerai wizard named Zardan, a visiting planar-studies researcher associated with [[N.E.R.D]], to investigate what he fears to be a hostile incursion by monsters from Limbo into [[Stickyickistan]]. His brother, Drarth, is a monk stationed in one of the Githzerai's outposts in [[The Outback]], near the unstable magical wetlands of [[Zooka Mire]]. The outpost monitors planar disturbances and repels threats from Limbo. Drarth and his comrades have been unreachable lately, even through magical means, and Zardan fears the worst might have happened.
10|
11|**Beings of Order.** Ever since their emancipation from the terrible mind flayers millennia ago, the Gith have battled against the illithids and all manner of aberrations from alternate dimensions. The Githzerai chose a path of strict mental discipline to achieve their goals and primarily built their fortresses in the chaos of Limbo. Their psionic abilities and mental fortitude allow them to thrive in this malleable environment, from which they departed in their quest to explore new realities and hunt down alien monsters. N.E.R.D's scholars believe the Githzerai outpost was established near Zooka Mire because Mount Zooka's [[Arcanite]] deposits distort the Weave and make the region a useful early-warning station for planar breaches.
12|
13|### Zardan, the Githzerai Wizard
14|
15|Zardan is a 3rd-level wizard of the divination school of magic. You can roleplay him however you want and take actions for him in combat. He is brilliant, underfunded, and deeply uncomfortable with the way N.E.R.D students describe his work as "applied catastrophe."
16|
17|Zardan doesn't possess the mental fortitude of his brethren and can't withstand the chaotic energy of Limbo, which is why he settled in the Material Plane. His superior memorization skills and natural learning abilities allowed him to quickly become a competent wizard. His research at N.E.R.D focuses on planar boundaries, aberration incursions, and methods of safely extracting useful information from dangerous creatures.
18|
19|Given his Portent class feature, roll two d20s at the start of the adventure and record the numbers rolled. Each of these numbers can be used once during the one-shot to replace a roll made by Zardan or a creature he can see, but you must choose to do this before the roll is made.
20|
21|## Stickyickistan Connections
22|
23|- **The FLS Guildhall:** The party accepts the contract here and can return here to file the report, collect payment, and record the adventure's consequences.
24|- **N.E.R.D:** The institution supplied Zardan's research grant, the planar hourglass, and the original survey maps. Its faculty wants the party to bring back notes, samples, and a clear explanation of why the outpost failed.
25|- **Zooka Mire:** The Githzerai outpost is hidden among the Mire's unstable wetlands. Arcanite runoff from [[Mount Zooka]] has made the local Weave unusually thin, allowing Limbo's influence to leak through.
26|- **The Ashen Shadow Society:** The Society holds the recovery contract for the missing researchers and equipment. If the party fails, a Bloodhound or Raven squad may be sent after them; if the party succeeds, the Society may claim the recovered artifacts as contracted property.
27|- **The Loot Tavern:** If the party needs an emergency escape route, [[Port Ale]] can return them to the extraplanar tavern. Lutecia can also prepare a teleportation flight back to [[Nevercough Island]], but the party must supply the drink and pay the usual fee.
28|
29|Zardan's research is useful to several groups for different reasons. N.E.R.D wants knowledge, the Free League wants its adventurers alive, and the Ashen Shadow Society wants anything valuable enough to sell. The party decides who receives the truth.
30|
31|## A Brother's Fate
32|
33|You may read from the following text box to describe the Githzerai citadel's first floor to the party:
34|
35|> [!Read Aloud]
36|> You enter a room that seems to serve multiple purposes: racks of basic survival equipment and weapons line one wall, cooking utensils and chests of non-perishable foods occupy a corner, shelves of maps and leather-bound tomes surround meditation mats, and a long table stands in the center. A Githzerai sits alone at this table, his back to you.
37|
38|**Githzerai Corpse.** If players choose to approach or investigate the figure, they notice that the body is withered and smells of decay. Deep slashes are gouged in its neck, and a massive hole gapes where its belly should be. A trail of dry blood and intestines sprawls on the table in front of it. A DC 12 Investigation, Perception, or Medicine check reveals that the stomach seems to have burst outward, as if something was violently ejected from it. Struggling to contain his grief, Zardan recognizes this corpse as his brother and, given the evidence, believes that a red slaad killed him.
39|
40|### Slaadi, the Terrors from Limbo
41|
42|If players don't know what slaadi are, you can have Zardan explain the following.
43|
44|Slaadi are large, malevolent, toad-like aberrations that spawned from the chaos of Limbo eons ago. They are extremely dangerous and follow their only instinct, which is to destroy inferior life forms. The Githzerai are committed to eliminating threats posed by these vile abominations, but rarely succeed without significant losses.
45|
46|The two types of slaadi reproduce parasitically in an unnatural cycle: a red slaad plants eggs in a living humanoid, which hatch into a blue slaad; conversely, a blue slaad infects a humanoid with a disease called "chaos phage" that transforms the afflicted creature into a red slaad.
47|
48|Additional slaad lore can be found in MM274.
49|
50|## Slaad Encounter
51|
52|A staircase leads from the citadel's ground-level floor of operations to the second-story habitation. In this room are five simple beds with chests containing the monks' personal belongings (robes, writing supplies, small wooden humanoid effigies, personal trinkets; nothing of value).
53|
54|The four other monks stationed in this outpost are piled in the center of the room. Their bodies are riddled with claw marks, but perceptive characters note that their pallid faces, sweat-covered brows, contorted expressions, and ragged breaths suggest that they are alive, but in excruciating pain. Even more perceptive characters notice that their stomachs are obscenely swollen.
55|
56|If a character approaches or tries to investigate, one of the monks feebly lifts his head and implores the party to put an end to their agony, when all of a sudden, the Githzerai's stomachs burst in unison. Four squalling slaadi tadpoles (MM 276) wriggle onto the floor and attack the party.
57|
58|The party should easily finish this combat in 2 rounds; it is meant to provide them a false sense of confidence before encountering a real slaad threat. Zardan laments that all the Githzerai were infected, but is troubled that they haven't actually found the red slaad itself. As a side note, he wonders aloud what might have happened to the tadpole that spawned from his brother...
59|
60|### A Blue Slaad Enraged
61|
62|As the wizard finishes his thought, a blue slaad (MM 276) crashes down from a shadowy alcove of the high ceiling and cries out in rage at the sight of its slaughtered baby brothers. Its monstrous croaking is psychically translated in the party's brains as a vengeful vow that announces their doom.
63|
64|Blue Slaad Combat. The blue slaad fights to the death and specifically targets the characters that killed a tadpole with its claws. Through violent psychic outbursts that accompany its attacks, the party learns that it slaughtered and ate the red slaad that spawned it, with the intent to freely terrorize the Material Plane with its brothers when they hatched. In order to make the fight manageable for a small group, you can choose to remove the slaad's Regeneration trait, reasoning that the slaad can't heal itself outside of Limbo's chaos.
65|
66|Take note of which characters fail the blue slaad's Claw attack saving throw, as these characters are now afflicted with chaos phage.
67|
68|### Grave Aftermath
69|
70|After defeating the blue slaad, Zardan is pale. He explains that anyone slashed by a blue slaad's claws has only a few days to live before the chaos phage that infected them turns them into a red slaad. Save for the *wish* spell, there is no way to stop this disease.
71|
72|## Chapter 2: Limbo Monastery
73|
74|The Arcanite beneath [[Mount Zooka]] has not created a new portal so much as loosened an old seam in reality. The Githzerai outpost near [[Zooka Mire]] was built over that seam, allowing the party to reach Limbo without leaving [[Mythmos]] entirely behind. From the Material Plane, the breach appears as a violet shimmer over the wetlands; from Limbo, it looks like a distant purple bruise in the chaos.
75|
76|Zahur al-Nasira's domain also exists within Limbo. His palace may be visible in the distance during the party's journey: a glittering landmark that remains stable only because Zahur wills it to remain so. Zahur does not need to appear in the adventure, but his presence gives the plane a familiar Stickyickistanian landmark and an optional explanation for why the party's arrival is noticed by powerful extraplanar eyes.
77|
78|**You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel when they first arrive in the plane of chaos:**
79|
80|> [!Read Aloud]
81|> You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of chaos. Far away, a palace of marble, gold, and lapis lazuli hangs above the flux like a stage set that someone forgot to anchor.
82|
83|> [!Read Aloud]
84|> You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound 
85|> 
86|> by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of chaos.
87|
88|### THE EVER-CHANGING CHAOS OF LIMBO
89|
90|Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a DC14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table (DMG260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be dispelled with the calm emotions, lesser restoration, or remove curse spells, and it ends if the character takes a short rest. 
91|
92|The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share with your players. 
93|
94|>The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG62), while the Chaos Control features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind (DMG61-62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's roleplay or gameplay load.
95|

97|>
98|>Creatures in Limbo gain the following action options. 
99|>
100|>**Telekinesis**. You can spend an action to mentally move an object you can see that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you move the object 5 feet plus 1 foot for every point by which you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below. ",

310|## Chapter 3: Slaad Assault
311|
312|Use the following text box to set the tone for the final battle:
313|
314|> [!Read Aloud]
315|> Safe in the belly of the steel apparatus, you have been roaming for what feels like too long in the chaotic void of Limbo, searching for a death slaad amidst the flux. Those of you afflicted by chaos phage can see your symptoms worsening; you feel in the pit of your stomach that very little time remains. The Zerthimon Steelbeast's sensors lead you further and further into the primordial soup until, finally, an earthy cliff fragment melts into bubbles, revealing a grey-skinned, necrotic toad. The Steelbeast's alarms blare and it rushes forward to meet this deadly foe, intent on subduing it. The battle of your lives begins now.
316|
317|The death slaad's den is not merely a random pocket of Limbo. The Steelbeast's sensors have followed an Arcanite resonance from [[Zooka Mire]] back through the breach, and the slaad has nested around a shattered Githzerai survey platform. Chunks of red-black stone drift through the den like broken pieces of [[Mount Zooka]], while violet lightning crawls over the wreckage. If the party destroys or secures the control gem, the resonance will collapse and the breach over Zooka Mire will begin to close.
318|

320|
321|You can use the tables in appendix B to generate a random battlefield of  
322|chaos for the showdown against the death slaad. Death slaadi are at home  
323|in the most chaotic environments of Limbo, so don't hold back on the  
324|initial generation and the terrain's subsequent randomization. 
325|
326|Treat the Zerthimon Steelbeast as untouchable by Limbo's chaotic shifts  
327|as with the Permanence feature of Chaos Control, in case matter randomly  
328|spawns in its area. New matter can instead appear around it. 
329|
330|> **Attacking as the Death Slaad**
331|> 
332|> The death slaad (MM278) relishes this challenge and attacks the  
333|> Steelbeast mercilessly with its claws, bite, and 
334|> 
335|> greatsword. It stays close to attack while still trying evade the  
336|> Steelbeast's pincers. After a few rounds or after the party performs an  
337|> action that would reveal their existence, the slaad shifts its murderous  
338|> focus to the characters. 
339|> 
340|> For example, it can telepathically threaten or taunt them, cast fear on  
341|> the group, or cast cloudkill inside the Steelbeast. 
342|> 
343|> The slaad fights to the death and prioritizes freeing itself if it is  
344|> restrained, unless it sadistically perceives a way to cause pain and  
345|> death while grappled. 
346|
347|### Obtaining the Control Gem
348|
349|The Steelbeast can use its Shock Stinger or Sleep Gas actions on the  
350|death slaad to incapacitate it for a few minutes (grappling it with  
351|Pincer Grab beforehand can help). The party then has that amount of time  
352|to attempt to extract the slaad's control gem using the method of their  
353|choice. 
354|
355|If the party wants to use the spell scroll of imprisonment but there are  
356|no wizards nor warlocks among them, they can summon Zardan using the  
357|planar recall bead he gave them earlier. The wizard needs to spend one  
358|minute after materializing to acclimate to Limbo's wracking chaos before  
359|he can take actions. If Zardan succeeds on a DC19 Intelligence saving  
360|throw, he can proceed to cast the spell. Otherwise, the scroll  
361|disintegrates. 
362|
363|> Keep in mind that Zardan can use the two rolls from his Portent class feature during this encounter, if he hasn't used them already.

367|Wisdom saving throw (with advantage, as per its Magic Resistance trait).

369|it fails, the death slaad's eyes gloss over and its entire body relaxes.  
370|The scroll disintegrates and is replaced by a cloudy grey asymmetrical  
371|gemstone in the palm of the scroll user's hand.

374|
375|If the party successfully defeats the death slaad and obtains its

## Chapter 1: Compromised Citadel

## A Brother's Fate

## Chapter 2: Limbo Monastery

The Arcanite beneath [[Mount Zooka]] has not created a new portal so much as loosened an old seam in reality. The Githzerai outpost near [[Zooka Mire]] was built over that seam, allowing the party to reach Limbo without leaving [[Mythmos]] entirely behind. From the Material Plane, the breach appears as a violet shimmer over the wetlands; from Limbo, it looks like a distant purple bruise in the chaos.

Zahur al-Nasira's domain also exists within Limbo. His palace may be visible in the distance during the party's journey: a glittering landmark that remains stable only because Zahur wills it to remain so. Zahur does not need to appear in the adventure, but his presence gives the plane a familiar Stickyickistanian landmark and an optional explanation for why the party's arrival is noticed by powerful extraplanar eyes.

**You may use the following text box to describe what the characters feel when they first arrive in the plane of chaos:**

> [!Read Aloud]
> You feel your body violently jerk as you materialize in the interminable flux of Limbo. Physics and matter aren't bound by the constraints of the Material Plane here: in the absence of gravity, you can float wherever you want at your normal speed by simply thinking about where you want to go; across the sea of churning energy and shifting substances, parcels of recognizable terrain, such as a tree on a grassy mound, a wooden hut on dirt foundations, and even a stone watchtower, drift, crash, and morph in a constant boil of chaos. Far away, a palace of marble, gold, and lapis lazuli hangs above the flux like a stage set that someone forgot to anchor.

### The Ever-Changing Chaos of Limbo

Limbo's chaos holds great potential for creation, but its instability threatens to render the weak-willed mad. Adventurers that first come into contact with this plane's overwhelming flux of energy must make a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, they suffer a random indefinite madness, as described in the Indefinite Madness table (DMG 260). This flaw must be roleplayed until cured. The madness can be dispelled with the *calm emotions*, *lesser restoration*, or *remove curse* spells, and it ends if the character takes a short rest.

The planar travelers are suffused with chaos and feel that the turmoil is theirs to shape, if they can sufficiently exert their willpower over it. For the duration of their stay in Limbo, they gain the temporary features described in the Chaos Control sidebar, which you can share with your players.

> The indefinite madness feature for Limbo was added by myself, based on Pandemonium's optional rule Mad Winds (DMG 62), while the Chaos Control features are derived from Limbo's optional rule Power of the Mind (DMG 61–62). You can choose to ignore these rules to lessen your group's roleplay or gameplay load.

### Chaos Control

Creatures in Limbo gain the following action options.

**Telekinesis.** You can spend an action to mentally move an object you can see that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you move the object 5 feet plus 1 foot for every point by which you beat the DC, which is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below.

**Transmutation.** You can spend an action to alter a nonmagical object you can see that isn't being worn or carried and that is within 30 feet of you. Make a Wisdom check. On a successful roll, you change the object into another nonliving form of the same size (for example, a boulder into a ball of fire). The number to beat is indicated in the DC by Object Size table below.

**Permanence.** You can spend an action to stabilize a spherical area centered around yourself. Make a Wisdom check. The DC is 5 for a 10-foot radius sphere, and increases by 5 for every 10 feet you add to the radius. On a successful roll, the area can't be altered by the plane for 24 hours, or until you use this ability again.

### DC by Object Size

| Object Size | Telekinesis DC | Transmutation DC |
|---|---:|---:|
| Tiny | 5 | 10 |
| Small | 10 | 15 |
| Medium | 15 | 20 |
| Large | 20 | 25 |
| Huge or larger | 25 | 25 |
